article_content:
ByteDance raised the ceiling on AI video generation Tuesday when it announced Seedance 2.5 at the Volcano Engine FORCE conference in Beijing — a model that, the company claims, can generate a single continuous 30-second clip without stitching shorter segments together. If those claims survive independent testing when the model launches in early July, Seedance 2.5 will mark the first major closed commercial AI video tool to reach that duration natively, without segment breaks.

The announcement arrives four months after ByteDance voluntarily paused the global rollout of its predecessor, Seedance 2.0, following cease-and-desist letters from every major Hollywood studio over alleged copyright infringement. Those legal disputes remain unresolved. The central question hanging over the June 23 event is whether Seedance 2.5 carries the same legal exposure — or whether the intervening months of remediation work have changed the equation for enterprise buyers.

Until now, professional AI video generators from Runway Gen-4.5, Google Veo 3.1, and OpenAI's Sora 2 — which was shut down on April 26, 2026 — topped out at roughly 8 to 15 seconds per native clip. Generating longer sequences required stitching shorter clips end-to-end, a process that introduces visible seams between segments, character faces that drift in appearance between shots, and lighting inconsistencies that mark the footage as artificial. Television commercials, social media ads, explainer videos, and short documentary segments all cluster in the 15–60 second range. A tool that can hold visual and audio consistency across an entire half-minute without a stitch changes the production economics for that entire format category.

ByteDance describes the architecture behind that consistency as a unified joint audio-video generation system, in which visual and audio signals are co-processed inside the same latent space rather than generated separately and synchronized after the fact. Combined with what the company calls optimized spatial-temporal attention mechanisms, the model holds character appearance, lighting, and motion style across the full clip duration. ByteDance announced Seedance 2.5 on stage, not as a shipped product — it is currently in global enterprise beta, with a public launch targeted for early July 2026. No pricing has been disclosed. All claimed capabilities are ByteDance's own statements; no independent benchmarks exist yet for Seedance 2.5.

Seedance 2.5 ships with three generation modes. Text-to-video produces a clip from a written prompt alone. Image-to-video animates a still image into a moving scene. A motion-reference mode uses an existing video clip to guide the movement style of a new generation — useful for advertisers or filmmakers who want to replicate a specific camera technique or action choreography without sourcing live footage.

The model's reference input capacity is a more significant upgrade than the generation modes alone suggest. Seedance 2.5 accepts up to 50 simultaneous multimodal reference materials — images, video clips, and audio files — compared to roughly 12 in Seedance 2.0. Volcano Engine president Tan Dai told the conference that this capacity is designed for brand-consistency and episodic storytelling workflows, where the model must lock a character's face, a product's appearance, an art style, and a music reference across an entire generation without drifting. Google's Veo 3.1, the closest Western competitor for reference control, accepts only three reference inputs — making the gap between the two substantial for production use cases that require strict consistency.

The system also introduces localized region editing: a creator can redraw one specific element in a frame — swap a character's clothing, change a background element, alter a product in a scene — without regenerating the entire clip. That capability addresses one of the most costly friction points in AI video production, where fixing one small error currently requires starting over and hoping the rest of the output survives intact.

How the Architecture Differs From Seedance 2.0

The distinction between Seedance 2.0 and 2.5 is not simply longer output — it is a change in how longer output is produced. Seedance 2.0 could produce clips of up to 15 seconds natively, and could reach 30 seconds only through sequential stitching, which meant extended output was a composite of shorter generated segments joined at their boundaries. Seedance 2.5, according to ByteDance, generates the entire 30-second clip as a single coherent diffusion pass. The spatial-temporal attention mechanisms that enable this hold object identity and scene state across a longer temporal horizon than previous diffusion window approaches could sustain.

ByteDance's predecessor had already established an independent quality benchmark before this announcement. On the Artificial Analysis Video Arena — a blind human-preference leaderboard that assigns scores through paired comparisons — Seedance 2.0 currently ranks first for text-to-video with audio, with an Elo score of 1,218, ahead of Kling 3.0 and Google Veo 3.1. That ranking reflects the shipping version of Seedance 2.0. No Seedance 2.5 score exists yet; benchmark numbers will not be reliable until the model is publicly available and independently tested.

ByteDance also announced at the same event that Seedance 2.0 has been upgraded to support native 4K output with 10-bit color depth — a separate improvement that benefits development teams already integrated with the current model. The company said its enterprise Seedance platform has reached $2 billion in annual recurring revenue, a figure that signals commercial traction ahead of the 2.5 launch.

Seedance 2.5 will be distributed through ByteDance's Volcano Engine cloud platform, with additional reach through CapCut — the video editing application with more than 400 million monthly active users — as well as the Dreamina and Doubao consumer interfaces.

Before committing to a Seedance 2.5 integration, development teams should weigh several operational factors that the conference announcement left unresolved.

No independent benchmark exists yet. All described capabilities — 30-second single-pass generation, 50-reference input handling, regional editing stability — are ByteDance's stated specifications from the June 23 keynote. They are consistent across multiple reporters covering the event and are plausible given the architecture, but they have not been verified by third-party testing. Early July access will provide the first real opportunity for external evaluation.

Copyright filters are active. Following the Motion Picture Association's formal cease-and-desist action against Seedance 2.0 in February 2026, ByteDance added content filters that block generation of recognizable real faces and copyrighted characters. Those filters remain active in the current model and are expected to carry forward into 2.5.

Pricing is undisclosed. Seedance 2.0 was priced at roughly $2.50 per 15-second clip on some third-party inference platforms. Seedance 2.5's cost structure has not been announced and may change the cost-per-second economics of longer clips.

The Unresolved Copyright Situation From Seedance 2.0

The context a developer evaluating Seedance 2.5 cannot ignore is the legal record of its predecessor. When Seedance 2.0 launched in China in February 2026, the Motion Picture Association described the tool's copyright infringement as "a feature, not a bug" in a formal cease-and-desist letter — the first such letter the MPA had ever sent to a major generative AI company. Disney, Warner Bros. Discovery, Paramount, Netflix, Sony Pictures, and Universal all sent their own cease-and-desist letters within days of the launch. SAG-AFTRA condemned the model's ability to produce realistic actor likenesses without consent.

ByteDance pledged to strengthen safeguards and voluntarily paused the global rollout in March 2026. As of May 2026, no federal lawsuit had been filed in the United States and no government had formally banned the model in any country — though US Senators Marsha Blackburn and Peter Welch had written to ByteDance's CEO demanding the model be shut down. The enforcement challenge is partly structural: serving legal process on a China-based company under the Hague Convention takes an estimated 18 to 24 months, a timeline that has given Chinese AI video companies a significant advantage over Hollywood's legal timeline.

ByteDance previewed a new AI copyright commercialization platform at the same FORCE conference, with filmmaker Stephen Chow named as an initial partner. Whether that platform meaningfully addresses the concerns raised by the studios — or whether the same generation capabilities that triggered Seedance 2.0's controversy carry forward into Seedance 2.5 — will only be assessed once independent testers gain public access in July.

ByteDance is headquartered in Beijing. China's National Intelligence Law, passed in June 2017, requires under Article 7 that "all organizations and citizens shall support, assist, and cooperate with national intelligence efforts in accordance with law." That requirement applies to ByteDance and its subsidiaries. China's Cybersecurity Law (2017) additionally requires businesses operating in China to store data on servers within China and permits Chinese authorities to conduct spot inspections of network operations.

The Chinese government holds a 1% "golden share" with a board seat in ByteDance's main Chinese subsidiary, Beijing ByteDance Technology, with a government official whose background is in propaganda appointed to that seat. ByteDance has maintained an internal Chinese Communist Party committee since 2014. The company has a strategic partnership with China's Ministry of Public Security. The US Department of Homeland Security has assessed that Chinese companies are "required to secretly share data with the PRC government or other entities upon request, even if that request is illegal under the jurisdiction in which these firms operate."

ByteDance has denied sharing user data with the Chinese government and states that its data practices comply with US law. Legal scholars have noted that the scope of Article 7's compulsion is contested: an analysis by China Law Translate argues the law may not require active participation in intelligence gathering beyond standard law enforcement cooperation requirements. Neither ByteDance's denial nor the scholarly debate changes the structural legal condition: a Chinese government request to ByteDance for enterprise API usage data, inference logs, or developer-submitted content would be made under a legal framework that does not require disclosure to the affected party.

Enterprise teams integrating Seedance 2.5 into their production pipelines should assess what data they plan to submit to the model — including reference content, brand assets, scripts, and proprietary visual material — against this legal condition before committing to the integration.

What the Seedance 2.5 Launch Does and Does Not Change

For the AI video production market, the 30-second native generation milestone matters even with a qualification attached. The realistic ceiling among major commercial models before this announcement was 8 to 15 seconds per native clip. Seedance 2.5's stated capability, if confirmed by independent testing, at minimum doubles that ceiling among closed commercial tools and removes the stitching step that has been the primary technical barrier to professional-grade long-form AI video.

The model that arrives in July will enter a market where its predecessor already holds the top rank on the leading independent benchmark, where the copyright compliance architecture is still being tested, and where the geopolitical context of its maker's home jurisdiction is a material enterprise decision — not a footnote. Developers who evaluate Seedance 2.5 on technical capability alone will have an incomplete picture. Those who factor in the copyright framework, the data jurisdiction conditions, and the still-pending independent verification of the 30-second claim will be better positioned to make the integration decision that matches their actual risk tolerance.

When can developers actually use Seedance 2.5?

As of the June 23, 2026 announcement, Seedance 2.5 is in global enterprise beta with limited access for qualifying organizations. ByteDance's stated target for public launch is early July 2026. A precise date has not been confirmed. Third-party platforms that have integrated Seedance 2.0 have indicated they will add 2.5 access once the official Volcano Engine API opens. Pricing has not been disclosed.

Does Seedance 2.5 resolve the copyright problems that shut down Seedance 2.0's global launch?

ByteDance has not made specific claims that Seedance 2.5's safeguards address all of the concerns raised by the Motion Picture Association and the major Hollywood studios in February and March 2026. The legal disputes from Seedance 2.0 — including the MPA's formal cease-and-desist characterizing infringement as "a feature, not a bug" — have not been resolved in court. ByteDance did announce a new AI copyright commercialization platform at the same event, but the relationship between that platform's licensing mechanisms and Seedance 2.5's generation safeguards has not been publicly documented. Independent testers who gain early July access will be in the first position to evaluate whether the generation capabilities that produced unauthorized character likenesses in Seedance 2.0 persist in 2.5.

What is technically different about native 30-second generation versus stitched-together clips?

Stitched generation assembles shorter clips — typically 5 to 15 seconds — end-to-end in post-processing. The boundaries between segments produce visible shifts in character appearance, lighting, and motion style, because each segment was generated independently with only limited conditioning from the previous one. Seedance 2.5's claimed approach processes the entire 30-second output as a single coherent diffusion pass, using spatial-temporal attention mechanisms to maintain scene state — character identity, lighting conditions, camera position — from the first frame to the last without segment breaks. Whether that claim holds under independent testing with complex prompts, multiple characters, and varied motion is unknown until public access opens.

Should enterprise teams using Seedance 2.5 be concerned about where their content goes?

ByteDance is headquartered in China and subject to China's National Intelligence Law (2017), which requires organizations to cooperate with national intelligence requests. Enterprise teams that submit proprietary brand assets, scripts, reference videos, or other confidential materials through the Seedance API are submitting that content to infrastructure operated by a company under that legal jurisdiction. ByteDance has stated it does not share user data with the Chinese government and maintains data practices compliant with US law. The structural legal condition — that a government request under Chinese law would not require notification to the data owner — does not change based on that denial. Enterprise security teams should evaluate this as a data governance question before integrating Seedance 2.5 into workflows that handle sensitive client or proprietary material.

title_en:
BANKS SELL AI DATA CENTER LOANS AS FINANCING RISKS MOUNT

Major banks are reducing exposure to AI data center financing amid concerns over construction delays, according to Reuters Breakingviews columnist Jennifer Johnson.

ING reportedly offered $500 million in data center loans for sale, while HSBC sold $300 million in loans linked to the OpenAI-backed Stargate project at prices in the mid-80s percent of face value.

Société Générale has also sought buyers for $300 million in Oracle-related project debt.

The ECB estimates data centers represent just 1.2% of banks' corporate exposures, suggesting limited systemic risk.

However, increasingly selective lenders could drive up borrowing costs for the AI infrastructure boom.

full_text_en:
BANKS SELL AI DATA CENTER LOANS AS FINANCING RISKS MOUNT

Major banks are reducing exposure to AI data center financing amid concerns over construction delays, according to Reuters Breakingviews columnist Jennifer Johnson.

ING reportedly offered $500 million in data center loans for sale, while HSBC sold $300 million in loans linked to the OpenAI-backed Stargate project at prices in the mid-80s percent of face value.

Société Générale has also sought buyers for $300 million in Oracle-related project debt.

The ECB estimates data centers represent just 1.2% of banks' corporate exposures, suggesting limited systemic risk.

However, increasingly selective lenders could drive up borrowing costs for the AI infrastructure boom.
full_text_zh:
随着融资风险的增加，银行出售人工智能数据中心贷款

路透社 Breakingviews 专栏作家 Jennifer Johnson 表示，由于担心建设延误，各大银行正在减少对人工智能数据中心融资的投资。

据报道，ING 提供了 5 亿美元的数据中心贷款出售，而汇丰银行则以票面价值 80% 的价格出售了 3 亿美元的与 OpenAI 支持的 Stargate 项目相关的贷款。

法国兴业银行还为 Oracle 相关项目债务寻找 3 亿美元的买家。

欧洲央行估计数据中心仅占银行企业风险敞口的 1.2%，表明系统性风险有限。

然而，日益挑剔的贷款机构可能会推高人工智能基础设施繁荣的借贷成本。

title: How can we distill frontier models on agentic tasks without access to their CoT? In our latest paper, we introduce a method that uses the reasoning summaries returned by closed-model providers and matches standard full-CoT fine-tuning on long-horizon tasks
title_en:
How can we distill frontier models on agentic tasks without access to their CoT?

In our latest paper, we introduce a method that uses the reasoning summaries returned by closed-model providers and matches standard full-CoT fine-tuning on long-horizon tasks.

CoT-proxy training works by introducing a train-eval format mismatch: during training, we place the summary after an *empty* think block and before the action/tool call. During inference, this additional training signal transfers to the student's own reasoning, without forcing it to mimic the summary verbatim.

Distilling GPT-5.6 Luna into post-trained Qwen3-4B raises the student's performance from 2.7% to 27.8% on SWE-bench Verified.
title_zh:
我们如何在不访问其 CoT 的情况下提取代理任务的前沿模型？

在我们最新的论文中，我们介绍了一种方法，该方法使用封闭模型提供者返回的推理摘要，并匹配长视野任务上的标准全 CoT 微调。

CoT-代理训练通过引入训练-评估格式不匹配来工作
author: @dawkopi
summary_zh:
在训练期间，我们将摘要放在*空*思考块之后和操作/工具调用之前。在推理过程中，这种额外的训练信号会转移到学生自己的推理中，而不会强迫其逐字模仿摘要。

将 GPT-5.6 Luna 提炼成训练后的 Qwen3-4B 可以将学生在 SWE-bench Verified 上的表现从 2.7% 提高到 27.8%。
full_text_en:
How can we distill frontier models on agentic tasks without access to their CoT?

In our latest paper, we introduce a method that uses the reasoning summaries returned by closed-model providers and matches standard full-CoT fine-tuning on long-horizon tasks.

CoT-proxy training works by introducing a train-eval format mismatch: during training, we place the summary after an *empty* think block and before the action/tool call. During inference, this additional training signal transfers to the student's own reasoning, without forcing it to mimic the summary verbatim.

Distilling GPT-5.6 Luna into post-trained Qwen3-4B raises the student's performance from 2.7% to 27.8% on SWE-bench Verified.
full_text_zh:
我们如何在不访问其 CoT 的情况下提取代理任务的前沿模型？

在我们最新的论文中，我们介绍了一种方法，该方法使用封闭模型提供者返回的推理摘要，并匹配长视野任务上的标准全 CoT 微调。

CoT-代理训练通过引入训练-评估格式不匹配来工作：在训练期间，我们将摘要放在*空*思考块之后和操作/工具调用之前。在推理过程中，这种额外的训练信号会转移到学生自己的推理中，而不会强迫其逐字模仿摘要。

将 GPT-5.6 Luna 提炼成训练后的 Qwen3-4B 可以将学生在 SWE-bench Verified 上的表现从 2.7% 提高到 27.8%。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 针对闭源前沿模型（Frontier Models）在思维链（CoT）不可见的情况，研究者提出了一种全新的蒸馏机制。该方法通过摄取闭源模型返回的推理摘要（Reasoning Summaries）进行知识迁移，在处理长程代理任务（Agentic Tasks）时，其效果已达到与全量思维链微调相当的基准水平。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Researchers have introduced a novel distillation mechanism for frontier models where CoT access is restricted. By leveraging reasoning summaries returned by closed-model providers, this method matches the performance of standard full-CoT fine-tuning on complex long-horizon agentic tasks.

elements_zh.what: 提出利用推理摘要蒸馏闭源模型思维链的方法

elements_en.where: AI model reasoning and distillation research field
elements_en.what: New method for distilling frontier models via reasoning summaries
elements_en.why: To address the challenge of limited CoT access for deploying high-performance agentic models

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 该研究直接切中了大模型部署的合规与成本痛点，通过摘要蒸馏绕过了模型权重隐私限制，为闭源闭环生态下的高性能轻量化模型构建提供了关键路径。这一技术路线验证了推理链信息在低维空间内的压缩潜力，将显著降低企业在垂类应用中对超大规模模型推理API的依赖。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This research addresses critical compliance and cost constraints in LLM deployment by bypassing proprietary weight restrictions via summary distillation. It validates the high-fidelity information density of reasoning chains in compressed spaces, fundamentally lowering enterprise reliance on hyperscale model inference APIs for vertical applications.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 针对闭源前沿模型在思维链不可见的情况，研究者提出了一种利用推理摘要进行蒸馏的创新路径。该技术有效替代了传统的全量思维链微调，在复杂长程任务中展现出极高的性能匹配度。
ai_analysis.digest_en: A new distillation path utilizing reasoning summaries has been proposed to address limited CoT access in closed-source frontier models. The method effectively replaces traditional full-CoT fine-tuning, achieving matching performance metrics in complex long-horizon tasks.

title: Google will start forcing AI agents to use MCP (instead of APIs) for Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Docs, etc.) starting Feb 1, 2027. AI agents will no longer be allowed to call the normal Workspace REST APIs freely starting Feb 1, 2027. Instead, they must
title_en:
Google will start forcing AI agents to use MCP (instead of APIs) for Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Docs, etc.) starting Feb 1, 2027. 

AI agents will no longer be allowed to call the normal Workspace REST APIs freely starting Feb 1, 2027. Instead, they must use Google’s official Workspace MCP servers (or the Workspace CLI).

Regular (non-AI) applications can continue using the existing REST APIs as usual.

According to Google, they are doing this to improve security, visibility, and control. MCP gives Google (and admins) better policy checks, human in the loop confirmations for sensitive actions, and clearer audit trails when autonomous agents interact with Workspace data.

The commercial reason (which Google won't admit) is that they can charge extra for higher usage (higher usage will move to a paid “Scaled” tier starting April 1, 2027.).

AI agents that call Workspace REST APIs directly will be limited to Standard tier quotas, no matter which tier the project is on. To get higher quotas for agent use, you must switch to MCP and enrol in the Scaled tier.

It is important to note that they are not fully blocked. But they get throttled to the low free-tier rate limits. Google has not published exact numbers for those Standard limits yet, but they are expected to be too low for most real agent workloads.

The Workspace AI Tools Addendum (effective the same day) requires AI agents to use MCP (or the CLI). It also says you may not obfuscate or circumvent that requirement.

Google’s standard language in these announcements is: "Failure to comply with the updated terms may result in a breach of your service agreement."

If Google determines you are running agents in a way that violates the Addendum (including continuing to use direct REST APIs for agentic access after the deadline), they can treat it as a terms violation. That can lead to further restrictions, suspension of API access, or other account-level actions, beyond just the automatic rate limiting.

What this means in practice is that:

>> Your AI Agents will generally have a lot more restricted capabilities than they do with direct API access. You only get the tools and actions Google exposes on its MCP servers, not every REST endpoint.

>> You have less control over your agents. Google decides what your agents can do, how data is returned, and when human confirmation is required.

>> You will pay more to Google to access Google Workspaces.

This move could encourage other enterprise vendors to move in a similar direction. They may also decide it’s easier and safer to steer agents through their own governed MCP servers rather than leave the full REST APIs wide open.

And let's be honest, in most cases, vendors can benefit more from selling (or metering) MCP access than from unrestricted direct API access, especially for AI agents. 

With direct REST APIs, it’s harder to distinguish “normal app” usage from high-volume, autonomous AI agent usage. MCP makes agent traffic more visible and controllable, so vendors can apply different (usually higher) pricing or stricter quotas.
title_zh: 谷歌将于2027年起强制AI代理使用MCP协议
author: @analyticsnerd
full_text_zh:
从 2027 年 2 月 1 日开始，Google 将开始强制 AI 代理在 Workspace（Gmail、Drive、日历、文档等）中使用 MCP（而不是 API）。

从 2027 年 2 月 1 日开始，AI 代理将不再被允许自由调用正常的 Workspace REST API。相反，他们必须使用 Google 的官方 Workspace MCP 服务器（或 Workspace CLI）。

常规（非 AI）应用程序可以照常继续使用现有的 REST API。

据谷歌称，他们这样做是为了提高安全性、可见性和控制力。 MCP 为 Google（和管理员）提供更好的策略检查、敏感操作的人机循环确认，以及自主代理与 Workspace 数据交互时更清晰的审计跟踪。

商业原因（谷歌不会承认）是他们可以对更高的使用量收取额外费用（从 2027 年 4 月 1 日开始，更高的使用量将转移到付费“扩展”层）。

无论项目位于哪一层，直接调用 Workspace REST API 的 AI 代理都将受到标准层配额的限制。要获得更高的代理使用配额，您必须切换到 MCP 并注册到 Scaled 层。

需要注意的是，它们并未完全被阻止。但他们受到了较低的免费套餐费率限制的限制。谷歌尚未公布这些标准限制的确切数字，但预计对于大多数实际代理工作负载来说，这些数字太低了。

Workspace AI 工具附录（当天生效）要求 AI 代理使用 MCP（或 CLI）。它还表示您不得混淆或规避该要求。

谷歌在这些公告中的标准语言是：“不遵守更新的条款可能会导致违反您的服务协议。”

如果 Google 确定您运行代理的方式违反了附录（包括在截止日期后继续使用直接 REST API 进行代理访问），他们可以将其视为违反条款。这可能会导致进一步的限制、暂停 API 访问或其他帐户级别的操作，而不仅仅是自动速率限制。

这在实践中意味着：

>> 与直接 API 访问相比，您的 AI 代理的功能通常会受到更多限制。您只能获得 Google 在其 MCP 服务器上公开的工具和操作，而不是每个 REST 端点。

>> 您对代理的控制权较少。 Google 决定您的代理可以做什么、如何返回数据以及何时需要人工确认。

>> 您需要向 Google 支付更多费用才能访问 Google Workspaces。

此举可能会鼓励其他企业供应商朝类似的方向发展。他们还可能认为通过自己管理的 MCP 服务器来引导代理更容易、更安全，而不是完全开放完整的 REST API。

老实说，在大多数情况下，与不受限制的直接 API 访问相比，供应商可以从销售（或计量）MCP 访问中获益更多，特别是对于 AI 代理而言。

使用直接 REST API，很难区分“正常应用程序”使用与大容量、自主 AI 代理的使用。 MCP 使代理流量更加可见和可控，因此供应商可以应用不同的（通常更高）定价或更严格的配额。

title: Google just silently dropped 6 groundbreaking math papers on github. all written by an AI agent, Cogentic on Gemini 4. factoring: first full proof that any number can be factored in the speed class of the number field sieve. the proven record was stuck since 199
title_en:
Google just silently dropped 6 groundbreaking math papers on github. all written by an AI agent, Cogentic on Gemini 4.

factoring: first full proof that any number can be factored in the speed class of the number field sieve. the proven record was stuck since 1992

deterministic factoring: first subexponential method with no randomness and no assumptions. everything before was still exponential

discrete log: faster than quasi-polynomial in small characteristic fields, which was the best anyone had proven

Nash equilibria: polynomial time approximation goes from 1/3 down to 1/5

log-rank conjecture: first result under the square root barrier on a conjecture from 1988

edge reconstruction: the 1964 conjecture is now settled for every graph with linear density, the old bound was from 1977

title: $META and $AMZN are in talks to let Muse shop directly on Amazon just two months after the retailer blocked the AI agent. With 25% of Muse users already shopping weekly I think Amazon sees an opportunity to bring its ~$78B ads business into agentic com
title_en:
$META and $AMZN are in talks to let Muse shop directly on Amazon just two months after the retailer blocked the AI agent.

With 25% of Muse users already shopping weekly I think Amazon sees an opportunity to bring its ~$78B ads business into agentic commerce by monetizing sponsored products inside Muse.

It’s similar to $GOOGL paying $AAPL for search distribution except Amazon would be getting paid to give Meta access to its store.
title_zh:
在零售商屏蔽人工智能代理两个月后，$META 和 $AMZN 正在商谈让 Muse 直接在亚马逊上购物。

25% 的 Muse 用户已经每周购物，我认为亚马逊看到了一个机会，通过在 Muse 内将赞助产品货币化，将其约 78B 美元的广告
author: @StockSavvyShay
summary_zh:
业务带入代理商务。

这类似于 $GOOGL 为搜索分发支付 $AAPL 费用，只不过亚马逊会因为允许 Meta 访问其商店而获得报酬。
full_text_en:
$META and $AMZN are in talks to let Muse shop directly on Amazon just two months after the retailer blocked the AI agent.

With 25% of Muse users already shopping weekly I think Amazon sees an opportunity to bring its ~$78B ads business into agentic commerce by monetizing sponsored products inside Muse.

It’s similar to $GOOGL paying $AAPL for search distribution except Amazon would be getting paid to give Meta access to its store.
full_text_zh:
在零售商屏蔽人工智能代理两个月后，$META 和 $AMZN 正在商谈让 Muse 直接在亚马逊上购物。

25% 的 Muse 用户已经每周购物，我认为亚马逊看到了一个机会，通过在 Muse 内将赞助产品货币化，将其约 78B 美元的广告业务带入代理商务。

这类似于 $GOOGL 为搜索分发支付 $AAPL 费用，只不过亚马逊会因为允许 Meta 访问其商店而获得报酬。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Meta与亚马逊正进行商业谈判，拟允许Meta旗下AI代理工具Muse直接连接亚马逊电商系统进行购物。此前亚马逊曾因数据隐私合规限制封锁Muse，但鉴于Muse已有25%的用户保持周频购物习惯，亚马逊正寻求通过接入该代理重振其规模达780亿美元的广告业务，将流量转化为代理驱动的商业行为。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Meta and Amazon are in discussions to enable Meta's AI agent, Muse, to facilitate direct shopping on Amazon's platform. Despite previous blocks due to data privacy concerns, the companies are negotiating a path forward as 25% of Muse users engage in weekly shopping; Amazon aims to integrate this into its $78 billion advertising engine by pivoting toward agentic commerce.

title: 🚨 A massive financial crisis could be brewing for Anthropic. Just days after its record breaking IPO, Wall Street is expecting Anthropic's bonds to receive a JUNK credit rating, according to WSJ. And this comes as its stock has already crashed below its $83 IPO
title_en:
🚨 A massive financial crisis could be brewing for Anthropic.

Just days after its record breaking IPO, Wall Street is expecting Anthropic's bonds to receive a JUNK credit rating, according to WSJ.

And this comes as its stock has already crashed below its $83 IPO price.

But the bigger problem is Anthropic's MASSIVE AI spending commitments.

Here's what's happening:

• Anthropic has committed to spending $900 BILLION on AI computing power over the coming years.

• The company generated $17 BILLION in revenue last quarter, yet it's still losing money due to its enormous computing costs.

• Anthropic has $96 BILLION in cash, but its future spending commitments are nearly 10 times that amount.

• Bond investors expect its debt to receive a BB rating, below investment grade, which could make borrowing significantly more expensive.

• The entire U.S. junk bond market is worth just $1.7 TRILLION, making it difficult to raise hundreds of billions through traditional high-yield bonds.

And the implications go far beyond Anthropic.

NVIDIA and Broadcom have already guaranteed tens of billions in loans tied to AI chip purchases, while lenders are becoming increasingly concerned about the industry's massive borrowing needs.

Even established tech giants are struggling to attract bond investors, with some AI-related bonds already suffering significant losses.

Anthropic has raised enormous amounts of cash, but roughly HALF of its spending commitments stretch from 2031 all the way to 2045.

That means the company will need access to affordable financing for YEARS.

If its debt receives a junk rating, borrowing could become much more expensive, putting pressure on its AI expansion plans.

And if a company worth over $1 TRILLION struggles to finance its AI spending, the damage could spread to chipmakers, data centers and the entire AI industry.
title_zh:
🚨 Anthropic 可能正在酝酿一场大规模的金融危机。

据《华尔街日报》报道，在破纪录的 IPO 几天后，华尔街预计 Anthropic 的债券将获得垃圾级信用评级。

与此同时，其股价已跌破 83 美元的 IPO 价格。

但更大的
author: @BullTheoryio
summary_zh:
问题是 Anthropic 的大规模人工智能支出承诺。

这是发生的事情：

• Anthropic 承诺未来几年在人工智能计算能力上投入 9000 亿美元。

• 该公司上季度收入达 170 亿美元，但由于计算成本巨大，仍处于亏损状态。

• Anthropic 拥有 960 亿美元现金，但其未来支出承诺几乎是该金额的 10 倍。

• 债券投资者预计其债务将获得低于投资级别的BB 评级，这可能会导致借贷成本大幅上涨。

• 整个美国垃圾债券市场价值仅为1.7万亿美元，因此很难通过传统的高收益债券筹集数千亿美元。

其影响远远超出了人择范畴。

英伟达和博通已经为与人工智能芯片采购相关的数百亿美元贷款提供了担保，而贷款机构也越来越担心该行业庞大的借贷需求。

即使是老牌科技巨头也难以吸引债券投资者，一些与人工智能相关的债券已经遭受了重大损失。

Anthropic 已筹集了大量现金，但其支出承诺的大约一半从 2031 年一直持续到 2045 年。

这意味着该公司将需要多年获得负担得起的融资。

如果其债务获得垃圾级评级，借款可能会变得更加昂贵，从而给其人工智能扩张计划带来压力。

如果一家价值超过 1 万亿美元的公司难以为其人工智能支出融资，损害可能会波及芯片制造商、数据中心和整个人工智能行业。

full_text_en:
🚨 A massive financial crisis could be brewing for Anthropic.

Just days after its record breaking IPO, Wall Street is expecting Anthropic's bonds to receive a JUNK credit rating, according to WSJ.

And this comes as its stock has already crashed below its $83 IPO price.

But the bigger problem is Anthropic's MASSIVE AI spending commitments.

Here's what's happening:

• Anthropic has committed to spending $900 BILLION on AI computing power over the coming years.

• The company generated $17 BILLION in revenue last quarter, yet it's still losing money due to its enormous computing costs.

• Anthropic has $96 BILLION in cash, but its future spending commitments are nearly 10 times that amount.

• Bond investors expect its debt to receive a BB rating, below investment grade, which could make borrowing significantly more expensive.

• The entire U.S. junk bond market is worth just $1.7 TRILLION, making it difficult to raise hundreds of billions through traditional high-yield bonds.

And the implications go far beyond Anthropic.

NVIDIA and Broadcom have already guaranteed tens of billions in loans tied to AI chip purchases, while lenders are becoming increasingly concerned about the industry's massive borrowing needs.

Even established tech giants are struggling to attract bond investors, with some AI-related bonds already suffering significant losses.

Anthropic has raised enormous amounts of cash, but roughly HALF of its spending commitments stretch from 2031 all the way to 2045.

That means the company will need access to affordable financing for YEARS.

If its debt receives a junk rating, borrowing could become much more expensive, putting pressure on its AI expansion plans.

And if a company worth over $1 TRILLION struggles to finance its AI spending, the damage could spread to chipmakers, data centers and the entire AI industry.
full_text_zh:
🚨 Anthropic 可能正在酝酿一场大规模的金融危机。

据《华尔街日报》报道，在破纪录的 IPO 几天后，华尔街预计 Anthropic 的债券将获得垃圾级信用评级。

与此同时，其股价已跌破 83 美元的 IPO 价格。

但更大的问题是 Anthropic 的大规模人工智能支出承诺。

这是发生的事情：

• Anthropic 承诺未来几年在人工智能计算能力上投入 9000 亿美元。

• 该公司上季度收入达 170 亿美元，但由于计算成本巨大，仍处于亏损状态。

• Anthropic 拥有 960 亿美元现金，但其未来支出承诺几乎是该金额的 10 倍。

• 债券投资者预计其债务将获得低于投资级别的BB 评级，这可能会导致借贷成本大幅上涨。

• 整个美国垃圾债券市场价值仅为1.7万亿美元，因此很难通过传统的高收益债券筹集数千亿美元。

其影响远远超出了人择范畴。

英伟达和博通已经为与人工智能芯片采购相关的数百亿美元贷款提供了担保，而贷款机构也越来越担心该行业庞大的借贷需求。

即使是老牌科技巨头也难以吸引债券投资者，一些与人工智能相关的债券已经遭受了重大损失。

Anthropic 已筹集了大量现金，但其支出承诺的大约一半从 2031 年一直持续到 2045 年。

这意味着该公司将需要多年获得负担得起的融资。

如果其债务获得垃圾级评级，借款可能会变得更加昂贵，从而给其人工智能扩张计划带来压力。

如果一家价值超过 1 万亿美元的公司难以为其人工智能支出融资，损害可能会波及芯片制造商、数据中心和整个人工智能行业。

title: Benchmark grading is getting honest. Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 asks one question only: would a real open source maintainer actually merge this pull request. Every model that took the test scored lower than it did on the easier 1.1 version, including Cogniti
title_en:
Benchmark grading is getting honest. Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 asks one question only: would a real open source maintainer actually merge this pull request. Every model that took the test scored lower than it did on the easier 1.1 version, including Cognition's own.

SWE-2.1 lands at 41.3 on that harder scale, up from 24.1 for the previous version, and it was built by running reinforcement learning on top of Moonshot's Kimi K3 rather than pretraining a new base model from scratch. That beats Kimi K3.1 itself, the newer tuned version of its own base, which only scores 19.9. Claude Opus 5.5 still tops the board at 45.5%, but that is down from 54.6% on FrontierCode 1.1, so the harder grading hit the leader hardest.

Cost is where it gets interesting. GPT-6.1 Sol scores 39.0% at $1.03 per task. Opus 5.5 costs $12.82 per task for six and a half more points. Claude Sonnet 5.5 scores lower than Opus at 41.0% while costing more per task, $19.94. GPT-6 Astra sits at 42.8% for $6.68. The pattern holding across the leaderboard is that higher reasoning effort does not reliably buy a higher score, and sometimes buys a lower one. Price and capability have quietly come apart.

What FrontierCode actually measures is whether a human maintainer would trust the code enough to ship it, graded on mergeability rather than whether a test suite passes. Tasks this round came from 55% more repositories than 1.1 and touched far more files per fix. That is a meaningfully different bar than SWE-bench ever set, and it is why a model fine-tuned on a Chinese open-weight base can close most of the gap to a frontier proprietary model for a fraction of the training cost, while still falling short of it on the one metric that was supposed to be hardest to game.

My read: the benchmarks are finally catching up to how skeptical working engineers already were about agent-written code, and a 41% to 45% top score on mergeability proves the point better than any vendor demo could. This category still has a long way to go before it can grade itself honestly.

summary_zh:
WE-2.1 在这个难度等级上的得分为 41.3，高于之前版本的 24.1，并且它是通过在 Moonshot 的 Kimi K3 上运行强化学习而构建的，而不是从头开始预训练新的基础模型。这击败了 Kimi K3.1 本身，它是自己底座的更新版本，得分仅为 19.9。 Claude Opus 5.5 仍然以 45.5% 的成绩位居榜首，但这低于 FrontierCode 1.1 上的 54.6%，因此更难的评分对领先者的打击最大。

成本是它变得有趣的地方。 GPT-6.1 Sol 在每项任务 1.03 美元的情况下得分为 39.0%。 Opus 5.5 每项任务的成本为 12.82 美元，多了六个半点。 Claude Sonnet 5.5 的得分低于 Opus，为 41.0%，但每项任务的成本更高，为 19.94 美元。 GPT-6 Astra 的售价为 42.8%，价格为 6.68 美元。排行榜上的普遍规律是，较高的推理努力并不能可靠地换来较高的分数，有时甚至会换来较低的分数。价格和功能已经悄然分离。

FrontierCode 实际上衡量的是人类维护人员是否足够信任代码来交付它，根据可合并性而不是测试套件是否通过进行评分。这一轮的任务来自比 1.1 多 55% 的存储库，并且每个修复涉及更多的文件。这与 SWE-bench 所设定的标准有很大不同，这就是为什么在中国开放重量基础上进行微调的模型可以以一小部分训练成本缩小与前沿专有模型的大部分差距，同时在一个被认为是最难竞争的指标上仍然达不到它。

我的解读是：基准测试终于赶上了工作工程师对代理编写的代码的怀疑程度，并且可合并性上 41% 到 45% 的最高分比任何供应商演示都更好地证明了这一点。这个类别距离诚实地给自己评分还有很长的路要走。

title: As MCP turns two, Claude gets Skills over MCP and better support for long-running tasks https://t.co/6LyVQo7wiH
title_en: As MCP turns two, Claude gets Skills over MCP and better support for long-running tasks https://thenewstack.io/mcp-skills-tasks-claude/?taid=6b06a3a14e2526000174fffc&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter
title_zh: 随着 MCP 两岁生日，Claude 获得了超过 MCP 的技能，并为长时间运行的任务提供了更好的支持
author: @thenewstack
article_content:
Anthropic enhances Claude with Skills over MCP in public beta, Tasks, Elicitation, and upcoming File Uploads for improved AI-server collaboration.

Anthropic has announced significant updates to its AI platform Claude, marking the second anniversary of the Model Context Protocol (MCP). These updates include the public beta release of Skills over MCP, the general availability of Tasks and Elicitation, and the upcoming rollout of File Uploads. These features aim to enhance Claude's ability to collaborate with MCP servers for more complex and interactive tasks.

Skills over MCP is now in public beta, enabling MCP servers to publish skills alongside their tools. Unlike tool names and descriptions, which only indicate functionality, Skills provide step-by-step workflows, best practices, and tailored playbooks for specific use cases. This allows Claude to handle longer, multi-step tasks efficiently by loading skills only when needed, reducing context usage. Skills automatically update with server changes, requiring no separate installations for users.

Examples of Skills over MCP in action include Shopify assisting with end-to-end online store design, HubSpot onboarding customers, Atlassian leveraging organizational insights, and Carta drafting equity documents from uploaded files. Skills over MCP is available by default for Pro, Max, and Ultra plans and can be enabled for Team plans by administrators. Enterprise availability is expected soon.

Tasks and Elicitation are now generally available, addressing the need for servers to manage long-running, interactive work. Tasks allow servers to execute time-intensive operations or full agent loops in the background while Claude continues other tasks. For instance, ZoomInfo uses Tasks for in-depth account and contact research that previously required multiple prompts.

Elicitation enables servers to pause operations to seek user input for critical decisions, such as spending approvals or data deletions. Examples include Supabase confirming costs before creating paid projects, Railway seeking confirmation before removing services, and GitHub requiring repository names before deletions. These features are available for Pro, Max, and Ultra plans and are rolling out to Team and Enterprise plans.

The upcoming File Uploads feature will allow Claude to send and receive files, such as PDFs, spreadsheets, and images, directly to MCP servers without relying on the context window. This extension is expected to streamline workflows by enabling seamless file-based interactions. File Uploads will be available for Pro, Max, Ultra, and eligible Team and Enterprise plans.

Since its launch two years ago, MCP has become a foundational standard for connecting AI agents to data systems, with over 700 million monthly SDK downloads and more than 10,000 MCP connectors for Claude. Recent improvements include enhanced token efficiency, scalability, simplified authorization through Enterprise Managed Auth, and interactive interfaces via MCP Apps. These developments aim to make MCP more accessible and reliable for developers and organizations.

Anthropic's latest updates underscore its commitment to advancing AI-server collaboration, providing tools that enable agents like Claude to perform more autonomously and effectively in production environments.

title: OpenAI publishes a preprint claiming to prove that the matrix multiplication exponent (ω) is exactly 9/4, addressing a major open problem in mathematics (Deedy/@deedydas)
title_en:
OpenAI just dropped a 111-page proof of a 57-year old math problem: the matrix multiplication exponent (ω) is exactly 9/4.

This problem ranks #31 on ProofAtlas’ top 500 open problems in math and is arguably 2nd only to P = NP in algorithms. 

The problem:
How many steps does it take to multiply two n×n matrices? The schoolbook method takes n^3. The true cost is n^ω. What is ω?

The history:
- 1969: Strassen beats 3 for the first time: 2.807
- 1981: Schönhage, 2.522
- 1990: Coppersmith-Winograd, 2.376
- 1990 to Aug 2026: 36 years to shave off 0.005, 2.3712
- Nov 2026: OpenAI proves the upper and lower bound is 2.25

Wild to see things we were taught in university be changed right before our very eyes.
title_zh: OpenAI 发布了一份预印本，声称证明矩阵乘法指数 (ω) 恰好是 9/4，解决了数学中的一个重大开放问题
author: Deedy Das
author_role: Menlo Ventures 合伙人 / AI 行业风向观察家
full_text_zh:
OpenAI 刚刚放弃了一个长达 57 年的数学问题的 111 页证明：矩阵乘法指数 (ω) 恰好是 9/4。

该问题在 ProofAtlas 的 500 个数学开放问题中排名第 31，并且可以说在算法中仅次于 P = NP，排名第二。

问题：
两个 n×n 矩阵相乘需要多少步？教科书方法取n^3。真实成本是n^ω。 ω是什么？

历史：
- 1969 年：施特拉森首次击败 3：2.807
- 1981 年：舍恩哈格，2.522
- 1990：铜匠-维诺格勒，2.376
- 1990年至2026年8月：36年削减0.005、2.3712
- 2026 年 11 月：OpenAI 证明上限和下限均为 2.25

很高兴看到我们在大学学到的东西就在我们眼前发生改变。
full_text_en:
OpenAI just dropped a 111-page proof of a 57-year old math problem: the matrix multiplication exponent (ω) is exactly 9/4.

This problem ranks #31 on ProofAtlas’ top 500 open problems in math and is arguably 2nd only to P = NP in algorithms. 

The problem:
How many steps does it take to multiply two n×n matrices? The schoolbook method takes n^3. The true cost is n^ω. What is ω?

The history:
- 1969: Strassen beats 3 for the first time: 2.807
- 1981: Schönhage, 2.522
- 1990: Coppersmith-Winograd, 2.376
- 1990 to Aug 2026: 36 years to shave off 0.005, 2.3712
- Nov 2026: OpenAI proves the upper and lower bound is 2.25

Wild to see things we were taught in university be changed right before our very eyes.

1. Simulate Realistic User Traffic

Testing with a few identical requests won't reveal how your application behaves in production.

→ Simulate thousands of concurrent users.
→ Generate different prompt lengths and request types.
→ Reproduce realistic traffic patterns and usage spikes.
→ Test both normal and peak traffic conditions.

title_en:
7 Techniques for Testing AI Applications Under Heavy Traffic

Your AI application works perfectly with 10 users.

But what happens when 10,000 users start sending requests simultaneously?

Suddenly, response times increase, GPU resources become saturated, API rate limits kick in, and requests start failing.

Traditional load testing isn't always enough for AI applications. You also need to understand token generation, model latency, concurrency, and infrastructure bottlenecks.

Here are 7 techniques for testing AI applications under heavy traffic.

title: ▲ ByteDance Seed and HKU researchers just open-sourced Laminar, an RL post-training framework that stops every GPU from waiting on the slowest agent trajectory. The key idea is full decoupling. Rollout, the experience buffer, training and weight sync run
title_en:
▲ ByteDance Seed and HKU researchers just open-sourced Laminar, an RL post-training framework that stops every GPU from waiting on the slowest agent trajectory.

The key idea is full decoupling. Rollout, the experience buffer, training and weight sync run as independent loops. Each trajectory can finish under 1 policy version (version-consistent rollout), so the prefix KV cache is kept and re-prefill is avoided.

On SWE agent RL with Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, SWE-bench Verified went from 46.6% to 52.2%, above the 51.4% baseline peak, with 33% fewer trained samples and 64% fewer GPU-hours. It is a trade-off though: the baseline ran on 64x H100 and Laminar on 64x H800 with different batch settings, so the team calls it an end-to-end comparison, not an ablation.

Apache-2.0, built on verl and Uni-Agent, vLLM for inference and Megatron-LM or FSDP2 for training. The paper reports up to 5.48x throughput on 1024 GPUs......

Full analysis: https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/11/24/bytedance-seed-laminar-async-rl-post-training-framework/

Repo: http://github.com/verl-project/laminar

Paper: http://doi.org/10.1145/3767295.3803580

Blog: http://verl-project.github.io/posts/2026-11-20-laminar/

@tongyx361 @ByteDanceSeed_
title_zh:
▲ 字节跳动种子公司和香港大学研究人员刚刚开源了 Laminar，这是一个 RL 后训练框架，可以阻止每个 GPU 等待最慢的智能体轨迹。

关键思想是完全解耦。推出、经验缓冲、训练和权重同步作为独立循环运行。每个轨迹可以在 1 个策略版本
author: @Marktechpost
summary_zh:
下完成（版本一致的推出），因此保留前缀 KV 缓存并避免重新预填充。

在使用 Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct 的 SWE 代理 RL 上，SWE-bench Verified 从 46.6% 上升到 52.2%，高于 51.4% 基线峰值，训练样本减少了 33%，GPU 小时减少了 64%。但这是一种权衡：基线在 64x H100 上运行，Laminar 在 64x H800 上运行，具有不同的批次设置，因此团队将其称为端到端比较，而不是消融。

full_text_en:
▲ ByteDance Seed and HKU researchers just open-sourced Laminar, an RL post-training framework that stops every GPU from waiting on the slowest agent trajectory.

The key idea is full decoupling. Rollout, the experience buffer, training and weight sync run as independent loops. Each trajectory can finish under 1 policy version (version-consistent rollout), so the prefix KV cache is kept and re-prefill is avoided.

On SWE agent RL with Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, SWE-bench Verified went from 46.6% to 52.2%, above the 51.4% baseline peak, with 33% fewer trained samples and 64% fewer GPU-hours. It is a trade-off though: the baseline ran on 64x H100 and Laminar on 64x H800 with different batch settings, so the team calls it an end-to-end comparison, not an ablation.

Apache-2.0, built on verl and Uni-Agent, vLLM for inference and Megatron-LM or FSDP2 for training. The paper reports up to 5.48x throughput on 1024 GPUs......

title_en:
Japan develops AI agent to crack down on anime and manga piracy

A 2025 government survey by Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs found that 84% of 1,168 suspicious X posts flagged by the AI were illegal. Of 1,564 anime websites flagged, 89% hosted pirated anime, while 94% of 1,935 flagged manga websites hosted pirated manga

The government plans to expand the AI's detection capabilities to overseas piracy sites, with further findings expected by March 2027. Its broader goal is to direct consumers toward legal platforms and make it easier for copyright holders to combat piracy

summary_zh: 开发者利用Claude Code构建由16个代理组成的自治系统，探索从底层流程构建向最终产品交付的演进。
summary_en: A developer built an autonomous system comprising 16 agents using Claude Code. The project initially focused on workflow orchestration and debugging complex agentic interactions, transitioning from systemic process building to final product delivery.
article_content_zh:
在构建多代理系统的过程中，研发者发现核心难点在于处理系统性损坏（Systemic Failure）。通过Claude Code，研发者将初期重心放在代理协作流程（Workflow）的编排上，而非急于产出功能模块。

项目调整重点在于优化多代理状态机的上下文传递逻辑，确保系统在面临复杂代码变更时能自动处理依赖冲突，从而实现了从纯粹研发流程到实际工程产品的跨越。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 开发者基于Anthropic推出的Claude Code工具构建了包含16个协作节点的自治代理系统。该项目在初期侧重于研发工作流的逻辑编排与故障调试，旨在解决多代理环境下的任务分配与状态一致性问题，目前已推进至产品化交付阶段。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: A developer built an autonomous system comprising 16 agents using Claude Code. The project initially focused on workflow orchestration and debugging complex agentic interactions, transitioning from systemic process building to final product delivery.

title: This wouldn’t have sounded possible a year ago, but it’s becoming much more reasonable now that you can get 10X output gains based on the latest in AI model and harness progress. The result is that teams within the same company are driving very different
title_en:
This wouldn’t have sounded possible a year ago, but it’s becoming much more reasonable now that you can get 10X output gains based on the latest in AI model and harness progress. The result is that teams within the same company are driving very different levels of output based on how they’ve adopted AI.

This is a different phenomenon from other tech. Typically in the economy you think of technology adoption rates on a per firm basis, because the company generally adopts a relatively standardized approach to doing the new tech thing. Like “that company has gone digital or adopted the cloud”. So generally the uplift across teams is more or less the same across teams. 

AI is starting to look quite different. Even within the same company you can have a 10X delta between the lowest and highest adopters of AI and the impact they’re seeing. The teams that are able to actually figure out how to redesign their processes to best deploy agents in their workflows can see up to an order of magnitude jump in productivity depending on the job function.

Right now this is heavily concentrated in coding, but more work will become coding adjacent so we can expect similar results elsewhere too. This is going to definitely lead to some wild dynamics within companies.

title: Travel writing is in practice some of the best sociology since the naivete of the foreigner grants the permission to make sweeping generalizations and claims that might otherwise seem too poorly-justified to merit publication. “My people have poor manners” is a
title_en:
Travel writing is in practice some of the best sociology since the naivete of the foreigner grants the permission to make sweeping generalizations and claims that might otherwise seem too poorly-justified to merit publication. “My people have poor manners” is a tough claim to credibly land (Who are you? Exactly which life experiences are you drawing on? And what is your agenda in pushing this line of argument?), whereas “on my travels in Scotland, I noticed that the people had poor manners” seems perfectly reasonable, and indeed thought-provoking. Random samples from a distribution help you understand the mean, and the aleatory nature of travel encounters lends credence to the whole assessment.

Alexis de Tocqueville was just 25 when he traveled across the US and 29 when his observations were published. So, Democracy in America is a giant Substack from a young backpacker, written on his peregrinations as he consumed Montesquieu, Pascal, and Rousseau. He was clearly inspired by Montesquieu’s The Spirit of the Laws, which made the case that countries’ governance, and their laws, are necessarily functions of their cultures and manners.

Building on this, Democracy in America is in many ways a “deep roots” work. Tocqueville is emphatic (at times comically so) that it is America's culture that explains its success, and that its culture in turn stems from the country’s initial conditions. “I think I can see the whole destiny of America contained in the first Puritan who landed on those shores.” He thinks it's important that New England was settled by “a greater mass of intelligence than is to be found in any European nation of our own time” who brought the “best elements of order and morality”. He points out that Mexico doesn’t work nearly as well, despite copying the American constitution and laws, and notes disapprovingly that Virginia was founded by gold-seeking people “without character” whose “turbulent spirit [...] endangered the infant colony.” At the end of Volume I, he concludes, practically table-thumping: “If in the course of this work I have not succeeded in making the reader feel the importance that I attribute to the practical experience of the Americans, to their habits, to their opinions, in a word, to their moeurs, in maintaining their laws, I have failed in the principal object that I proposed to myself in writing it.”

We could look at Democracy in America as an early work of development economics: he is attempting to systematically figure out why it is that America works. (And not just out of casual interest: he was a member of an aristocratic family that was entangled with recent French political upheaval.) By placing primacy on culture, Tocqueville’s explanation deviates from the institutional and structural explanations often favored by today’s economists. Daron Acemoglu, to choose one prominent present-day example, firmly rejects the “Culture Hypothesis” in Why Nations Fail. In explaining Virginia, he instead points to structural incentives. Poor Economics, from Esther Duflo and Abhijit Banerjee, contains a similar rejection of cultural explanations. Comparable examples from other leading economists abound. An aversion to cultural explanations is of course understandable for all sorts of reasons: cultures are opaque, protean, and resistant to quantitative characterization. Cultures are themselves shaped by other factors, such that it’s hard to attribute definitive causality, and it’s uncomfortable to adopt anything that feels like a normative orientation. Nonetheless, can we explain why New England differs from Mexico without starting with the inner disposition, habits, and worldviews of the people? Tocqueville thinks not.

For all culture’s importance, it would be wrong to suggest that Tocqueville believes that culture is the only factor that matters. He dwells extensively on how America’s institutions are important, and how the microstructure of town life shapes the country’s federal civics. It is also true that development economics has taken a more strongly cultural turn in recent times, most of all in Joel Mokyr’s 2025 Nobel Prize. Mokyr’s work feels downright Tocquevillian at times: contra the intimidatingly quantitative econometrics that dominates today, Mokyr engages in an extended and earnestly curious qualitative synthesis of relevant patterns (in his case, in service of trying to figure out why the Industrial Revolution started when it did). Like Tocqueville, he concludes that the best explanation places cultural changes above other factors.

I’m very interested in whether LLMs will help us characterize culture in new and at least somewhat more objective ways. Can we ingest and process vast quantities of work that may not even have been OCR’d or translated until now? Can we map cultural corpora to vectors in some foundation model embedding space? Where large datasets and computational techniques enabled new ways to analyze many economic questions in recent decades, perhaps LLMs will enable newly objective light to be shone on hypothesized cultural explanations.

–

Speaking of LLMs, Democracy in America is a book about a new kind of society, and a Frenchman trying to figure out what the future might hold. As we sit on the cusp of another upheaval, is there anything that reads with resonance today?

Part of the declared promise of AI is that it might obviate our need to work. In slavery, Tocqueville observes a version of this phenomenon on his travels. He is struck by its barbarous cruelty (and his travel companion later published an anti-slavery novel), but also by its effects on the slaveowners themselves. He perceived that the practice rendered work dishonorable, and thus yielded idleness, ignorance, and pride. Slavery, he says, “enervates the powers of the mind, and benumbs the activity of man.” He observes the contrast between slavery-rejecting Ohio and slavery-embracing Kentucky. In Kentucky, “those who are active and enlightened either do nothing or pass over into the State of Ohio, where they may work without dishonor.” Ohio’s harvests are more abundant, homes are more elegant, and people seem to be “in enjoyment of that wealth and contentment which is the reward of labor.”

Presented with an evil release from manual labor, the Kentuckians did not apply themselves to productive studies and great creations, and the South did not become a new Florence. There is an obvious question for us: how will AI change our relationship with work? Will it become dishonorable, and what will the reflexive effect on our society be if so? Should this change our view of utopian visions of “automated communism”?

Tocqueville also raises the issue of coexistence with more advanced neighbors. He noted that the arrival of the Europeans had been ruinous for the Indians (as he termed them). European technology – firearms, metallurgy, steam power – was a kind of superintelligence relative to their practices. The disruptions and destruction wrought by the settlers led to cultural problems (“their traditions obscured, and the chain of their recollections broken”), which in turn led to declines in both the physical and the moral conditions of the tribes. Tocqueville believed that the Indians faced a choice given that their old way of living was no longer viable: they could adopt European mores or suffer inevitable destruction. He predicted that they would reject cultural adaptation, and thus were “doomed to perish”. This is all to say that the arrival of the European settlers was in Tocqueville’s eyes injurious to the Indians not only because of the direct violence and displacement, but also because the contact was itself so disruptive to their societies that their cultures ceased to function. Some of this was later observed in Pacific island societies – even though there wasn’t the same degree of violent dispossession, the mere presence of Western contact was intrinsically destabilizing. In many visions of the future, superintelligent AIs are much more numerous than humans, with consequences that are hard to predict. In Tocqueville, there is a cautionary suggestion.

Given the new powers afforded by AI, there is a question of what we will choose to do with it – to the extent that we are in control, we will wield a vastly expanded authority. Americans faced some version of this question: in democracy, society was endowed with wholly new ways to express its collective will, with no ultimate superior power, for society was for the first time in charge of itself. Tocqueville repeatedly emphasizes how democracy thus increased the importance of religion as a regulator of hasty or unwise impulses. “Whilst the law permits the Americans to do what they please, religion prevents them from conceiving, and forbids them to commit, what is rash or unjust.” If we take seriously Tocqueville’s idea that religion was a critical complement in ensuring that people shaped societies in prudent ways, Democracy implicitly raises a question: which are the ideas, philosophies, religions, or doctrines that will help us wield AI well?

Part of what’s interesting and memorable about the work is Tocqueville’s combination of curiosity, enthusiasm, and slight ambivalence about democracy itself. He grants that democracy is likely to be the future of governance, and he is admiring of what it has achieved in America, but he can’t avoid concerns about what it may augur (such as the unchecked and totalitarian impulses of the mob). At the end of Volume II, he describes his chief concern with democracy: that it may yield a new form of despotism that he struggles to define. He fears not tyrants, but, he says, “guardians”. He is worried about a world where:

> Above this race of men stands an immense and tutelary power, which takes upon itself alone to secure their gratifications, and to watch over their fate. [...] It would be like the authority of a parent, if, like that authority, its object was to prepare men for manhood; but it seeks on the contrary to keep them in perpetual childhood: it is well content that the people should rejoice, provided they think of nothing but rejoicing. For their happiness such a government willingly labors, but it chooses to be the sole agent and the only arbiter of that happiness. [...] What remains, but to spare them all the care of thinking and all the trouble of living? Thus it every day renders the exercise of the free agency of man less useful and less frequent; it circumscribes the will within a narrower range, and gradually robs a man of all the uses of himself.

The Iain Banks Culture novels are often invoked by AI proponents. For Tocqueville, something strikingly like the world that they describe was his dystopian fear, for a world bereft of autonomy would be intrinsically degrading and humiliating for humanity:

> The will of man is not shattered, but softened, bent, and guided: men are seldom forced by it to act, but they are constantly restrained from acting: such a power does not destroy, but it prevents existence; it does not tyrannize, but it compresses, enervates, extinguishes, and stupefies a people, till each nation is reduced to be nothing better than a flock of timid and industrious animals, of which the government is the shepherd.

The analogy to animals is noteworthy. In interviews, AI leaders occasionally analogize the future human state to that of pets. Banks himself noted that in the Culture novels, “[humans] have a status somewhere between passengers, pets and parasites.” In Richard Brautigan’s famous poem, All Watched Over by Machines of Loving Grace, he hopes that humans are “returned to our mammal brothers and sisters”.

Tocqueville at heart thought that agency and cultivation of people came above all else. He dreaded anesthetized placidity. In soft despotism, he feared that “ambition will lose its vigor and its greatness; that human passions will be appeased and lowered at the same time”. This vigor was for Tocqueville at the heart of what was admirable in America, whose bustle and intensity he repeatedly extols. American self-reliance and self-direction are paramount: “the citizen of the United States is taught from his earliest infancy to rely upon his own exertions in order to resist the evils and the difficulties of life.” For Tocqueville, any kind of servile and manicured comfort was not just undesirable, but a negation of the American promise.

Many of the Elysian visions for AI hinge on AI resolving the messy coordination challenges that afflict humans. (Scott Alexander invokes this vision towards the end of Meditations on Moloch.) For Tocqueville, the arbitration of such differences was precisely the constructive activity that reaffirmed our agency. Townships, juries, associations, and their attendant squabbles are how culture is reinforced and how judgment is cultivated. When a town decides whether to fund a school, there are two outputs: a decision, and practice in governance itself. If AI could resolve such matters, we might get better outcomes, but will we get better people?
title_zh: 旅行写作实际上是最好的社会学之一，因为外国人的天真允许他们做出全面的概括和主张，否则这些概括和主张可能看起来缺乏合理性，不值得发表。 “我的人民没有礼貌”是一个很难获得可信土地的说法（你是谁？你到底借鉴了哪些生活经历？你推动这一论点的议程是
author: @patrickc
summary_zh:
什么？），而“在我在苏格兰的旅行中，我注意到人们没有礼貌”似乎完全合理，而且确实发人深省。分布中的随机样本可帮助您了解平均值，而旅行遭遇的偶然性则为整个评估提供了可信度。

亚历克西斯·德·托克维尔 (Alexis de Tocqueville) 穿越美国时年仅 25 岁，发表观察结果时年仅 29 岁。所以，《美国的民主》是一位年轻背包客写的一个巨大的子堆栈，写的是他在阅读孟德斯鸠、帕斯卡和卢梭时的旅行经历。他显然受到了孟德斯鸠的《法律精神》的启发，该书认为国家的治理及其法律必然是其文化和行为方式的功能。

在此基础上，《美国的民主》在很多方面都是一部“根深蒂固”的作品。托克维尔强调（有时是滑稽的），美国的文化解释了它的成功，而它的文化又源于这个国家的初始条件。 “我想我可以看到美国的整个命运包含在第一个登陆这些海岸的清教徒身上。”他认为，重要的是，新英格兰的定居者“比我们这个时代的任何欧洲国家都拥有更多的智慧”，他们带来了“秩序和道德的最佳要素”。他指出，尽管抄袭了美国宪法和法律，但墨西哥的运作情况却差强人意，他不以为然地指出，弗吉尼亚是由“没有品格”的淘金者建立的，他们的“狂暴精神……危及了刚刚诞生的殖民地”。在第一卷的结尾，他几乎是震撼地总结道：“如果在这部作品的过程中，我没有成功地让读者感受到我赋予美国人的实践经验、他们的习惯、他们的观点，总之，他们的摩尔和维护他们的法律的重要性，那么我就没有实现我在写这本书时向自己提出的主要目标。”

我们可以将《美国的民主》视为发展经济学的早期著作：他试图系统地找出美国运转的原因。 （不仅仅是出于偶然的兴趣：他是一个与最近的法国政治动荡纠缠在一起的贵族家庭的成员。）通过将文化置于首位，托克维尔的解释偏离了当今经济学家通常青睐的制度和结构解释。达龙·阿塞莫格鲁（Daron Acemoglu）选择当今一个著名的例子，坚决拒绝《国家为何失败》中的“文化假设”。在解释弗吉尼亚州时，他转而指出了结构性激励措施。埃丝特·迪弗洛和阿比吉特·班纳吉的《贫穷经济学》也包含了对文化解释的类似拒绝。其他领先经济学家的类似例子比比皆是。由于各种原因，对文化解释的厌恶当然是可以理解的：文化是不透明的、千变万化的，并且抵制定量表征。文化本身是由其他因素塑造的，因此很难归因于明确的因果关系，并且采用任何感觉像是规范取向的东西都会让人感到不舒服。尽管如此，我们能否在不从人们的内在性格、习惯和世界观出发的情况下解释为什么新英格兰与墨西哥不同呢？托克维尔认为不是。

尽管文化很重要，但如果认为托克维尔认为文化是唯一重要的因素，那就错了。他详细阐述了美国机构的重要性，以及城镇生活的微观结构如何塑造该国的联邦公民制度。发展经济学近年来也确实发生了更强烈的文化转向，尤其是乔尔·莫克尔 (Joel Mokyr) 获得 2025 年诺贝尔奖。莫基尔的作品有时给人一种彻头彻尾的托克维尔式的感觉：与当今占主导地位的令人生畏的定量计量经济学相反，莫基尔对相关模式进行了广泛而真诚的定性综合（在他的例子中，是为了试图找出工业革命为何在此时开始）。和托克维尔一样，他得出的结论是，最好的解释是将文化变化置于其他因素之上。

我对法学硕士是否能帮助我们以新的、至少更客观的方式描述文化非常感兴趣。我们能否摄取和处理大量迄今为止可能尚未进行 OCR 或翻译的工作？我们可以将文化语料库映射到某些基础模型嵌入空间中的向量吗？近几十年来，大型数据集和计算技术为分析许多经济问题提供了新的方法，也许法学硕士将为假设的文化解释提供新的客观视角。

–

说到法学硕士，《美国的民主》是一本关于新型社会的书，讲述的是一个法国人试图弄清楚未来会怎样。当我们正处于另一场剧变的风口浪尖时，今天有什么东西读起来能引起共鸣吗？

人工智能所宣称的部分承诺是它可能会消除我们工作的需要。在奴隶制中，托克维尔在他的旅行中观察到了这种现象的一个版本。他对其野蛮的残忍感到震惊（他的旅伴后来出版了一本反奴隶制小说），但也对其对奴隶主本身的影响感到震惊。他认为这种做法使工作变得不光彩，从而导致懒惰、无知和骄傲。他说，奴隶制“削弱了思想的力量，麻木了人类的活动”。他观察了拒绝奴隶制的俄亥俄州和拥护奴隶制的肯塔基州之间的对比。在肯塔基州，“那些积极主动、开明的人要么什么也不做，要么就转到俄亥俄州，在那里他们可以毫无耻辱地工作。”俄亥俄州的收成更加丰富，房屋更加优雅，人们似乎“享受着劳动的回报所带来的财富和满足”。

肯塔基人从体力劳动中得到了邪恶的释放，他们没有致力于富有成效的研究和伟大的创造，南方也没有成为新的佛罗伦萨。我们面临一个显而易见的问题：人工智能将如何改变我们与工作的关系？它会变得不光彩吗？如果是的话，会对我们的社会产生什么反射性影响？这是否应该改变我们对“自动化共产主义”乌托邦愿景的看法？

托克维尔还提出了与更先进的邻国共存的问题。他指出，欧洲人的到来对印第安人（他是这样称呼他们的）来说是毁灭性的。欧洲技术——火器、冶金、蒸汽动力——相对于他们的实践来说是一种超级智能。定居者造成的破坏和破坏导致了文化问题（“他们的传统被模糊了，他们的记忆链被打破了”），这反过来又导致了部落的物质和道德状况的下降。托克维尔认为，鉴于印第安人旧有的生活方式不再可行，他们面临着一个选择：他们要么接受欧洲的习俗，要么遭受不可避免的毁灭。他预测他们会拒绝文化适应，因此“注定要灭亡”。这就是说，在托克维尔看来，欧洲定居者的到来对印第安人造成了伤害，不仅因为直接的暴力和流离失所，而且因为这种接触本身对他们的社会造成了如此大的破坏，以至于他们的文化停止了运作。后来在太平洋岛屿社会中观察到了其中的一些情况——尽管没有同等程度的暴力剥夺，但西方接触的存在本质上是不稳定的。在未来的许多愿景中，超级智能人工智能的数量比人类多得多，其后果难以预测。托克维尔有一个警告性的建议。

鉴于人工智能提供的新权力，存在一个问题，即我们将选择如何利用它——在我们能够控制的范围内，我们将拥有极大扩展的权力。美国人面临着这个问题的某种版本：在民主制度下，社会被赋予了全新的方式来表达其集体意志，没有最终的超级权力，因为社会第一次掌握了自己。托克维尔反复强调，民主如何增强了宗教作为调节草率或不明智冲动的作用的重要性。 “虽然法律允许美国人做他们想做的事，但宗教却阻止他们怀孕，并禁止他们做出鲁莽或不公正的事情。”如果我们认真对待托克维尔的观点，即宗教是确保人们以审慎方式塑造社会的关键补充，那么民主就隐含地提出了一个问题：哪些思想、哲学、宗教或教义将帮助我们很好地运用人工智能？

这部作品的有趣和令人难忘的部分原因在于托克维尔对民主本身的好奇、热情和轻微的矛盾心理的结合。他承认民主很可能是治理的未来，他对民主在美国取得的成就表示钦佩，但他无法避免对其可能预示的事情的担忧（例如暴民不受控制的极权主义冲动）。在第二卷的结尾，他描述了他对民主的主要担忧：民主可能会产生一种他努力定义的新形式的专制主义。他说，他害怕的不是暴君，而是“守护者”。他担心这样一个世界：

> 在这个人类种族之上矗立着一种巨大的守护力量，它独自承担起确保他们的满足并守护他们的命运的责任。 [...] 如果像父母的权威一样，它的目的是让男人为成年做准备，那么它就像父母的权威一样；但它的目的恰恰相反，让他们永远处于童年状态：人民应该感到高兴，只要他们只想到高兴，它就很满足了。为了他们的幸福，这样的政府愿意努力工作，但它选择成为这种幸福的唯一代理人和唯一仲裁者。 [...]除了让他们免去思考的烦恼和生活的烦恼之外，还剩下什么？因此，人的自由意志的行使日益变得不那么有用，也越来越不频繁。它把意志限制在一个更窄的范围内，并逐渐剥夺一个人对自己的一切用处。

人工智能支持者经常引用伊恩·班克斯的文化小说。对于托克维尔来说，与他们所描述的世界惊人相似的是他的反乌托邦恐惧，因为一个失去自治的世界本质上是对人类的侮辱和羞辱：

> 人的意志不是被粉碎，而是被软化、弯曲和引导：人很少被它强迫去行动，而是不断地被限制去行动：这样的力量不会毁灭，但它阻止存在；它不是暴政，而是压迫、削弱、消灭和麻痹人民，直到每个国家沦为一群胆怯而勤劳的动物，而政府就是它们的牧羊人。

与动物的类比值得注意。在采访中，人工智能领导者偶尔会将未来人类的状态与宠物的状态进行类比。班克斯本人指出，在文化小说中，“[人类]的地位介于乘客、宠物和寄生虫之间。”在理查德·布劳蒂根（Richard Brautigan）的著名诗《一切都被慈爱的机器守护着》中，他希望人类“回到我们的哺乳动物兄弟姐妹身边”。

托克维尔内心认为，人的能动性和修养高于一切。他害怕麻醉般的平静。在软专制下，他担心“野心将失去活力和伟大；人类的激情将同时被平息和降低”。对托克维尔来说，这种活力是美国令人钦佩的事物的核心，他一再赞扬美国的喧嚣和强度。美国人的自力更生和自我指导至关重要：“美国公民从小就被教导要依靠自己的努力来抵抗生活中的邪恶和困难。”对于托克维尔来说，任何形式的奴性和精心设计的舒适不仅是不可取的，而且是对美国承诺的否定。

人工智能的许多极乐愿景都依赖于人工智能解决困扰人类的混乱协调挑战。 （斯科特·亚历山大在《摩洛沉思录》的结尾处引用了这一愿景。）对于托克维尔来说，对这些分歧的仲裁恰恰是重申我们能动性的建设性活动。乡镇、陪审团、协会以及随之而来的争吵是文化得以强化、判断力得以培养的方式。当一个城镇决定是否资助一所学校时，有两个产出：决策和治理本身的实践。如果人工智能能够解决这些问题，我们可能会得到更好的结果，但我们会得到更好的人吗？
