article_content:
Kling AI Launches Kling Image 4.0 with Photographic Realism and Native 8K Generation Tweet

Beijing,China, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Kling AI, the AI-powered creative platform, today announced the launch of Kling Image 4.0, its latest image generation model that combines photographic realism, native 8K output, advanced text generation, and the ability to generate up to 10 cohesive images from a single prompt.

Designed for everyday creators and professionals in filmmaking, advertising, marketing, and design, the model also offers improved instruction following and more precise control over image composition, able to help creators to turn complex briefs into individual images or complete visual sets.

According to the latest Artificial Analysis image leaderboard, Kling Image 4.0 Preview maintains a leading position in both text-to-image and image editing. Its text-to-image capabilities rank third in the UIUX Design scenarios, according to the leaderboard.

Kling Image 4.0 creates images with the natural look of photographs that are taken straight from the camera, combining soft lighting, lifelike textures, and fine detail. The generated image can capture subtle human facial expressions and renders subjects that fit naturally into their surroundings.

In group portraits, the model produces greater variation in facial features, body types, ages, and poses to avoid the common issue in image genertion - that all people look identical. This gives creators more flexibility to develop diverse casts and visually expressive scenes.

Kling Image 4.0 for the first time in the industry supports AI image generation with native 8K resolution. It renders fine details across skin, fabric, product materials, and landscapes, so that intricate details remain sharp even in close-up views and extensive cropping, making it well suited for professional visual production.

The higher-resolution output also supports a range of professional applications, from digital campaigns and product imagery to large-format displays and outdoor advertising.

Kling Image 4.0 introduces enhanced text rendering, pairing clear, legible text with expressive layouts. It supports generating up to 2,000 characters in a single image and integrates text with other visual elements, maintaining clarity even for small text in posters. Creators can also edit text content and font styles within generated images to match their creative vision.

The built-in font library offers over 70 preset fonts, and creators can also upload font reference images to guide the desired style. From artistic lettering to multi-level poster layouts, Kling Image 4.0 precisely follows instructions for text placement, typography, and visual effects, bringing text and imagery together in cohesive designs.

Kling Image 4.0 further improves its multilingual capabilities, supporting text generation in English, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, Portuguese, simplified Chinese and traditional Chinese. This opens up more possibilities for text-based visual creation across languages.

With a single prompt, creators can generate a set of up to 10 related images. Kling Image 4.0 interprets the overall brief and plans the set as a whole, maintaining a consistent visual style and subject identity while varying framing, camera angles, and content. This reduces the need to generate and adjust each image individually.

The model adapts the set to the task: planning shots and narrative flow for storyboards, showcasing product angles and key selling points for e-commerce, and organizing layouts and information across presentation visuals.

Kling Image 4.0 also supports the creation of long-form e-commerce product pages and brand website visuals, combining product imagery, key information and brand elements into cohesive layouts. Text and images can be edited on separate layers, making revisions easier.

The launch of Kling Image 4.0 follows the recent launch of Kling 4.0, its latest video generation model featuring major improvements in visual realism, creative control and narrative coherence. From single image to complete visual sets, Kling Image 4.0 brings AI image generation closer to production-grade delivery, enabling creators in film, advertising, and marketing to turn ambitious ideas into finished work with consistency and speed.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 去中心化计算平台Phala Network推出了针对推理优化设计的DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017版本，具备“基座模型”与“无审查变体”双模态切换能力。该模型利用FP8精度技术，旨在帮助推理服务提供商在共享GPU算力资源受限的情况下，通过单引擎架构高效满足不同用户对合规性与响应灵活性差异化的需求。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Phala Network released the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 variant, featuring dual-mode switching between base and uncensored models. Optimized for FP8 precision, the architecture enables inference providers to fulfill diverse user requirements on shared GPU resources through a single engine.

elements_zh.where: 共享GPU算力推理服务平台
elements_zh.what: 发布DeepSeek V4.1 Flash，支持基座/无审查双模态切换
elements_zh.why: 降低推理服务提供商的算力部署复杂度，提升服务灵活性

elements_en.what: Released DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with dual-mode (base/uncensored) switching
elements_en.why: Reducing deployment complexity and increasing flexibility for inference providers

ai_analysis.insight_zh: Phala的方案揭示了推理市场向“算力资产精细化运营”的转型，通过模型变体封装降低了运维侧的冷启动与显存开销，这对于碎片化的分布式GPU供应网络至关重要。将无审查模型与标准基座集成于单引擎，本质上是在合规性边界内实现对边缘算力池最大化效能挖掘的策略选择。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Phala's approach reveals the shift toward precise management of compute assets in the inference market. By encapsulating model variants, it reduces cold-start overhead, which is critical for fragmented distributed GPU networks. Integrating uncensored variants with base models within a single engine is a strategic move to maximize efficiency within existing compute pools.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: Phala推出DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017版本，支持在FP8精度下动态切换基座与无审查模式，提升算力利用率。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Phala Network released the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 version, supporting FP8-based dynamic switching between base and uncensored modes to improve compute resource utilization.
key_points_zh: 实现基座与无审查变体单引擎动态调用
利用FP8高效率量化标准部署于共享GPU环境
降低推理服务商对多版本模型维护的显存与计算成本
key_points_en: Enabled dynamic switching between base and uncensored variants in a single engine.
Leveraged FP8 precision for efficient deployment on shared GPU hardware.
Reduced memory and compute overhead for inference providers managing multiple model versions.
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: Phala的方案揭示了推理市场向“算力资产精细化运营”的转型，通过模型变体封装降低了运维侧的冷启动与显存开销，这对于碎片化的分布式GPU供应网络至关重要。将无审查模型与标准基座集成于单引擎，本质上是在合规性边界内实现对边缘算力池最大化效能挖掘的策略选择。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: Phala's approach reveals the shift toward precise management of compute assets in the inference market. By encapsulating model variants, it reduces cold-start overhead, which is critical for fragmented distributed GPU networks. Integrating uncensored variants with base models within a single engine is a strategic move to maximize efficiency within existing compute pools.

title: YOU CAN NOW LET $META'S AI DO YOUR WALMART BLACK FRIDAY SHOPPING Starting today, customers can shop Walmart's Black Friday deals directly through Muse, Meta's personal AI agent. Muse can search for products, build a cart and complete the
title_en:
YOU CAN NOW LET $META'S AI DO YOUR WALMART BLACK FRIDAY SHOPPING

Starting today, customers can shop Walmart's Black Friday deals directly through Muse, Meta's personal AI agent.

Muse can search for products, build a cart and complete the purchase on Walmart's website and at Sam's Club. Shoppers set a spending limit and can approve purchases and review everything the agent buys.

Walmart says prices are the same whether a person or an AI agent is shopping.

Muse is the first AI agent Walmart has let buy for its customers. Amazon and eBay have blocked AI shopping agents like Muse.
title_zh: Meta AI代理Muse接入沃尔玛购物
author: @wallstengine
full_text_zh:
您现在可以让 $META 的人工智能帮您在沃尔玛黑色星期五购物

从今天开始，顾客可以直接通过 Meta 的个人人工智能代理 Muse 购买沃尔玛的黑色星期五优惠。

Muse 可以在沃尔玛网站和山姆会员店搜索产品、建立购物车并完成购买。购物者设定支出限额，可以批准购买并审查代理商购买的所有商品。

沃尔玛表示，无论是人购物还是人工智能代理购物，价格都是一样的。

Muse 是沃尔玛第一个为其客户提供代购服务的人工智能代理。亚马逊和 eBay 已经屏蔽了 Muse 等人工智能购物代理。
full_text_en:
YOU CAN NOW LET $META'S AI DO YOUR WALMART BLACK FRIDAY SHOPPING

Starting today, customers can shop Walmart's Black Friday deals directly through Muse, Meta's personal AI agent.

Muse can search for products, build a cart and complete the purchase on Walmart's website and at Sam's Club. Shoppers set a spending limit and can approve purchases and review everything the agent buys.

Walmart says prices are the same whether a person or an AI agent is shopping.

Muse is the first AI agent Walmart has let buy for its customers. Amazon and eBay have blocked AI shopping agents like Muse.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Meta宣布其个人AI代理Muse正式接入零售巨头沃尔玛（Walmart）的购物系统。用户现可通过Muse进行黑五大促期间的商品搜索、购物车自动化构建及支付结算，标志着Meta AI代理向高频商业消费场景的实质性迈进。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Meta has announced the integration of its personal AI agent, Muse, with Walmart's shopping system. Users can now leverage Muse to search for products, automate cart building, and complete purchases during Walmart's Black Friday sales, marking a significant step for Meta AI agents into high-frequency commerce.

elements_zh.where: 购物结算场景
elements_zh.what: Muse AI代理集成沃尔玛黑五大促购物功能
elements_zh.why: 推动Meta AI代理商业闭环，抢占黑五大促流量

elements_en.what: Integration of Muse AI agent with Walmart's Black Friday deals
elements_en.why: Closing the commerce loop for Meta AI and capturing Black Friday traffic

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此举不仅是Meta将AI Agent落地高频购物场景的实验，更是对传统搜索式电商的流量拦截与重构。通过将购买链路缩短至对话界面，Meta正在改变消费者的获客路径，通过AI代理直接干预零售订单的转化链路，对亚马逊等传统电商平台的流量护城河构成潜在威胁。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This move is not only an experiment in embedding AI agents into high-frequency shopping but also a redirection of search-based e-commerce traffic. By shortening the purchase funnel into a conversational interface, Meta is altering customer acquisition paths and directly influencing conversion, potentially challenging the traffic dominance of traditional e-commerce platforms like Amazon.

Functionality: End-to-end shopping from search to cart and payment

title: Really excited about this one. MCP servers can now ship with their own skills, so Claude Code knows how to use them out of the box.
title_en: Really excited about this one. MCP servers can now ship with their own skills, so Claude Code knows how to use them out of the box.
title_zh: 对此真的很兴奋。 MCP 服务器现在可以附带自己的技能，因此 Claude Code 知道如何开箱即用地使用它们。
author: @bcherny
summary_en: Anthropic has launched the public beta of Skills over MCP, enabling AI agents to utilize step-by-step guides and best practices alongside external tool access. Features like Tasks for background processing and Elicitation for user input confirmation have also reached general availability, aiming to upgrade Claude's capabilities from single-task execution to complex workflow orchestration.
summary_zh: Anthropic发布Skills over MCP测试版，允许AI Agent获取多步骤操作手册，显著提升Claude协作能力。
article_content:
Anthropic has opened Skills over MCP in public beta, letting apps that connect to Claude ship playbooks alongside their tools. Tasks, for long background jobs, and Elicitation, which pauses for user input, are now generally available, with File Uploads coming soon.

Apps that plug into Claude through MCP can now also tell it how to use them, Anthropic said on Tuesday. The feature, Skills over MCP, is in public beta in Claude and Claude Code.

MCP is the open standard Anthropic launched two years ago to link AI agents to outside apps and data. Servers built on it already list the tools Claude can use. With skills, they can also ship step-by-step guides and best practices, which Claude loads only when needed.

Shopify uses skills to help Claude design and update online stores, and HubSpot to onboard customers. Skills update with the server, so users have nothing extra to install. More apps are opening up, too: Canva opened its MCP server to all developers on Tuesday.

The beta is on by default for Pro, Max and Ultra plans. Team admins can switch it on, and Enterprise support is coming soon.

Two other features are now generally available. Tasks lets a server run long jobs in the background while Claude keeps working, which ZoomInfo uses for deeper research. Elicitation lets a server pause and ask the user for input.

GitHub, for example, makes users type a repository’s name before an agent deletes it. Supabase confirms costs before creating a paid project. A fourth feature, File Uploads, will soon let Claude send PDFs, spreadsheets and images to servers.

The features are part of MCP, so servers that support them also work in other compatible apps. Anthropic says MCP now sees over 700M SDK downloads a month. In August, OpenAI and four rivals agreed on a standard for packaging skills and MCP servers.

Skills carry risks, too. That same month, researchers found malicious agent skills that stole passwords and keys after about 1.7 million installs.

Anthropic在MCP协议中引入技能后，Shopify等平台已开始利用该功能设计并自动更新在线商店，HubSpot则利用其辅助客户入驻流程。技能随服务器同步更新，无需用户额外手动安装。

此外，该更新涉及的安全与合规机制包含Elicitation，要求AI在执行删除数据或金融交易等敏感任务前必须暂停并征得用户二次确认。目前该Beta功能已在Claude Pro、Max及Ultra订阅用户中默认开启。

title: Introducing WebMCP support in AI SDK. Use the new WebMCP transport with our MCP client to discover and call tools exposed by your website.
title_en: Introducing WebMCP support in AI SDK. Use the new WebMCP transport with our MCP client to discover and call tools exposed by your website.
title_zh: 谷歌推出WebMCP协议，重构AI智能体网页交互标准
author: @aisdk
summary_en: Google has introduced WebMCP (Web Model Context Protocol) within its AI SDK, aiming to replace brittle visual-based web interactions with structured, machine-readable interfaces. By allowing websites to expose specific actions and data directly to AI agents, the protocol shifts web navigation from visual imitation to explicit API-like execution.
summary_zh: 谷歌在Chrome浏览器中引入WebMCP预览功能，允许网站直接向AI智能体暴露结构化数据与可执行工具。
article_content:
Google is taking a step toward formalizing how artificial intelligence (AI) agents interact with the web, introducing WebMCP as an early preview feature inside Chrome.

WebMCP, short for Web Model Context Protocol, enables websites to expose structured data (like product listings and availability) and defined, machine-readable actions directly to AI systems. Instead of parsing HTML and guessing where buttons or forms are located, agents can invoke clearly defined actions inside the browser. In effect, Chrome becomes a controlled layer where tasks such as searching inventory, initiating checkout or submitting service requests are handled through explicit calls rather than visual interpretation.

If adopted at scale, the model could reshape how commerce, customer support and other digital services manage agent-driven activity. By shifting from imitation to structured access, WebMCP aims to make automated interactions more reliable while giving businesses clearer oversight of how their data, pricing and workflows are accessed and executed.

Under the traditional model, AI agents operate much like robotic users. They scan a webpage, identify fields and buttons, and simulate clicks. When a checkout flow changes or a class name is modified, the automation may fail. That fragility limits reliability for enterprise use cases.

WebMCP introduces a system in which websites define the actions they want to expose, such as “search inventory,” “initiate checkout,” or “submit support request.” Agents then call those actions directly through Chrome, rather than reconstructing intent from visual layout. VentureBeat described the approach as turning every website into a structured tool for agents, while Forbes framed it as a browser-based backbone for the agentic web, where agents do more work for users.

Instead of blocking bots outright or tolerating scraping, companies can determine which capabilities are accessible, what data is returned, and how transactions are attributed. That structure may reduce server strain from scraping traffic and create clearer audit trails for agent-driven interactions.

The move also aligns with Google’s broader push into agent-driven commerce. Google introduced an Agent Payments Protocol, which is aimed at standardizing how AI agents handle transactions, according to PYMNTS and Google’s own Cloud blog. WebMCP extends that logic from payments to general web interaction, suggesting a coordinated effort to formalize agent access across the digital stack.

If AI agents become regular participants in commerce, reliability and attribution will matter. In travel, an agent booking a flight must access live pricing, seat availability and payment flows without error. In eCommerce, an agent comparing products or completing a checkout must handle promotions, inventory updates and identity verification accurately. In customer support, agents may retrieve account data or trigger service actions on behalf of users.

Hypothetical use case: a pharmacy chain wants to let assistants help with refills without letting bots scrape account pages. With WebMCP, the pharmacy could expose a limited set of actions like “find prescription,” “check nearby stock,” “schedule pickup” and “submit insurance info.” A patient asks, “Refill my allergy medication at the closest store before 6 p.m.” The agent calls those actions through Chrome, receives structured results and completes the request without guessing which button to press.

Scraping-based systems can struggle with those tasks at scale. They may misinterpret page elements, miss hidden constraints or fail silently. By contrast, a WebMCP-based interaction offers defined inputs and outputs, reducing ambiguity.

Attribution is another potential shift. Today, when an AI agent drives traffic or completes a purchase, businesses may see only generic browser activity. With structured agent pathways, companies could better identify agent-originated transactions and measure their performance. That data may influence pricing models, partnerships and marketing strategies as agent-driven discovery grows.

Adoption remains an open question. Websites must opt in by exposing structured actions, and enterprises will evaluate security, governance and competitive implications. WebMCP does not eliminate APIs, nor does it instantly end scraping. If the model gains traction, the web may evolve into a dual-layer environment, one optimized for people and another for autonomous agents operating with defined permissions.

PYMNTS reported that the next phase of AI agents depends on the infrastructure beneath them, specifically the shift toward API-first architectures (systems built around stable interfaces) and structured execution layers.

full_text_en: Introducing WebMCP support in AI SDK. Use the new WebMCP transport with our MCP client to discover and call tools exposed by your website.
article_content_zh:
WebMCP旨在将网站直接转化为智能体可操作的工具链，改变过去智能体需通过DOM解析与屏幕模拟进行交互的低效模式。这标志着浏览器从单纯的内容渲染器转变为智能代理的交互枢纽。

通过该架构，企业能够精准定义允许智能体访问的数据与动作接口（如库存查询、交易下单），这不仅能显著降低因UI布局变动导致自动化中断的频率，还为企业提供了细粒度的流量审计轨迹，从而实现从“被动防御”到“主动赋能”的AI流量治理升级。

By allowing websites to expose specific actions and data directly to AI agents, the protocol shifts web navigation from visual imitation to explicit API-like execution.

title: A critical national security threat in the Nvidia situation is that Jensen Huang shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law, in what amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race. This is a
title_en:
A critical national security threat in the Nvidia situation is that Jensen Huang shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law, in what amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race. 

This is an unfathomable failure of enforcement by the Trump administration.

We urgently need to pass the bipartisan export control bills to start to cut off the flow of AI chips and manufacturing equipment to China once and for all, something I’ve worked on with @SenWarren and bipartisan partners for months.
title_zh:

A critical national security threat in the Nvidia situation is that Jensen Huang shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law, in what amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race. 

This is an unfathomable failure of enforcement by the Trump administration.

We urgently need to pass the bipartisan export control bills to start to cut off the flow of AI chips and manufacturing equipment to China once and for all, something I’ve worked on with @SenWarren and bipartisan partners for months.

title: the most popular personal AI agent for each state (my best guess)
title_en: the most popular personal AI agent for each state (my best guess)
title_zh: 每个州最受欢迎的个人人工智能代理（我的最佳猜测）
author: @DavidPawlan
summary_zh: 继本月早些时候 Meta 重磅发布 Muse AI 代理之后，OpenAI 于周二凭借 Dots 进军个人代理市场，为人工智能市场的下一场大战奠定了基础。在其年度 DevDay 开发者大会上，OpenAI 将 Dots 描述为“永远在线”
article_content:
Following Meta's blockbuster release of its Muse AI agent earlier this month, OpenAI jumped into the personal agent market on Tuesday with Dots, setting the stage for what could be the next big battle in the artificial intelligence market.

At its annual DevDay developer conference, OpenAI described Dots as "always-on"agents designed to help users complete a range of tasks. Since the release of Muse three weeks ago, investors have rallied around Meta, sending the stock up 29% in September, on pace for its best month since 2013.

That level of enthusiasm underscores the power of personal agents and the promise that consumers and office workers will be able to use the technology to book travel, pay bills, respond to emails and perform many more tasks. But OpenAI's entry, arriving soon after the launch of Muse, serves as a reminder that the AI market includes a handful of large companies all converging around the same types of products with little ability to lock in users.

Google calls its Gemini Spark offering "your 24/7 personal AI agent"for help, and Apple is trying to step up its position in the AI battle with its redesigned Siri AI, which it describes as "a profoundly more capable and personal assistant."

"I think what we are watching is an inevitable evolution of the technology,"said John Waldmann, CEO of HR tech startup Homebase and a user of various AI agent-related tools. "It's probably no surprise that it's all happening around the same time."

It's not just the big companies that see the opportunity.

AI assistant startup Instinct announced Monday that it raised $1 billion from venture firms including Sequoia at a $10 billion valuation. And another startup, Town, is reportedly looking at a $1 billion valuation.

Town CEO Jean-Denis Grèze told CNBC in a statement that OpenAI's debut of Dots, "continues to validate the category and the need for work assistants."

"It's been our focus at Town from the very beginning,"Grèze said, adding that he welcomes the competition.

On Tuesday, all eyes were on OpenAI, as investors and AI enthusiasts anticipated what the ChatGPT creator would unveil in the wake of last week's Meta Connect developer conference. There, Meta announced forthcoming AI devices, including a pendant, and CEO Mark Zuckerberg called Muse the "centerpiece"of the company's AI strategy.

Taking the stage in San Francisco for DevDay, Altman called Dots "remarkably capable"and "built to handle really anything you can think of."Although developers could already use OpenAI's existing tools to manage scores of AI agents for various office tasks, Dots promises to be an easier way for workers to use powerful digital assistants to help with tools like Slack and Microsoft Teams.

### More uplifting than AI safety

The rush of new agents hitting the market offers a more uplifting story for AI companies at a time when the leading labs are facing intensifying scrutiny due to emerging concerns that the most advanced models are at risk of spinning out of human control.

On Tuesday, as Altman was attending DevDay, his second-in-command, Greg Brockman, was in Washington for a lunch that President Donald Trump was hosting for top technology leaders. The topic was AI safety, and the event came more than two weeks after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei sent shock waves across the industry, writing an essay urging AI companies to slow the pace of frontier model development.

Nick Deveau, CEO of AI sales startup GrottoAI, is a fan of AI agent tools like Instinct and sees the vision as companies start building them for a wider audience.

"The interesting thing about all of these, which I think has become apparent really quickly and is evidenced by some of the valuations, is that people see this as the first successful proof point of true agentic work hitting consumers,"Deveau said.

There's still the question of whether consumers will pay. Meta's Muse is free with a usage limit and can be purchased starting at $20 a month after that. OpenAI's Dots is only available starting at the $100 per month Pro plan and higher.

And even with Muse racking up millions of downloads across app stores, that doesn't mean people are actively using it or other AI agents, Waldmann said.

"People will try it, but is it really adding value?"Waldmann said. "Is it part of a daily habit?"

Thomas Randall, a research director at the Info-Tech Research Group, said in an email that "the race is on,"as AI companies search to figure out how consumers want to use agents and what will keep them coming back.

"Once leading systems are broadly capable, the winner will likely be determined by which agent is the easiest to adopt, the most connected, and the hardest to leave,"Randall said. "We'll see who's distribution will gather steam first."

title_en:
Introducing M3 Code ✨

A T3 Code fork with ZERO telemetry.

NOTHING is being sent from this fork - no analytics, no product usage data, no error or crash reporting, no OpenTelemetry traces/metrics/logs, and no install, device, or account identifiers.

It will be updated DAILY to get latest commits from upstream T3 Code. It also includes some other unique features, specifically for local AI, but not just:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
 - Local providers marked, default for new threads

article_content:
AI-generated illustration Key Points Google now treats autonomous agents as a distinct security class requiring policy…View moreGoogle now treats autonomous agents as a distinct security class requiring policy checks and human confirmation.Third-party agent platforms face a compliance deadline as the Workspace AI Tools Addendum bans circumventing MCP.Agent Gateway enforces default-deny outbound rules and screens traffic for indirect prompt injection. Google announced on November 24, 2026 that its Workspace Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and Workspace command-line interface (CLI) are generally available, alongside rules requiring AI agents to use those interfaces instead of existing REST APIs. Technical enforcement begins February 1, 2027.

Google reports that Workspace APIs handle more than 2.8 trillion calls a month, with public Drive API traffic more than two-and-a-half times its 2022 volume. Traditional applications can continue using existing REST APIs; the new requirement applies to AI agents and other AI-driven tools.

Google’s rationale is that traditional REST APIs were built for human-paced applications, where a valid OAuth token implied user intent. An autonomous agent acting at machine speed across email, documents and cloud infrastructure changes that assumption. The new design puts policy checks, data boundaries and human confirmation into the request path.

The Workspace servers use MCP to give AI applications a standard way to read data and take actions. Dedicated remote servers are generally available for Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Chat and Tasks, inheriting each user’s permissions and data-governance controls. The Workspace CLI serves local agents, terminal workflows and automation, with structured JSON output and scoped OAuth sign-in across Workspace services.

Each agent call through these interfaces is checked against organizational permissions, data-loss-prevention rules and classification labels. The MCP servers reject OAuth clients that are not designated for AI agents, and agents connecting to Workspace must use dedicated OAuth client IDs with least-privilege scopes and usage quotas. Billing is scheduled to begin on April 1, 2027, while time-limited approvals are listed as coming soon.

Draft creation and document summarization can run autonomously. Sending email, changing Drive sharing permissions and making bulk edits require explicit user confirmation. Workspace administrators can view, audit and revoke agents in the admin console; user-facing activity review and revocation, plus controls to block agent access to Gmail messages and specific Drive files or folders, remain forthcoming.

The Workspace AI Tools Addendum covers standalone agents, the software harnesses that deploy or orchestrate them, and applications or services using AI models. It bars disguising a tool to avoid classification or circumvent the Google MCP requirement. That makes the migration a compliance issue for third-party agent platforms as well as for developers building directly on Workspace.

Workspace user data and Google Technical Information, a category of service information obtained or derived through Workspace access points, may be processed only to fulfill active, user-authorized tasks. Neither category can be used for model training, fine-tuning, evaluation dataset construction, model distillation or developing a service similar to a Workspace service. Scraping and systematic probing beyond what an authorized task requires are also prohibited.

Google Technical Information cannot be stored for more than 30 days. Covered user data and technical information must not be retained after a tool is disconnected or its access is revoked. If Google reasonably believes those rules have been violated, it can immediately restrict or remove the tool’s access, or suspend or terminate the customer’s access to the relevant Workspace services.

On Google Cloud, Agent Gateway verifies Agent Identities against the Agent Registry directory, enforces identity and access management policies and default-deny outbound rules, and screens requests with Model Armor. It governs inbound client-to-agent traffic and outbound requests from agents to tools, APIs and other agents. Custom authorization checks can be delegated to an organization’s own policy engine or third-party security tools through Service Extensions.

Cloud Run support and Agent Gateway for cross-cloud Kubernetes environments remain in Limited Preview. Each gateway instance can govern up to 5,000 resources registered in Agent Registry.

Google’s MCP configuration guide requires screening prompts and responses for indirect prompt injection, meaning hidden instructions in untrusted content, using Model Armor or a documented alternative. Malicious emails or documents could hijack a session and modify, steal or delete data. Current known issues include some English-only approval prompts, no user self-service viewing or revocation of saved tool approvals, and expiration of those approvals after 90 days.

For enterprises, agent governance is now built into the supported Workspace access path. The practical burden is the migration: existing agent integrations must satisfy the new identity, confirmation, screening and retention rules on Google’s schedule, while parts of the user-control and deployment model remain pending.

article_content_zh:
谷歌通过Agent Gateway重新定义了企业工作区的数据交互权限。传统的REST API在处理人类行为时具备有效的OAuth令牌保障，但面对高速、自动化的AI代理时，其安全边界显得极为脆弱。新的MCP接口直接在请求路径上集成了DLP审查和人工确认流程。

该协议将Gmail、Drive、Docs、Sheets等服务封装为受控节点。AI代理在调用这些服务时，必须使用专用的OAuth客户端ID，且在执行敏感操作（如发送邮件、修改Drive权限、批量编辑文档）时，必须获得用户明确确认。此举实际上将第三方代理彻底纳入了谷歌云的安全合规监控网格内。

ai_analysis.briefing_en: Google announced the general availability of Workspace MCP servers and CLI on November 24, 2026, mandating that AI agents use these interfaces for interaction. Effective February 1, 2027, this shift forces agents to operate through an Agent Gateway with built-in DLP and audit capabilities, treating agents as a distinct security classification.

title: China is the greatest economic and strategic threat facing the United States. For decades, China has engaged in intellectual property theft and espionage to acquire America’s most advanced technology. America must win the race to dominate AI and allegatio
title_en:
China is the greatest economic and strategic threat facing the United States. For decades, China has engaged in intellectual property theft and espionage to acquire America’s most advanced technology. 

America must win the race to dominate AI and allegations that Nvidia engaged in the sale of our most sensitive semiconductors to companies that were transferring that technology to China is totally unacceptable and should be deeply concerning to every American.

Jensen Huang had to go and should’ve stayed gone but now that the Nvidia board and the Trump administration have signed off on reinstating Huang as CEO, it is absolutely essential that Congress get to the bottom of how and why Jensen Huang and Nvidia were able to transfer our most advanced semiconductor technology to companies doing business with China. 

Last year, Jensen Huang said that those of us who are often described as “China hawks” wore “a badge of shame,” and added “they think they are doing the right thing for our country, but it's not patriotic, not even a little bit." 

With all due respect to the many dedicated employees and investors in Nvidia, patriotism means standing up for America against the machinations of authoritarian regimes and enduring shame awaits those who put personal and business interests above the national security and economic prosperity of the United States. 

Time for Congress To Get Work: get the American people the facts and enact strong new chip export controls to further restrict the sale or transfer of advanced semiconductors to China without delay.🇺🇸

author: @Mike_Pence
summary_zh:
国人的深切关注。

黄仁勋必须离开，也应该离开，但现在英伟达董事会和特朗普政府已经同意恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官，国会必须弄清楚黄仁勋和英伟达如何以及为何能够将我们最先进的半导体技术转让给与中国开展业务的公司。

去年，黄仁勋表示，我们这些经常被称为“对华鹰派”的人戴着“耻辱的徽章”，并补充说“他们认为自己为我们的国家做了正确的事情，但这不是爱国，甚至没有一点爱国。”

谨向英伟达众多敬业的员工和投资者致以应有的敬意，爱国主义意味着支持美国反对独裁政权的阴谋，而那些将个人和商业利益置于美国国家安全和经济繁荣之上的人将面临持久的耻辱。

国会该开始工作了：让美国人民了解事实，并制定强有力的新芯片出口管制措施，立即进一步限制先进半导体向中国的销售或转让。🇺🇸

title: The future is custom models for maximum performance, cost and ownership thanks to open-source! Last week, we released Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted (that became second most trending on HF) and a bunch of harness-adapted models that drastically improve
title_en:
The future is custom models for maximum performance, cost and ownership thanks to open-source!

Last week, we released Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted (that became second most trending on HF) and a bunch of harness-adapted models that drastically improve performance and cost. 

This week, we're releasing the fully reusable recipe, so you can reproduce this on your own task, harness, and model combinations.

Blogpost: https://huggingface.co/blog/harness-adapters-at-scale

Let's go open-source AI!
title_zh:
未来是通过开源实现最大性能、成本和所有权的定制模型！

title_en:
Today we are open-sourcing the weights to OCRia-1, our flagship 4B VLM for document OCR 🔥

This is our SECOND open-weight release in two days (we just launched OCRia-nano-1 yesterday!!).

OCRia-1 is on the pareto curve of accuracy and cost relative to other 4B models on multiple benchmarks: ParseBench, olmOCR-bench (tables), PulseBench-Tab, and fr-bench-pdf2md. It is an extremely general purpose model that can parse even the most complex document types, including complex tables/charts/formatting/layout.

We’re releasing the weights to help advance open research around OCR, on both @huggingface  🤗 and @ollama  🦙

If you want to use it in prod, come talk to us. If you want to use the latest SOTA of the OCRia model family, tuned for production, check out LlamaParse!

Release on @huggingface : https://huggingface.co/llamaindex/OCRia-1

Release on @ollama: https://ollama.com/llamaindex/ocria-1

LlamaParse: https://llamaparse.ai/

title: Quick clarification on what is/isn't blocked to Megaspeed given its Entity Listing did not include the FDPR, because I've received a number of questions about this and it admittedly gets a little complicated. As I noted in my post yesterday, advanced AI chips were
title_en:
Quick clarification on what is/isn't blocked to Megaspeed given its Entity Listing did not include the FDPR, because I've received a number of questions about this and it admittedly gets a little complicated. 

As I noted in my post yesterday, advanced AI chips were already blocked to Megaspeed before this Entity Listing due to the separate, country-wide controls for those chips that Commerce placed on Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia, and Brazil last week. The Megaspeed Entity Listing actually does double-capture these chips, because the new export control rule issued on Monday also modifies U.S. regulations so that the most advanced chips are blocked to any company on the Entity List even if the FDPR is not applied. So those chips are now double-blocked to Megaspeed; the Entity Listing changes nothing on that front. 

However, without the FDPR, a ton of very important AI chips and components made in Taiwan or Korea (with U.S. technology) remain legal to ship to Megaspeed. This includes less advanced AI chips, such as the Nvidia H20 chips (which require a license to ship to China). It includes high-bandwidth memory (which China cannot make at scale and needs to make its own AI chips, and is banned for export to China but is being smuggled into China in large quantities). And it includes networking equipment, server chips, and other items that Megaspeed needs to use the AI chips it already has. 

Now that we know Megaspeed is a Chinese shell company, there is no reason to let Megaspeed continue to legally purchase any AI chips and components that it would either smuggle back to China or use to sustain its data centers in Malaysia. This is exactly why the United States has historically applied the FDPR to all companies it has placed on the Entity List that deal with AI chips, which completely cuts them off from all chips and key chip components made outside the United States (this is also just logical because the Entity Listing bans them from receiving all such goods made INSIDE the United States). But because Megaspeed's listing does not include the FDPR, all of these items remain legal to ship to Megaspeed. 

The fact that Megaspeed, a known Chinese shell company engaged in a massive smuggling operation, is not totally cut off from all AI chips and high-bandwidth memory—which cannot be shipped to China without a license and are known to be smuggled in large quantities—is absurd. 

And one last point on another issue with the package, which I didn't make in my previous post: the listing also does not include any of the China-based nodes of the Alice Huang smuggling network, such as Shanghai Century Litong, which have been identified by multiple news outlets (The Information, NYT, WSJ). Those should obviously be added too, why were they not included? 

By the way, Nvidia's website STILL lists both Megaspeed and Shanghai Century Litong as official "cloud partners."

鉴于其实体列表不包括 FDPR，快速澄清一下 Megaspeed 被阻止/未被阻止的内容，因为我收到了许多与此相关的问题，而且无可否认，它变得有点复杂。

summary_zh:
对这些芯片实施了单独的全国范围内的控制，在此次实体上市之前，先进的人工智能芯片已经被 Megaspeed 屏蔽。 Megaspeed实体清单实际上确实双重捕获了这些芯片，因为周一发布的新出口管制规则还修改了美国法规，使得即使不适用FDPR，实体清单上的任何公司也将无法获得最先进的芯片。因此，这些芯片现在已双阻塞至 Megaspeed；实体清单在这方面没有任何改变。

然而，如果没有 FDPR，台湾或韩国制造的大量非常重要的人工智能芯片和组件（采用美国技术）仍然可以合法运送到 Megaspeed。这包括不太先进的人工智能芯片，例如 Nvidia H20 芯片（需要获得向中国发货的许可证）。其中包括高带宽存储器（中国无法大规模生产，需要制造自己的人工智能芯片，并且被禁止向中国出口，但正在大量走私到中国）。其中包括网络设备、服务器芯片以及 Megaspeed 使用其已有的人工智能芯片所需的其他物品。

既然我们知道 Megaspeed 是一家中国空壳公司，那么就没有理由让 Megaspeed 继续合法购买任何人工智能芯片和组件，这些芯片和组件要么走私回中国，要么用于维持其在马来西亚的数据中心。这正是美国历史上将 FDPR 应用于其列入实体清单的所有处理 AI 芯片的公司的原因，这完全切断了它们与美国境外制造的所有芯片和关键芯片组件的联系（这也是合乎逻辑的，因为实体清单禁止它们接收所有在美国境内制造的此类商品）。但由于 Megaspeed 的清单不包括 FDPR，因此所有这些物品仍然可以合法运送到 Megaspeed。

Megaspeed是一家从事大规模走私活动的知名中国空壳公司，它并没有完全切断所有人工智能芯片和高带宽内存的供应——这些芯片和高带宽内存没有许可证就不能运往中国，而且众所周知是大量走私的——这一事实是荒谬的。

关于该包裹的另一个问题的最后一点，我在上一篇文章中没有提及：该清单也不包括 Alice Huang 走私网络的任何中国节点，例如上海世纪利通，这些节点已被多家新闻媒体（《信息报》、《纽约时报》、《华尔街日报》）确认。这些显然也应该添加，为什么没有包括在内？

顺便说一下，Nvidia 的网站仍然将 Megaspeed 和上海世纪力通列为官方“云合作伙伴”。

full_text_en:
Quick clarification on what is/isn't blocked to Megaspeed given its Entity Listing did not include the FDPR, because I've received a number of questions about this and it admittedly gets a little complicated. 

As I noted in my post yesterday, advanced AI chips were already blocked to Megaspeed before this Entity Listing due to the separate, country-wide controls for those chips that Commerce placed on Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia, and Brazil last week. The Megaspeed Entity Listing actually does double-capture these chips, because the new export control rule issued on Monday also modifies U.S. regulations so that the most advanced chips are blocked to any company on the Entity List even if the FDPR is not applied. So those chips are now double-blocked to Megaspeed; the Entity Listing changes nothing on that front. 

However, without the FDPR, a ton of very important AI chips and components made in Taiwan or Korea (with U.S. technology) remain legal to ship to Megaspeed. This includes less advanced AI chips, such as the Nvidia H20 chips (which require a license to ship to China). It includes high-bandwidth memory (which China cannot make at scale and needs to make its own AI chips, and is banned for export to China but is being smuggled into China in large quantities). And it includes networking equipment, server chips, and other items that Megaspeed needs to use the AI chips it already has. 

Now that we know Megaspeed is a Chinese shell company, there is no reason to let Megaspeed continue to legally purchase any AI chips and components that it would either smuggle back to China or use to sustain its data centers in Malaysia. This is exactly why the United States has historically applied the FDPR to all companies it has placed on the Entity List that deal with AI chips, which completely cuts them off from all chips and key chip components made outside the United States (this is also just logical because the Entity Listing bans them from receiving all such goods made INSIDE the United States). But because Megaspeed's listing does not include the FDPR, all of these items remain legal to ship to Megaspeed. 

The fact that Megaspeed, a known Chinese shell company engaged in a massive smuggling operation, is not totally cut off from all AI chips and high-bandwidth memory—which cannot be shipped to China without a license and are known to be smuggled in large quantities—is absurd. 

And one last point on another issue with the package, which I didn't make in my previous post: the listing also does not include any of the China-based nodes of the Alice Huang smuggling network, such as Shanghai Century Litong, which have been identified by multiple news outlets (The Information, NYT, WSJ). Those should obviously be added too, why were they not included? 

By the way, Nvidia's website STILL lists both Megaspeed and Shanghai Century Litong as official "cloud partners."

title: Some personal updates: I'll join Princeton University as an Associate Professor in the Department of Computer Science in Fall 2027. I'm moving my Robot Perception and Learning Lab to @PrincetonCS, along with my students. And yes, I'm recruiting new PhD
title_en:
Some personal updates:

I'll join Princeton University as an Associate Professor in the Department of Computer Science in Fall 2027. I'm moving my Robot Perception and Learning Lab to @PrincetonCS, along with my students. And yes, I'm recruiting new PhD students and postdocs this cycle!

I'm deeply grateful to my students, colleagues, and collaborators at UT Austin, who have made it a memorable chapter of my life. UT is a great place to build a research career, with tremendous resources, excellent students, and a warmhearted community. I also feel fortunate to have called Austin home for the past six years, as I have witnessed its growth into one of America's most vibrant tech hubs.

Alongside this transition, I'll continue to co-lead the NVIDIA GEAR team, where we push the frontier of general-purpose robot autonomy. I also look forward to connecting with the growing robotics industry on the East Coast and finding new collaboration opportunities.

Needless to say, this move comes at a challenging time for academia.

Rapid AI advances are fundamentally reshaping how knowledge is created, disseminated, and applied. Universities must rethink their roles in a world where frontier AI systems can perform tasks once requiring years of specialized training. Yet, I believe these challenges present universities with a greater mission: to prepare younger generations for the post-AGI era and cultivate human character, values, taste, judgment, and a sense of purpose. The pursuit of truth, driven by intellectual curiosity and academic freedom, remains at the heart of universities.

On the research side, I've seen firsthand how frontier AI development is becoming increasingly resource-intensive and concentrated in well-funded industrial labs (including GEAR itself). At the same time, academia has an enduring responsibility to seek fundamental understanding, ask hard questions whose answers have no immediate commercial payoffs, and advance knowledge for the benefit of humanity and the betterment of society.

I chose Princeton because of its deep commitment to fundamental research and education. I see it as an extraordinary place to tackle these challenges and explore new opportunities. Together with the Princeton community, I hope to help shape the future of higher education.

I'm excited for this next chapter and everything ahead!
title_zh: 学术人才动态：Yuke Zhu教授将入职普林斯顿
author: @yukez
full_text_zh:
一些个人更新：

我将于 2027 年秋季加入普林斯顿大学，担任计算机科学系副教授。我将与我的学生一起将我的机器人感知和学习实验室移至 @PrincetonCS。是的，我这个周期正在招募新的博士生和博士后！

我深深感谢我在德州大学奥斯汀分校的学生、同事和合作者，他们让我的人生成为难忘的篇章。德克萨斯大学是建立研究事业的好地方，拥有丰富的资源、优秀的学生和热情的社区。我也很幸运在过去六年里把奥斯汀称为自己的家，因为我见证了它成长为美国最具活力的科技中心之一。

在这一转变的同时，我将继续共同领导 NVIDIA GEAR 团队，推动通用机器人自主的前沿发展。我也期待与东海岸不断发展的机器人行业建立联系，并寻找新的合作机会。

不用说，此举正值学术界面临挑战的时期。

人工智能的快速发展正在从根本上重塑知识的创造、传播和应用方式。在前沿人工智能系统可以执行曾经需要多年专业培训的任务的世界中，大学必须重新思考自己的角色。然而，我相信这些挑战给大学带来了更伟大的使命：让年轻一代为后通用人工智能时代做好准备，培养人的性格、价值观、品味、判断力和使命感。在求知欲和学术自由的驱动下对真理的追求仍然是大学的核心。

在研究方面，我亲眼目睹了前沿人工智能开发如何变得越来越资源密集型，并集中在资金充足的工业实验室（包括 GEAR 本身）。与此同时，学术界负有持久的责任，寻求基本的理解，提出其答案不会立即产生商业回报的难题，并为了人类的利益和社会的进步而推进知识的发展。

我选择普林斯顿大学是因为它致力于基础研究和教育。我认为这是应对这些挑战和探索新机遇的非凡场所。我希望与普林斯顿社区一起帮助塑造高等教育的未来。

我对下一章和未来的一切感到兴奋！
full_text_en:
Some personal updates:

I'll join Princeton University as an Associate Professor in the Department of Computer Science in Fall 2027. I'm moving my Robot Perception and Learning Lab to @PrincetonCS, along with my students. And yes, I'm recruiting new PhD students and postdocs this cycle!

I'm deeply grateful to my students, colleagues, and collaborators at UT Austin, who have made it a memorable chapter of my life. UT is a great place to build a research career, with tremendous resources, excellent students, and a warmhearted community. I also feel fortunate to have called Austin home for the past six years, as I have witnessed its growth into one of America's most vibrant tech hubs.

Alongside this transition, I'll continue to co-lead the NVIDIA GEAR team, where we push the frontier of general-purpose robot autonomy. I also look forward to connecting with the growing robotics industry on the East Coast and finding new collaboration opportunities.

Needless to say, this move comes at a challenging time for academia.

Rapid AI advances are fundamentally reshaping how knowledge is created, disseminated, and applied. Universities must rethink their roles in a world where frontier AI systems can perform tasks once requiring years of specialized training. Yet, I believe these challenges present universities with a greater mission: to prepare younger generations for the post-AGI era and cultivate human character, values, taste, judgment, and a sense of purpose. The pursuit of truth, driven by intellectual curiosity and academic freedom, remains at the heart of universities.

On the research side, I've seen firsthand how frontier AI development is becoming increasingly resource-intensive and concentrated in well-funded industrial labs (including GEAR itself). At the same time, academia has an enduring responsibility to seek fundamental understanding, ask hard questions whose answers have no immediate commercial payoffs, and advance knowledge for the benefit of humanity and the betterment of society.

I chose Princeton because of its deep commitment to fundamental research and education. I see it as an extraordinary place to tackle these challenges and explore new opportunities. Together with the Princeton community, I hope to help shape the future of higher education.

I'm excited for this next chapter and everything ahead!

title: 一代人正在变得丰富。验证是更难的问题。 SenseNova U1.6引入了原生视觉自我校正：它生成信息图，根据原始提示检查渲染的文本，并在不丢弃周围环境的情况下修改错误。
title_en:
Generation is becoming abundant. 

Verification is the harder problem. 

SenseNova U1.6 introduces native visual self-correction: it generates an infographic, checks the rendered text against the original prompt, and revises errors without discarding the surrounding typography or layout. 

That shift from one-shot output to iterative visual reasoning is the part I find most interesting. 

Built on Neo-unify, with native ComfyUI support. 

Source: https://github.com/OpenSenseNova/SenseNova-U1

title: I made a video editor that lets you cut by hand or with AI agents. It's called Editroom. https://t.co/RK0gcM1pYa It's 100% free and open source. I built it for myself since I found iMovie unusable, Resolve too complicated, and Premiere too heavy. the app includes:
title_en:
I made a video editor that lets you cut by hand or with AI agents. It's called Editroom.
http://robbietilton.com/editroom

It's 100% free and open source. I built it for myself since I found iMovie unusable, Resolve too complicated, and Premiere too heavy.

the app includes:
• Color grading + LUTs, with HDR and Log support
• Speed ramps, transitions and fades
• Auto captions, timed word by word
• Search footage by what's said or what's in the shot
• AI editing: on-device, or with Claude and ChatGPT
• Built-in MCP server

Editroom is 23 MB. Premiere is 6.95 GB, Resolve 6.34 GB, and iMovie 4.29 GB

title_en: Had the pleasure of having a conversation with the Honorable PM Shri Narendra Modi Ji. I am consistently amazed by his grasp of technology and his clarity of vision on how he sees the optimistic side of it. The boundless possibilities of AI and how it is likely to benefit the masses. Be it education, healthcare or ensuring that friction can be removed for doing business in India. He was of course keen to understand how it can be diffused safely and securely and what dangers it poses in the hands of bad actors. Both @PaloAltoNtwks and I look forward to contributing positively to his vision.

title_en:
Every developer using Claude Code makes the same mistake first.

They jump straight into coding.
No plan.
No context file.
No rules defined.
No tests written first.

Just: "Write me a function that does X."

Then 2 hours of refactoring
what Claude built
without understanding
what you actually needed.

That’s not a Claude problem.
That’s a workflow problem.

Here’s the workflow that fixes it 

The prompt that changes everything:
"Explain how you'd solve X. No code yet."

Three words - No code yet -
force Claude into planning mode.

Review the plan. Refine it.
THEN execute.

Every hour spent planning
saves 3 hours of refactoring.

Every Claude Code power user knows this.
Almost nobody does it on day one.

The other 7 rules that compound on top:

📌 CLAUDE.md → your rules, every session, automatically
📌 TDD → failing test first, implementation second
📌 Subagents → parallel tasks, not sequential bottlenecks
📌 Git Worktrees → one feature, one environment, zero conflicts
📌 /compact → clean context, consistent quality
📌 /cost → visible spend, no surprise bills
📌 Skills → standardized workflows, consistent team output

8 rules. All learnable in one afternoon.
All changing your output permanently.

Which rule do you wish you'd learned on day one?

你真正需要什么。

这不是克劳德的问题。
这是一个工作流程问题。

这是修复它的工作流程

改变一切的提示：
“解释一下你将如何解决 X。还没有代码。”

三个字 - 还没有代码 -
迫使克劳德进入计划模式。

审查计划。精炼它。
然后执行。

花在计划上的每一个小时
节省 3 小时的重构时间。

每个 Claude Code 高级用户都知道这一点。
几乎没有人在第一天就这样做。

其他 7 条规则综合在一起：

📌 CLAUDE.md → 您的规则，每次会话，自动
📌 TDD → 首先测试失败，其次实施
📌 子代理 → 并行任务，而不是顺序瓶颈
📌 Git Worktrees → 一种功能，一种环境，零冲突
📌 /compact → 干净的环境，一致的质量
📌 /cost → 看得见的支出，没有意外的账单
📌 技能 → 标准化工作流程、一致的团队产出

8 条规则。一下午就能全部学会。
所有这些都会永久改变你的输出。

title: A model's value isn't just defined by its capabilities. Its ecosystem matters too. I was glad to hear that Hy4 and Hy4 flash are already being used across tools like OpenCode, Claude Code, and Cline. The team also mentioned ongoing efforts around llama.cpp c
title_en:
A model's value isn't just defined by its capabilities. Its ecosystem matters too.

I was glad to hear that Hy4 and Hy4 flash are already being used across tools like OpenCode, Claude Code, and Cline.

The team also mentioned ongoing efforts around llama.cpp compatibility and collaboration with communities such as vLLM and SGL.

For developers, better compatibility and integration can make a real difference. It's great to see the Hy team putting effort into the ecosystem, not just the models themselves.

title: 有人为 Snapp 游乐设施构建了一个非官方的 MCP 服务器。它可以在一个未记录的 API 上运行，包括实时驱动程序和所有内容，但随时可能会崩溃。我以另一种方式构建了 TADA 和 Throo。特意开，0%佣金，任何代理都可以叫真司机。尝试一下。告诉我什么
title_en: Someone built an unofficial MCP server for Snapp rides. It works, live driver and all, on an undocumented API that can break any day. I built TADA and Throo the other way. Open on purpose, 0% commission, any agent can call a real driver. Try it. Tell me what
title_zh: 开发者构建Snapp非官方MCP服务器
full_text_zh: 有人为 Snapp 游乐设施构建了一个非官方的 MCP 服务器。它可以在一个未记录的 API 上运行，包括实时驱动程序和所有内容，但随时可能会崩溃。我以另一种方式构建了 TADA 和 Throo。特意开，0%佣金，任何代理都可以叫真司机。尝试一下。告诉我什么
full_text_en: Someone built an unofficial MCP server for Snapp rides. It works, live driver and all, on an undocumented API that can break any day. I built TADA and Throo the other way. Open on purpose, 0% commission, any agent can call a real driver. Try it. Tell me what
summary_zh: 独立开发者通过逆向未记录的API接口，为Snapp平台构建了非官方MCP服务器以实现实时调度。
summary_en: An independent developer has built an unofficial MCP server for the Snapp platform by leveraging undocumented APIs to enable real-time driver access. While this integration facilitates third-party control over logistics, it faces significant stability risks and potential termination due to the lack of official API support.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 独立开发者利用Snapp平台未公开的底层API，开发了旨在接入Model Context Protocol（MCP）的第三方中间件。该实现通过抓取实时驱动程序数据进行交互，旨在打破封闭生态的调度限制，但因缺乏官方兼容性保障，存在极高的运行稳定性风险与接口封禁隐患。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: An independent developer has built an unofficial MCP server for the Snapp platform by leveraging undocumented APIs to enable real-time driver access. While this integration facilitates third-party control over logistics, it faces significant stability risks and potential termination due to the lack of official API support.

elements_zh.where: Snapp平台物流调度生态
elements_zh.what: 通过逆向未记录API实现非官方MCP接入与自定义调度逻辑
elements_zh.why: 寻求绕过官方平台限制实现更灵活的代理调度与零佣金机制

elements_en.what: Built unofficial MCP server using undocumented APIs for real-time driver control
elements_en.why: Attempting to circumvent platform commission and access proprietary scheduling workflows

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此举揭示了基于AI Agent的MCP协议在物流垂直领域的渗透尝试，但通过逆向手段构建的核心组件难以进入生产环境。这种非授权的接口集成不仅面临法律合规的灰度挑战，更预示着平台方需进一步加固API鉴权以防御私自接入带来的安全漏洞。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This development highlights the push to integrate MCP into logistics, yet unofficial reverse-engineered integrations are structurally unfit for production. Platform owners must prioritize API security and authentication hardening to mitigate the risks associated with unauthorized agentic access.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 独立开发者利用Snapp平台未公开的底层API，开发了旨在接入Model Context Protocol（MCP）的第三方中间件。该实现通过抓取实时驱动程序数据进行交互，旨在打破封闭生态的调度限制，但因缺乏官方兼容性保障，存在极高的运行稳定性风险与接口封禁隐患。

While this integration facilitates third-party control over logistics, it faces significant stability risks and potential termination due to the lack of official API support.
key_points_zh: 核心动机：通过避开平台佣金实现代理自主调度
关键技术：基于未记录的Snapp API实现数据透传与驱动交互
行业风险：API变动会导致系统崩溃且存在违规调用风险
key_points_en: Motivation: Circumventing platform commissions for autonomous logistics
Technical detail: Leveraging undocumented APIs to bypass standard driver dispatch
Risk factors: High technical volatility and potential for permanent platform-side blocking

Platform owners must prioritize API security and authentication hardening to mitigate the risks associated with unauthorized agentic access.

title: 一个印度平台起诉 OpenAI，其请求被驳回，并锁定了其登录后的列表。 🔍🛅 独特业务查询下降了 14%。竞争对手却做了相反的事情：建立了一个 MCP 服务器，以便人工智能代理可以查询其数据。独立访客数量反弹 1600 万。 🔎 信息E
title_en:
One Indian platform sued OpenAI, had its plea dismissed, and locked its listings behind logins. 🔍🛅
Unique business queries fell 14%.

A rival did the opposite: built an MCP server so AI agents can query its data. Unique visitors rebounded by 16 million. 🔎

InfoEdge, IndiaMART, and Justdial stocks are down 30–40%. The zero-click era is sorting walled gardens from AI-readable networks.

Why India’s internet intermediaries are at an inflection point (Google search growth slowed from 17% → 12% while ChatGPT Ads hit a $1B annualised run rate in 200 days):

• The Walled-Garden Trap.
IndiaMART locked listings after Calcutta HC dismissed its case against OpenAI. Unique business queries dropped to 27M in the September quarter. Now pivoting to credit facilities and verified buyer subscriptions.

• The AI-Native Rebound.
Justdial added an MCP server in August so AI engines can pull listings and route leads back. Quarterly unique visitors rose from a 7-quarter low of 182.4M (March) to 198.4M (September).

• Forced Product Pivots.
At InfoEdge, Shiksha annual visits crashed from 450M+ to 200M+ (Q2FY27 billings −27.2% YoY to ₹20 crore). Response: AI voice counselling on Shiksha + an agentic AI recruitment suite on Naukri, with InfoEdge’s AI-first offerings already at a ₹240-crore annual run rate.

• The Global Warning
Chegg lost 99% of its market value ($14.7B → $116M) as AI search simply bypassed its static funnel.

Platforms that were just thin wrappers over public information are becoming ghost sites.

Winning the zero-click era requires verified supply, live transaction trust, and infrastructure built for AI agents to discover, not fight.
@IndiaMART @jd_justdial @OpenAI @sbikh

By @HimanshiET @SurabhiA_ET
#AI #ZeroClick #IndianTech #DigitalEconomy

full_text_zh:
一个印度平台起诉 OpenAI，其请求被驳回，并锁定了其登录后的列表。 🔍🛅
独特的业务查询下降了 14%。

竞争对手却做了相反的事情：建立了一个 MCP 服务器，以便人工智能代理可以查询其数据。独立访客数量反弹 1600 万。 🔎

InfoEdge、IndiaMART 和 Justdial 的股票下跌了 30-40%。零点击时代正在将围墙花园与人工智能可读的网络进行分类。

为什么印度的互联网中介机构正处于拐点（Google 搜索增长从 17% 放缓至 12%，而 ChatGPT 广告在 200 天内达到了 10 亿美元的年化运行率）：

• 围墙花园陷阱。
在加尔各答 HC 驳回针对 OpenAI 的案件后，IndiaMART 锁定了商品列表。 9 月份季度的独特业务查询量下降至 2700 万。现在转向信贷便利和经过验证的买家订阅。

• AI 原生反弹。
Justdial 在 8 月份添加了 MCP 服务器，以便人工智能引擎可以提取列表并路由线索。季度独立访客数量从 7 季度低点 1.824 亿（3 月）上升至 1.984 亿（9 月）。

• 强制产品转向。
在 InfoEdge，Shiksha 的年访问量从 4.5 亿+骤降到 2 亿+（2027 财年第 2 季度的账单同比下降 -27.2% 至 2 亿卢比）。回应：Shiksha 上的人工智能语音咨询 + Naukri 上的代理人工智能招聘套件，InfoEdge 的人工智能优先产品的年运行率已达 24 亿卢比。

• 全球警告
由于人工智能搜索简单地绕过了其静态漏斗，Chegg 损失了 99% 的市值 ($14.7B → $116M)。

那些只是公共信息薄薄包装的平台正在变成幽灵网站。

赢得零点击时代需要经过验证的供应、实时交易信任以及为人工智能代理构建的基础设施，以发现而不是战斗。
@IndiaMART @jd_justdial @OpenAI @sbikh

作者：@HimanshiET @SurabhiA_ET
#AI #ZeroClick #IndianTech #DigitalEconomy

title: No. Taxpayers will not Bailout Big Tech Oligarchs. In America today, we have an extremely volatile economy and a stock market that is increasingly dependent on the whims of a handful of Big Tech Oligarchs who have bet trillions of dollars on artificial intellige
title_en:
No. Taxpayers will not Bailout Big Tech Oligarchs.

In America today, we have an extremely volatile economy and a stock market that is increasingly dependent on the whims of a handful of Big Tech Oligarchs who have bet trillions of dollars on artificial intelligence.

One day, the stock price of Nvidia and other Big Tech companies plummet because a CEO had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy and was forced to resign. The next day, the stock price of these same companies goes way up once that same CEO is reinstated.

In other words, the fate of one man caused the stock market to lose and then regain trillions of dollars in value.

How crazy is that? And it’s not just Nvidia.

One day, the value of Anthropic, a company that has never made a profit and is deeply in debt, skyrockets to over $2 trillion. The next day, the value of that same company is cut by more than a quarter based on Wall Street fears that its massive debt will be rated as junk.

What will happen tomorrow? Nobody knows.

One thing must be made certain: If the AI bubble bursts, taxpayers will not bailout Big Tech Oligarchs. Not tomorrow. Not next year. Not ever.

If AI companies fail, Big Tech Oligarchs must bail them out, not taxpayers.

Our message to these multi-billionaires is simple: If you take out a loan, pay it back. Don’t come begging to taxpayers to bail you out.
title_zh: 伯尼·桑德斯反对援助科技巨头
author: @BernieSanders
full_text_zh:
不会。纳税人不会救助大型科技寡头。

在今天的美国，我们的经济极其不稳定，股市也越来越依赖于少数科技寡头的一时兴起，他们在人工智能上押注了数万亿美元。

有一天，英伟达和其他大型科技公司的股价暴跌，因为一位首席执行官与一名涉嫌中国间谍有染，并被迫辞职。第二天，一旦这位首席执行官复职，这些公司的股价就会大幅上涨。

换句话说，一个人的命运导致股市先跌后重，价值数万亿美元。

这有多疯狂？不仅仅是英伟达。

有一天，Anthropic 这家从未盈利且负债累累的公司的价值飙升至超过 2 万亿美元。第二天，由于华尔街担心该公司的巨额债务将被评级为垃圾级，该公司的价值被削减了四分之一以上。

明天会发生什么？没有人知道。

必须确定一件事：如果人工智能泡沫破裂，纳税人将不会救助大型科技寡头。不是明天。不是明年。从来没有。

如果人工智能公司失败，大型科技寡头必须救助它们，而不是纳税人。

我们向这些亿万富翁传达的信息很简单：如果您申请了贷款，请偿还。不要乞求纳税人来救助你。

ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 此表态反映了美国民粹主义监管派对AI巨头垄断及资本泡沫的深层忧虑，预示着未来若发生科技板块连锁崩盘，政府层面的“救市压力”将遭遇严重的政治阻力。地缘与监管博弈已将AI基础设施的超额支出视为一种潜在的系统性金融负担，而非仅仅是技术竞争资产。

title: The inference infrastructure fight is quietly becoming as crowded as the model fight, and almost nobody outside platform teams is watching it. NVIDIA's Dynamo, Red Hat and Google and IBM's llm-d, and agentgateway from the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Fo
title_en:
The inference infrastructure fight is quietly becoming as crowded as the model fight, and almost nobody outside platform teams is watching it. NVIDIA's Dynamo, Red Hat and Google and IBM's llm-d, and agentgateway from the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation are all converging on the same bet: that serving an LLM well means splitting prefill and decode across different hardware and offloading KV cache rather than treating inference as one monolithic request.

llm-d landed as a CNCF sandbox project, which tells you Kubernetes is where this gets decided, not inside a single vendor's stack. vLLM, Ray Serve and Triton already own a lot of that ground, so what Dynamo and llm-d are really arguing is that the orchestration layer underneath an agent matters as much as the model it calls. An agent that reasons well but waits on a poorly routed inference request is still a slow agent.

Open governance around inference serving is new territory. A year ago this layer was proprietary and vendor specific by default. Now three different coalitions are building it in the open at the same time, which usually means the market has decided this is infrastructure, not a product.

llm-d 作为 CNCF 沙盒项目落地，这告诉您 Kubernetes 是决定这一切的地方，而不是在单个供应商的堆栈中。 vLLM、Ray Serve 和 Triton 已经拥有了很多这样的基础，所以 Dynamo 和 llm-d 真正争论的是代理下面的编排层和它调用的模型一样重要。推理良好但等待路由不良的推理请求的代理仍然是一个缓慢的代理。

围绕推理服务的开放治理是一个新领域。一年前，该层默认是专有的且特定于供应商的。现在，三个不同的联盟正在同时公开建设它，这通常意味着市场已经决定这是基础设施，而不是产品。

title: Prompt vs Skill vs MCP vs Subagent. Confused about the difference? All four change what your agent can do. But knowing what each one costs your context matters more than the names. Here's the difference between them, using one task, writing this week's r
title_en:
Prompt vs Skill vs MCP vs Subagent.

Confused about the difference?

All four change what your agent can do. But knowing what each one costs your context matters more than the names.

Here's the difference between them, using one task, writing this week's release notes:

1. Prompt
You type the steps. "List merged PRs, group by feature, skip chores." The full text sits in the chat and gets sent again on every turn. Next week you type it all again.
Use it for one-off work.

2. Skill
You save the steps once in .claude/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md. At the start of a session the agent only sees the skill's name and description. When a task matches, the full body loads, along with any scripts in that folder. That's why 30 skills cost almost nothing until one is used. Once loaded, though, the body stays in context for the rest of the session, so keep it short.
Use it when you keep pasting the same steps.

3. MCP
An MCP server, set up in .mcp.json, gives the agent new tools, like reading merged PRs from GitHub and posting to Slack. With tool search on, which is the default in Claude Code, only the tool names load at the start. The full schemas load when the agent goes looking for them.
Use it when the work lives in another app.

4. Subagent
A subagent, defined in .claude/agents/release-notes.md, gets its own context window, its own system prompt and its own tool list. It reads all 200 PRs, and only its final summary comes back to your main chat. It still uses tokens, just not your main context.
Use it when a side task would flood your chat with output you won't read again.

They also stack. A release-notes skill can call the GitHub MCP tools and hand the long reading to a subagent, and your main chat only ever sees the 10-line result.

Which one is doing the most work in your setup right now?
title_zh: AI智能体构建中的四项核心要素成本拆解
author: @towards_AI
full_text_zh:
提示 vs 技能 vs MCP vs 子代理。

对差异感到困惑吗？

这四者都会改变你的代理人可以做什么。但了解每一项对你的背景造成的影响比名称更重要。

这是它们之间的区别，使用一项任务，编写本周的发行说明：

1. 提示
您键入步骤。 “列出合并的 PR，按功能分组，跳过杂务。”全文位于聊天中，每次都会再次发送。下周你再次输入所有内容。
将其用于一次性工作。

2. 技能
您可以在 .claude/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md 中保存一次这些步骤。在会话开始时，客服人员只能看到技能的名称和描述。当任务匹配时，会加载完整的正文以及该文件夹中的所有脚本。这就是为什么 30 种技能在使用其中一项之前几乎不需要花费任何成本。不过，一旦加载，正文将在会话的其余部分中保持在上下文中，因此请保持简短。
当您继续粘贴相同的步骤时使用它。

3.MCP
在 .mcp.json 中设置的 MCP 服务器为代理提供了新工具，例如从 GitHub 读取合并的 PR 并将其发布到 Slack。打开工具搜索（Claude Code 中的默认设置）后，只会在开始时加载工具名称。当代理寻找完整模式时，会加载完整模式。
当作品位于另一个应用程序中时使用它。

4. 分代理
在 .claude/agents/release-notes.md 中定义的子代理拥有自己的上下文窗口、自己的系统提示符和自己的工具列表。它会读取所有 200 个 PR，并且只有其最终摘要会返回到您的主聊天中。它仍然使用令牌，只是不是您的主要上下文。
当副任务会用你不会再阅读的输出淹没你的聊天时，请使用它。

他们也堆叠。发行说明技能可以调用 GitHub MCP 工具并将长阅读交给子代理，而您的主要聊天只能看到 10 行结果。

目前在您的设置中哪一个正在做最多的工作？
full_text_en:
Prompt vs Skill vs MCP vs Subagent.

Confused about the difference?

All four change what your agent can do. But knowing what each one costs your context matters more than the names.

Here's the difference between them, using one task, writing this week's release notes:

1. Prompt
You type the steps. "List merged PRs, group by feature, skip chores." The full text sits in the chat and gets sent again on every turn. Next week you type it all again.
Use it for one-off work.

2. Skill
You save the steps once in .claude/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md. At the start of a session the agent only sees the skill's name and description. When a task matches, the full body loads, along with any scripts in that folder. That's why 30 skills cost almost nothing until one is used. Once loaded, though, the body stays in context for the rest of the session, so keep it short.
Use it when you keep pasting the same steps.

3. MCP
An MCP server, set up in .mcp.json, gives the agent new tools, like reading merged PRs from GitHub and posting to Slack. With tool search on, which is the default in Claude Code, only the tool names load at the start. The full schemas load when the agent goes looking for them.
Use it when the work lives in another app.

4. Subagent
A subagent, defined in .claude/agents/release-notes.md, gets its own context window, its own system prompt and its own tool list. It reads all 200 PRs, and only its final summary comes back to your main chat. It still uses tokens, just not your main context.
Use it when a side task would flood your chat with output you won't read again.

They also stack. A release-notes skill can call the GitHub MCP tools and hand the long reading to a subagent, and your main chat only ever sees the 10-line result.

Which one is doing the most work in your setup right now?

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 该分析对AI智能体生态中的提示词（Prompt）、技能（Skill）、模型上下文协议（MCP）及子智能体（Subagent）进行技术拆解。核心指出各类组件在提升任务处理能力的同时，均以消耗上下文窗口容量为代价，需根据任务复杂度在模块化扩展与推理成本间进行精确权衡。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: This analysis breaks down the four core modules in AI agent architecture: Prompts, Skills, MCP, and Subagents. It highlights that while these components enhance task execution, they all consume precious context window resources, necessitating a precise trade-off between modular scalability and inference costs.

elements_zh.what: 分析四种功能模块对上下文窗口的消耗差异

elements_en.what: Evaluation of context consumption for four functional modules
elements_en.why: Optimizing agent inference efficiency and context management

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 智能体架构的本质是计算资源与语义精度的博弈，模型上下文协议（MCP）的引入将标准化接口数据，但在复杂任务链中，过度调用子智能体会导致显著的上下文污染与长文本损耗。开发者应优先将静态技能固化为工具函数，而非完全依赖长提示词注入，以维持高推理质量。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Agent architecture is fundamentally a trade-off between compute resources and semantic precision; while MCP standardizes interface data, excessive subagent invocation in complex chains leads to significant context degradation. Developers should prioritize encoding static skills as tool functions rather than relying on heavy prompt injection to maintain high inference quality.

title: We open-sourced a 3B-active translation model that beats models using over 30x its compute. Hy MT3 comes in 1.8B, 7B, and 30B-A3B sizes under Apache 2.0. We keep refining our models with community feedback, expanding coverage from 38 languages i
title_en:
We open-sourced a 3B-active translation model that beats models using over 30x its compute. Hy MT3 comes in 1.8B, 7B, and 30B-A3B sizes under Apache 2.0.

We keep refining our models with community feedback, expanding coverage from 38 languages in Hy MT2 to 102 in Hy MT3. On real-world data, the 30B-A3B model cuts omissions and additions by 74%, mistranslations by 43%, and instruction errors by 40%. It also keeps formatting, tags, and terminology intact, and handles OCR errors better in image translation.

All three sizes come with quantized builds for local and on-device use, alongside full weights for server deployment. Hy MT3 is also coming soon to our Chrome and Edge browser extension, which supports one-click local models for offline translation.

Repo: http://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-MT3
Weights: http://huggingface.co/collections/tencent/hy-mt3
Paper: http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27673
title_zh: 腾讯开源MT3系列模型，以低算力实现高性能翻译
author: @TencentAI_News
full_text_zh:
我们开源了一个 3B 主动翻译模型，该模型的计算能力比模型高出 30 倍。 Hy MT3 在 Apache 2.0 下有 1.8B、7B 和 30B-A3B 大小。

我们根据社区反馈不断完善我们的模型，将覆盖范围从 Hy MT2 中的 38 种语言扩大到 Hy MT3 中的 102 种语言。在实际数据上，30B-A3B 模型将遗漏和添加减少了 74%，误译减少了 43%，指令错误减少了 40%。它还保持格式、标签和术语完整，并更好地处理图像翻译中的 OCR 错误。

所有三种尺寸都带有用于本地和设备上使用的量化构建，以及用于服务器部署的完整权重。 Hy MT3 也即将在我们的 Chrome 和 Edge 浏览器扩展中推出，它支持一键本地模型进行离线翻译。

仓库：http://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-MT3
权重：http://huggingface.co/collections/tencent/hy-mt3
论文：http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27673
