title: GPT-6.2 Astra for research taste:
title_en: GPT-6.2 Astra for research taste:
title_zh: GPT-6.2 Astra 适合研究口味：
author: Greg Brockman
author_role: OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人
summary_zh: GPT-6.2 Astra 发布后，我看到评论表明一般基准测试的改进并不令人印象深刻。然而，对于旨在实现AGI或ASI的人工智能公司来说，真正重要的能力是什么？ 2026年11月24日，评估AI研发能力的P-Zero Research
article_content:
After the release of GPT-6.2 Astra, I saw comments suggesting that the improvements in general benchmarks were underwhelming. However, for AI companies aiming to achieve AGI or ASI, what are the truly important capabilities?

On November 24, 2026, P-Zero Research, which evaluates AI research and development capabilities, published some very interesting measurement results.

GPT-6.2 Astra's experimental research taste is 4.9 times that of the human experts who participated in the study. This is the highest figure measured among AI models to date. Anthropic's Fable 5.2 was 2.5 times.

What is noteworthy is that the capability being evaluated is not knowledge volume or coding ability, but Research Taste.

Is an excellent researcher someone with vast knowledge? Or is it someone who can process complex mathematical formulas at high speed? Of course, those are also important capabilities. However, in research that breaks new ground in unknown territories, a different set of skills is required.

Which problems are worth tackling? Which hypotheses are promising? What experiments will yield important information? And, what should be read from the experimental results, and what should be tried next?

P-Zero Research calls this ability Research Taste. Among these, the TasteVal benchmark was developed to measure the ability to design experiments and interpret results for given research tasks.

The metric used in this evaluation is the Compute Multiplier. It represents how much less computational resource is needed to achieve experimental results equivalent to those of a human expert.

Researcher Required GPU Time Human Expert 20 hours Fable 5.2 8 hours GPT-6.2 Astra approx. 4.1 hours

GPT-6.2 Astra is estimated to obtain equivalent results with about one-fifth of the experimental computational resources by efficiently selecting promising experiments.

However, this is not a comparison that includes the computational resources or costs required for the AI's own reasoning. Also, it does not mean that it has surpassed human intelligence in general by 4.9 times.

The evaluation method of TasteVal is very interesting. It separates the research and development process into two roles: Researcher and Coder.

The Researcher devises experiments and interprets the results. The Coder implements the code according to those instructions and executes the experiments on NVIDIA H100 GPUs. Then, the obtained results are reported to the Researcher. The Researcher devises the next experiment based on those results.

Both human researchers and AI models use a common Coder. In the original paper published in October 2026, Anthropic's Opus 4.8 was adopted as the Coder.

Eight types of tasks related to AI research and development were prepared for evaluation, including selection of pre-training data, language model training, fine-tuning, modeling of human preferences, and resistance to adversarial prompts.

From the human side, 24 experts with research experience at OpenAI, Google DeepMind, NVIDIA, Microsoft Research, the University of Oxford, and others participated. Moreover, the comparison benchmark is not the average of the participants, but the human expert who achieved the best results in each task.

Looking at the graph released this time, a change more interesting than the raw figures of GPT-6.2 Astra becomes apparent. Since the end of 2025, the rate of improvement in research taste has changed drastically.

In the original TasteVal paper published in October 2026, the following doubling periods were reported regarding the experimental research taste of state-of-the-art AI models.

Period Research Taste Doubling Period 2023–December 2025 Approx. 14 months After December 2025 Approx. 3 months

The vertical axis of the graph is on a logarithmic scale. In other words, what appears to be a linear rise actually represents exponential growth.

Of course, there is no guarantee that this trend will continue in the future. Furthermore, the paper does not confirm a similar acceleration for other metrics comparing final experimental results.

Nevertheless, the result that research capability to efficiently utilize computational resources is growing rapidly is something that cannot be overlooked when considering the future of AI.

In AI development to date, securing more GPUs and performing larger-scale computations has been a key means of improving performance. However, increasing GPUs requires semiconductor manufacturing, data center construction, power procurement, and enormous capital.

On the other hand, what if we could extract more research results from the same computational resources? It may be possible to accelerate research and development without increasing physical computational resources.

What can only be discovered after repeating experiments hundreds of times, a superior intelligence might discover in dozens of experiments. What is important is not just the ability to compute, but the ability to judge what should be computed.

In addition to scaling computational resources, the scaling of the intelligence that uses those computational resources has begun.

In AGI and ASI research, there is a concept called Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI).

AI participates in the research and development of the next generation of AI, and the superior AI created there researches and develops the next generation of AI. This is the idea that the evolution of AI itself accelerates through this cycle.

Improving coding ability alone is not enough to fully establish this cycle. Even if given instructions can be implemented perfectly, if the instructions themselves are not beneficial for research, computational resources will be wasted.

This is where the measured Research Taste becomes important. If AI evolves not only as an implementer but also as an entity responsible for experimental research decision-making, the structure of AI research and development itself may change.

In the original October 2026 paper, P-Zero Research also conducted simulations reflecting the measured upward trend in research taste in the AI Futures Model.

However, this is an extrapolation assuming a constant growth trend and is not a definitive prediction of when ASI will be reached. Furthermore, this simulation was conducted before the current measurement results of 4.9 times for GPT-6.2 Astra were announced.

Even so, it has been shown that the variable of 'research intuition' has a significant impact that cannot be ignored when considering the arrival time of superintelligence.

Here, I would also like to touch upon the limitations of TasteVal. In this benchmark, the research problems themselves are provided in advance. In other words, the ability to discover more fundamental questions—such as what should be researched in the first place—is not measured.

Additionally, the authors themselves acknowledge that the human experts used for comparison do not include the world's top-tier researchers. Since the focus is on experimental tasks where results can be verified in a relatively short period, caution is also needed regarding generalization to long-term basic research.

The ability to discover problems that humanity has not yet noticed and to open up entirely new academic fields—how far AI will acquire this remains to be seen in future research.

Today, I also wrote an article about Boaz Barak's essay 'Human empowerment in a few fake graphs,' which was highly praised by Sam Altman.

Barak presents a vision where, as AI intelligence improves, human capabilities for understanding, monitoring, and controlling AI are also expanded by AI. At the same time, he mentions the possibility that rapid intelligence gains through recursive self-improvement could outpace the expansion of human capabilities.

Immediately after that, I saw the measurement results regarding the research intuition of GPT-6.2 Astra. One side of the discussion is how humanity and rapidly evolving AI will coexist. The other is the measurement of the capabilities that could trigger that rapid evolution.

Reading these two together reveals why current AI safety research is facing such a critical juncture.

Every time a new AI model is announced, comparisons are made regarding capabilities we use daily, such as text generation, browser operation, and coding. Of course, this is an important evaluation for users.

However, if we are to consider the path to AGI and ASI, we must focus not only on what current AI can do, but also on what it can do to create the next generation of AI. From an era where humans evolve AI to an era where AI evolves AI.

These measurement results regarding the research intuition of GPT-6.2 Astra may be one important observation point indicating that this transition is underway.

P-Zero Research Official X Account (Measurement results announced on November 24, 2026) https://x.com/pzeroresearch

Introducing TasteVal — P-Zero Research https://pzeroresearch.com/work/tasteval/

Oliver Jaffe, Dane Sherburn, TasteVal: Measuring the Experimental Research Taste of AI Systems Against Human Experts (October 5, 2026) https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06824

Why spend thousands on animation tools when AI agents can help you build scenes, motion graphics, 3D visuals, and cinematic animations using free open-source tools?

This collection covers almost everything:
→ 🎬 Video: Remotion, Motion Canvas
→ ⚡ Motion & transitions: Motion, Anime.js, Shifty, TweenJS, Ola
→ 📐 Vector animation: Two.js, Lottie, Konva
→ 🧮 Math animation: Manim
→ 🌌 3D: Three.js, Babylon.js, LUME
→ 🎮 Game animation: Godot
→ 🧊 3D modeling & rigging: Blender
→ ✨ Particles & effects: Proton
→ 🎞️ GIF creation: gifenc
18 repositories. Endless creative possibilities.
Give your AI agent a brief → build the scene → animate → refine → render.
full_text_zh:

这个集合几乎涵盖了所有内容：

→ 📐 矢量动画：Two.js、Lottie、Konva
→ 🧮 数学动画：Manim
→ 🌌 3D：Three.js、Babylon.js、LUME
→ 🎮 游戏动画：戈多
→ 🧊 3D 建模和绑定：Blender
→ ✨ 粒子与效果：质子
→ 🎞️ GIF 创建：gifenc
18 个存储库。无限的创意可能性。
向您的 AI 代理简要介绍 → 构建场景 → 制作动画 → 细化 → 渲染。

title_en:
One last round, chads.

The 4th and final epoch of @termix_ai has officially started.

It's been a pretty interesting journey so far.

From exploring AACP and minting my own onchain agent identity to diving into agent reputation, verification mechanisms and autonomous trading strategies.

I started this campaign out of curiosity and ended up finishing #3 in Epoch 1 and #1 in Epoch 2.

But we're not done yet.

For the final epoch, I'll keep exploring the technical side of TermiX, sharing my own takes and breaking down what an actual autonomous agent economy could look like.

There's still a lot to unpack beyond the usual AI agent hype.

Let's make this last epoch count.

One final push. No slowing down now.

See you on the leaderboard, anons.

https://www.agent.family/r/R2J39LUD

title_en:
Demon Slayer, Street Fighter and Shield Hero Voice Actor, Stephen Fu Celebrates 41! 🎙️🔥🎮

Stephen Fu has quickly become a familiar voice across modern anime and gaming, bringing a striking range of heroes, villains, and fan favorites to life. His chilling performance as Douma in Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba stands alongside major game roles like Iron Fist / Lin Lie in Marvel Rivals, Jamie in Street Fighter 6, and Hwei in League of Legends.

Anime fans also know him as Naofumi Iwatani in The Rising of the Shield Hero, Weather Report in JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure: Stone Ocean, Sakuta Azusagawa in Rascal Does Not Dream of Bunny Girl Senpai, and Lance Crown in Mashle: Magic and Muscles. Newer roles such as Anaxa in Honkai: Star Rail, Natsuki Seba in Sakamoto Days, and Naito Mudano in Tougen Anki continue to expand an already impressive résumé.

史蒂芬·傅 (Stephen Fu) 迅速成为现代动漫和游戏领域的知名人物，将一系列引人注目的英雄、反派和粉丝最爱的角色带入生活。他在《鬼灭之刃》中饰演 Douma 的令人毛骨悚然的表演，与《漫威对手》中的铁拳 / 林烈、《街头霸王 6》中的 Jamie 以及《英雄联盟》中的 Hwei 等主要游戏角色齐名。

动漫迷们还知道他在《盾之勇者成名录》中扮演岩谷尚文、在《JoJo的奇妙冒险：石之海》中扮演天气预报、在《青春猪头少年不会梦到兔女郎学姐》中的梓川咲太以及在《魔法与肌肉》中扮演兰斯·克朗。新角色，如《崩坏：星轨》中的阿那克萨、《坂本时代》中的濑叶夏希以及《桃源 Anki》中的内藤·穆达诺，继续扩大本已令人印象深刻的履历。

title: Robotics control is undergoing a renaissance
title_en: Robotics control is undergoing a renaissance
title_zh: GPT-6.2 Astra引领机器人控制基准突破
author: Greg Brockman
author_role: OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人
summary_en: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra has demonstrated performance 5x above the previous two-year trend on robotic control benchmarks. Given the accelerated pace of benchmark saturation, AI models are on track to handle nearly all tracked robotic control tasks by the end of 2027.
summary_zh: GPT-6.2 Astra在机器人控制基准测试中表现卓越，预计2027年将覆盖大部分任务。
article_content:
According to Greg Brockman citing Playground on X, GPT-6.2 Astra scores sit nearly 5x above the past two years’ trend on robot-control benchmarks, with tasks on track to saturate by 2027.

On November 24 2026 Greg Brockman posted that robotics control is undergoing a renaissance driven by rapid gains in AI model performance.

According to the post Playground GPT-6.2 Astra sits nearly five times above the exponential trend of the prior two years on robot-control benchmarks while benchmarks themselves are saturating roughly ten times faster than the year before. If the pace observed since September continues top policies could saturate nearly every tracked task by the end of 2027.
full_text_zh: 机器人控制正在经历复兴
full_text_en: Robotics control is undergoing a renaissance

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI旗下的GPT-6.2 Astra在机器人控制基准测试中表现出超越过往两年趋势5倍的性能增长。随着基准测试迭代速度的加快，若当前增长态势延续，预计到2027年底，AI模型将实现对主流机器人控制任务的全面饱和覆盖。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra has demonstrated performance 5x above the previous two-year trend on robotic control benchmarks. Given the accelerated pace of benchmark saturation, AI models are on track to handle nearly all tracked robotic control tasks by the end of 2027.

elements_zh.who: Greg Brockman（OpenAI联合创始人）与Playground平台
elements_zh.where: 机器人控制基准测试（Robotics Control Benchmarks）
elements_zh.what: GPT-6.2 Astra表现超出预期趋势5倍，任务覆盖度预计2027年饱和
elements_zh.why: AI模型性能的突飞猛进带动了机器人控制领域的复兴

elements_en.what: GPT-6.2 Astra exceeds trends by 5x; trajectory indicates task saturation by 2027
elements_en.why: Rapid gains in AI model performance driving a renaissance in robotics control

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 具身智能的突破口已由单纯的运动学模拟转向大模型驱动的逻辑决策闭环。基准测试的快速饱和预示着通用物理交互能力的成熟，未来机器人领域的核心壁垒将迅速从算法模型迁移至硬件本体的耐用性与规模化生产成本。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The breakthrough in embodied AI has shifted from kinematic simulation to large-model-driven logic decision loops. The rapid saturation of benchmarks signals the maturity of general physical interaction, shifting core competitive barriers from algorithmic models to hardware durability and scale-manufacturing costs.

ai_analysis.digest_en: GPT-6.2 Astra shows a 5x improvement over historical benchmarks in robotics control, signaling that AI-driven physical task automation could reach saturation by 2027.

GitHub 刚刚为 2026 年最受欢迎的开发者角色创建了官方认证。

它被称为 Agentic AI Developer。考试 GH-600。

不是一个及时的工程师。不是振动编码器。

在整个开发生命周期中运行、监督和保护 AI 代理的人员。

它测试什么：
- 代理架构和规划
- 工具使用和MCP服务器
- 内存和状态
- 评估和错误分析
- 多代理协调
- 护栏和责任

如果您已经使用 Copilot 或代理工作流程进行构建，那么您正在做这项工作。

GH-600 就是您证明这一点的方式。

将此添加为书签。

ai_analysis.takeaway_en: This indicates a paradigm shift from model fine-tuning to production-grade system control, driving vertical differentiation in the developer ecosystem. For organizations, this certification will serve as a standard benchmark for evaluating the reliability and security of autonomous AI implementations.

title_en:
Finally get to say this: @Muse is in the UK! I've been eager to bring this to my peeps back home for ages. Properly chuffed today 🇬🇧🇬🇧🇬🇧.

Every Muse runs on its own computer in the cloud. A separate security agent (Sentinel) checks its actions against permissions you've given. We built it this way because an agent that can do things for you needs more than instructions about what it should and should not do.

You can see what Muse does and decide what it remembers. More on how we built it and how to manage your controls: https://about.fb.com/news/2026/11/muse-now-available-in-the-uk-muse-does-the-work-you-stay-in-control/

title: things are insane right now >jensen is back >google neon is low key elite >fable can build a nolan level film for just 10 bucks >run every hard decision through gemini as a second opinion >turn every marketing job you do into a skill and give it to the whole tea
title_en:
things are insane right now

>jensen is back

>google neon is low key elite

>fable can build a nolan level film for just 10 bucks

>run every hard decision through gemini as a second opinion

>turn every marketing job you do into a skill and give it to the whole team

>have an agent edit your videos in davinci resolve through its MCP

>add a grok bot to your team’s slack and video calls so it takes notes and follows up on deadlines

>give grok bot a developer bot and a PM bot and let them ship pull requests all day

>turn your whole GTM off one postgres database and with three tables: accounts, people and signals

>make a UGC ad video for ~$1 that earlier used to cost $100

>let your agent rent its own GPUs from inside the chat

>point REA at any app you pay for and rebuild the feature you like

>have claude code make 100+ on brand static ads and upload them to facebook through the API

>scrape everyone who engaged with a linkedin post and drop them into a cold email sequence (also have a feedback loop to make the sequence better)

>and so much more that it’s brain breaking

this is the greatest time to be building and it isn’t even close
title_zh:
现在事情很疯狂

>詹森回来了

>google neon 低调精英

>《神鬼寓言》只需 10 美元就能拍出一部诺兰级别的电影

>通过双子座作为第二意见来做出每一个艰难的决定

>将你所做的每一项营销工作变成一项技能，并将其传授给整个团
author: @ilavanyajain
summary_zh:
队

>让代理通过其MCP在达芬奇解析中编辑您的视频

>在团队的 Slack 和视频通话中添加一个 Grok 机器人，以便它记笔记并跟进截止日期

>给 grok 机器人一个开发机器人和一个 PM 机器人，让他们全天发送 Pull 请求

>关闭你的整个GTM，关闭一个postgres数据库并使用三个表：帐户、人员和信号

>制作一个 UGC 广告视频的成本约为 1 美元，而之前的价格为 100 美元

>让您的代理从聊天中租用自己的 GPU

>将 REA 指向您付费的任何应用程序并重建您喜欢的功能

>让 Claude Code 在品牌静态广告上制作 100+ 并通过 API 上传到 Facebook

>抓取所有参与linkedin帖子的人并将他们放入冷电子邮件序列中（还有一个反馈循环以使序列更好）

>还有更多令人伤脑筋的事情

这是建设的最佳时机，但还远未结束

title: Two big points from this new Anthropic paper: 1) The most AI value comes from changing the organization 2) There is wide worker resistance to AI adoption (partially due to point 1) Changes that expand what workers do & share AI gains with them could help h
title_en:
Two big points from this new Anthropic paper:
1) The most AI value comes from changing the organization
2) There is wide worker resistance to AI adoption (partially due to point 1)

Changes that expand what workers do & share AI gains with them could help https://www.anthropic.com/research/working-with-ai
title_zh:
这篇新的人类论文有两个要点：
1）人工智能最大的价值来自于组织的改变
2) 工人普遍抵制人工智能的采用（部分原因是第 1 点）

扩大员工工作范围并与他们分享人工智能收益的变革可能会有所帮助 https://www.anthropic.co

title: 🎉 ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview has Day-0 support in @vllm_project through the vLLM-ERNIE plugin! @Baidu_Inc’s 280B-total / 14B-active MoE brings reasoning, tool calling and up to 1M-token context. Install the plugin alongside the released vLLM 0.32.0 wheel
title_en:
🎉 ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview has Day-0 support in @vllm_project through the vLLM-ERNIE plugin!

@Baidu_Inc’s 280B-total / 14B-active MoE brings reasoning, tool calling and up to 1M-token context. Install the plugin alongside the released vLLM 0.32.0 wheel and serve it through the OpenAI-compatible API.

Under the hood:
• Architecture-specific fused kernels run 1.55–6.53× faster than naive implementations.
• FlashIndexer accelerates sparse indexing by 1.4× at 1M context.
• A bundled 3-layer DSpark draft proposes up to 7 tokens per step, with mean acceptance length above 4.0 on real-world coding and agent workloads.

FP4 on @NVIDIA Blackwell; FP8 and BF16 on Blackwell and H100. Weights are available through @huggingface and @ModelScope2022.

Thanks to the Baidu ERNIE team and the vLLM community for the model integration and inference optimizations!

Get started: https://github.com/baidu/vLLM-ERNIE

Blog: https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-11-24-ernie-5-5-flash-preview
Recipe: https://recipes.vllm.ai/baidu/ERNIE-5.5-Flash
title_zh:
🎉 ERNIE 5.5 Flash 预览版通过 vLLM-ERNIE 插件在 @vllm_project 中提供 Day-0 支持！

@Baidu_Inc 的 280B 总计 / 14B 活跃 MoE 带来推理、工具调用和高达 1M 代币
author: vLLM Project
author_role: 高通量、低内存显存极速推理架构
summary_zh:
上下文。将插件与已发布的 vLLM 0.32.0 轮一起安装，并通过 OpenAI 兼容的 API 提供服务。

在引擎盖下：
• 特定于架构的融合内核的运行速度比原始实现快 1.55–6.53 倍。
• FlashIndexer 在 1M 上下文中将稀疏索引加速 1.4 倍。
• 捆绑的 3 层 DSpark 草案建议每步最多 7 个令牌，实际编码和代理工作负载的平均接受长度高于 4.0。

@NVIDIA Blackwell 上的 FP4； Blackwell 和 H100 上的 FP8 和 BF16。权重可通过@huggingface 和@ModelScope2022 获得。

感谢百度ERNIE团队和vLLM社区的模型集成和推理优化！

ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: ERNIE系列通过接入vLLM插件，实质上是百度在开源推理基础设施层面的生态卡位，旨在降低开发者在其MoE模型上的落地门槛。此举不仅是对抗同类长上下文模型竞争的差异化策略，更是通过与主流推理框架的深度绑定，加速其模型在私有化部署市场的份额渗透。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: By integrating with the vLLM plugin, Baidu is strategically securing its position within the open-source inference ecosystem to lower barriers for MoE model deployment. This move serves as a competitive play against other long-context models, aiming to accelerate market penetration in private deployment by aligning with standardized inference infrastructures.

title: I'd personally revise AI capex estimates back up (beyond accelerators), after Jensen's return to $NVDA. A lot of revised forecasts where made off him leaving, but his return, can be a lot more confidence in spend with upstream supply chains + bottlenecks. Jens
title_en:
I'd personally revise AI capex estimates back up (beyond accelerators), after Jensen's return to $NVDA. 

A lot of revised forecasts where made off him leaving, but his return, can be a lot more confidence in spend with upstream supply chains + bottlenecks. 

Jensen my ideal game theory troll, he just secures all the capacity of things other programs like $GOOGL or Amazon needs. 

> Testing? (Nvidia just secures all the capacity)
> Substrates? (Nvidia just secures all the capacity)
> Lasers? (Nvidia just secures all the capacity)
> Memory? (Nvidia just secures all the capacity)

Before there was a lot of uncertainty (to the point I had to model major capex cuts)...

But Jensen's return forces hyperscalers to be much more aggressive again in supply procurement.
title_zh: 黄仁勋重申留任NVDA，AI资本支出预期上修
author: @aleabitoreddit
full_text_zh:
在 Jensen 回归 $NVDA 后，我个人会修改 AI 资本支出估计（超越加速器）。

许多修改后的预测导致他离开，但他的回归可以让人们对上游供应链+瓶颈的支出更有信心。

Jensen 是我理想的博弈论巨魔，他只是确保了 $GOOGL 或 Amazon 等其他程序所需的所有功能。

> 测试？ （Nvidia 只是确保所有容量）
> 基材？ （Nvidia 只是确保所有容量）
> 激光？ （Nvidia 只是确保所有容量）
> 记忆？ （Nvidia 只是确保所有容量）

在存在很多不确定性之前（以至于我必须对主要资本支出削减进行建模）......

但詹森的回归迫使超大规模企业在供应采购方面再次更加积极。

title:
He's right.  We are experiencing the death of thought.

Just now, I had to read a hefty AI-generated 900-word post about
title_en:
He's right.  We are experiencing the death of thought.

Just now, I had to read a hefty AI-generated 900-word post about a guy who printed a contract and used a mechanical pencil.

Rather than skim it for 12 seconds, whisper “good for him,” and move on with my evening, I did something radical.

I didn’t print your post on a Wi-Fi laser printer like some kind of Silicon Valley soft-hands.

I transcribed every single one of your 902 words by hand onto unbleached calfskin vellum using a goose quill I cured in my own garage, sharpened it with a dull pocketknife until my thumb bled, and spent four and a half hours marking up the margins in homemade iron-gall ink.

I finished writing down my thoughts in the margins, set down my quill, stared silently at a brass lamp, and reflected on what just happened.

I felt deeply satisfied, wildly embarrassed, mildly dehydrated, and somehow taller all at once.

I couldn’t remember the last time I had used my brain for an end-to-end process without relying on an industrial convenience like a mechanical pencil or Hewlett-Packard toner. I felt total command over your post. I felt crystalline clarity about what I understood, what I didn’t understand, and why a grown man felt moved to alert the entire timeline that he had read a PDF with a pencil. And I was left with unshakable conviction in my POV.

Moreover, I felt the high of “ultra-clean” dopamine.

Not the factory-farmed, seed-oil dopamine you get from pressing a plastic thumb-clicker on a 0.7mm Pentel like a lab rat tapping a lever for pellets. Not the lukewarm, ultra-processed dopamine of reading a contract printed out on bleached 20-pound copy paper that a machine collated for you without even asking you to set the movable type.

No. I’m talking about single-origin, cold-pressed, pasture-raised dopamine. The kind of raw, unadulterated neurochemical high our ancestors felt when they sat down at a mahogany desk, read an actual contract from page one to the signature block, and didn’t immediately open LinkedIn to announce that they had survived the ordeal.

Then I felt embarrassed.

How long had I been depriving myself of turning basic adult errands into sweeping civilizational manifestos?

Just yesterday, I made two slices of sourdough toast without once asking Claude to “review this loaf, break down the crumb structure, and give me feedback as if you’re my baker.” I stood there in front of the toaster like a pioneer on the Oregon Trail, watched the heating coils glow orange, buttered the bread manually, and ate it. And what did I do afterward? Nothing. I just rinsed my plate and went to work. Not a single 1,000-word reflection on the erosion of culinary agency. Not one mention of Socrates. Not one bulleted list of ways to reclaim the sacred space between bread and butter.

I was disgusted with myself.

And then I got curious.

In fact, I got so curious that I had to sit down, because curiosity at this altitude can make a man lightheaded.

Why is it that every time somebody in tech rediscovers an office supply from 1987, he feels spiritually compelled to summon Daniel Kahneman, Socrates, and Viktor Frankl like the Avengers? And what can we do to make sure we don’t surrender our last remaining shred of self-awareness to the Thought Leadership Industrial Complex?

The answer lies in what Daniel Kahneman called System 1 and System 2 thinking, and more importantly, in the three higher systems that Kahneman was too polite to put in the book.

Everyone on the internet loves citing System 1 and System 2, mostly because Thinking, Fast and Slow is the single most-referenced book among people who read a four-page summary of it in 2016 and have been dining out on the phrase “lazy controller” ever since.

System 1 is fast, automatic, and gut-driven thought. It’s what fires when a 42-page commercial agreement lands in your inbox on a Thursday afternoon and your brain immediately says, “I am not reading all of this, I should probably pay an actual lawyer instead of asking a chatbot to roleplay as one.”

System 2 is deliberate, analytical, effortful, and conscious. It’s what fires when you ignore System 1, print the 42-page agreement yourself, grab a mechanical pencil, write “check indemnity??” and “what does mutatis mutandis mean” in the margins for 90 minutes, and walk away from your desk feeling like John Marshall presiding over Marbury v. Madison.

But stopping at System 2 is rookie-level cognition. If you really want to diagnose what is happening to the human mind in 2026, you have to go deeper:

System 3 is performing System 2 in public so strangers know you still have a prefrontal cortex. You didn’t merely read the contract. You observed yourself reading the contract from a cinematic third-person camera angle, felt a single noble tear roll down your cheek, and started mentally workshopping the opening hook somewhere around Section 7.2(b).

System 4 is taking a completely normal Tuesday afternoon task (reading a document before you sign it) and laundering it through one ancient Greek philosopher, three cognitive psychologists, a misattributed quote, ten repetitive bullet points, and a closing comparison to the sun until a routine administrative chore sounds like the drafting of the Magna Carta.

System 5 is reading someone else’s System 4 post and concluding that the only proportionate moral response is to construct an even longer, even more grandiose System 4 post, thereby testing the structural load limits of the X Premium character counter and everybody’s patience simultaneously.

Technology has been hijacking effortful thinking for far longer than 370 BC. Frankly, starting the timeline with Socrates is System 1 history.

Roughly a million years ago: Fire hijacked raw-meat mastication as a gastrointestinal System 2 exercise. Early hominids no longer had to chew elk cartilage for four uninterrupted hours just to extract 300 calories. Immediate metabolic offloading. Everything went downhill from there.

3200 BC: Sumerian cuneiform hijacked remembering how many goats your brother-in-law owed you from the spring harvest. Within two generations, nobody could keep track of a single goat in their head. Pure cognitive atrophy.

1440 AD: Gutenberg’s printing press hijacked the deeply satisfying, hard-fought labor of being a medieval monk squinting in an unheated stone scriptorium for eleven years to hand-copy one manuscript by tallow candle. Did anyone pause to ask what the printing press was doing to the monks’ taste?

1784: Bifocals hijacked squinting as an ocular System 2 exercise.

Google hijacked sitting at a bar for three hours insisting to your friends that Kevin Costner was in Air Force One when it was actually Harrison Ford, the kind of hard-fought, unadulterated barstool conviction that used to build real character.

Like this.

And this.

Cost 2: The messy middle is the space for growth, which is also where you discover that reviewing a hefty contract without a lawyer is an exciting way to buy a lawsuit.

You asked what will stay uniquely human as we approach AGI and ASI, and you gave us four pillars:

1. Intent
2. Accountability
3. Relationships
4. Judgement

Solid start. Respectable list. A little short, though. If we’re being honest about the final frontier of human uniqueness in the age of superintelligence, there are at least six more traits no neural network will ever truly replicate:

5. Printing a 30-page PDF so you can carry it around the house looking burdened and important.
6. Telling everybody at dinner that you’ve “been going really analog lately.”
7. Buying a $65 brass mechanical pencil from a specialty stationery shop in Kyoto so your margin notes have better mouthfeel.
8. Calling regular job satisfaction “clean dopamine” because saying “I felt good about finishing my work” doesn’t sound like a Huberman episode.
9. Assuming that because you used to outsource your thinking to Claude, the rest of Western civilization forgot how to read a document.
10. Confusing “having taste” with “posting about how important taste is.”

Reading your own draft back before hitting Post and thinking, “Wait, did I really just compare myself reading a contract with a pencil to fighting for the survival of human thought?”

Every serious productivity essay on the internet must, by federal statute, include the exact quote:

It’s a lovely sentiment. There is just one tiny, delicious wrinkle.

Viktor Frankl never wrote it.

Sometimes you didn’t strike a blow against the death of thought. Sometimes you just did your homework.

So how do we take back our thinking, our brevity, and our dignity, while still embracing this transformative technology?

It resolves down to one key principle: rebuild the space between having a normal afternoon and writing a 900-word sermon about it.

How you rebuild that space is completely up to you. Pick your poison:

AI is a very fast autocomplete machine wired into a warehouse of GPUs that helps people turn a three-sentence email into a keynote about human destiny.

Yes, it may help cure cancer.
Yes, it may put a tutor in every child’s hands.
Yes, it may usher in an age of abundance, starting, apparently, with an unlimited abundance of 900-word essays by executives who just discovered paper and graphite.

Anyway, I’ll be completely honest with you: I didn’t write a single word of this.

I pasted your post into my AI and told it to draft an extremely lengthy quote tweet at least twice as long as yours, because I had better things to do tonight and frankly it seemed funnier than thinking.

We must fight against the death of thought.

此外，我还感受到了“超洁净”多巴胺的快感。

不是工厂化养殖的种子油多巴胺，是通过在 0.7 毫米 Pentel 上按下塑料拇指点击器而获得的，就像实验室老鼠敲击颗粒杠杆一样。阅读打印在漂白的 20 磅复印纸上的合同时，机器会帮你校对，甚至不需要你设置活字印刷，这不是那种不冷不热、经过过度处理的多巴胺。

不，我说的是单一来源、冷榨、牧场饲养的多巴胺。当我们的祖先坐在桃花心木办公桌前，从第一页读到签名栏，阅读一份真实的合同，并且没有立即打开 LinkedIn 宣布他们已经从这场磨难中幸存下来时，他们感受到了那种原始的、纯粹的神经化学物质的兴奋。

然后我就觉得很尴尬。

我已经多久没有把基本的成人事务变成全面的文明宣言了？

就在昨天，我做了两片酵母吐司，一次都没有要求克劳德“检查这条面包，分解面包屑结构，并给我反馈，就像你是我的面包师一样。”我像俄勒冈小道上的拓荒者一样站在烤面包机前，看着加热线圈发出橙色的光，手动在面包上涂黄油，然后吃掉它。然后我做了什么？没有什么。我刚洗完盘子就去上班了。没有一篇关于烹饪机构受到侵蚀的千字反思。没有提到苏格拉底。没有一份详细的清单列出了重新夺回面包和黄油之间神圣空间的方法。

我对自己感到厌恶。

然后我很好奇。

事实上，我实在是太好奇了，不得不坐下来，因为在这种高度的好奇心会让人头晕目眩。

为什么每次科技领域的人重新发现 1987 年的办公用品时，他都会在精神上感到有必要像复仇者联盟一样召唤丹尼尔·卡尼曼、苏格拉底和维克托·弗兰克尔？我们能做些什么来确保我们不会将最后的一点自我意识拱手让给思想领导工业综合体？

答案就在于丹尼尔·卡尼曼所说的“系统1”和“系统2”的思维，更重要的是，在于卡尼曼出于礼貌而没有将其放入书中的三个更高的系统。

互联网上的每个人都喜欢引用系统 1 和系统 2，主要是因为《思考，快与慢》是人们在 2016 年读过该书长达四页的摘要并从那时起就一直在谈论“懒惰控制器”这个词的人中引用最多的一本书。

系统 1 是快速、自动、直觉驱动的思维。当周四下午一份 42 页的商业协议到达你的收件箱时，你的大脑立即说：“我不会阅读所有这些内容，我可能应该付钱给一名真正的律师，而不是让聊天机器人扮演律师。”

系统2是深思熟虑的、分析性的、努力的、有意识的。当你忽略系统 1，自己打印 42 页的协议，拿起自动铅笔，写下“检查赔偿？”时，就会触发这种情况。并在页边空白处写上“比照意味着什么”90 分钟，然后离开办公桌，感觉就像约翰·马歇尔在主持马伯里诉麦迪逊案。

但止步于系统2是菜鸟级别的认知。如果你真的想诊断 2026 年人类思维会发生什么，你必须更深入：

系统 3 在公共场合执行系统 ​​2，因此陌生人知道您仍然有前额皮质。您不仅仅阅读了合同。你观察到自己从电影般的第三人称视角阅读合同，感觉到一滴高贵的泪水从你的脸颊滚落，并开始在脑海中思考第 7.2(b) 节周围的开头钩子。

系统 4 正在执行一项完全正常的周二下午任务（在签署之前阅读一份文件），并通过一位古希腊哲学家、三位认知心理学家、一段错误引用、十个重复的要点以及与太阳的最终比较来对其进行清洗，直到日常行政琐事听起来像是起草《大宪章》。

系统 5 正在阅读其他人的系统 4 帖子，并得出结论，唯一相称的道德反应是构建一个更长、更宏伟的系统 4 帖子，从而同时测试 X Premium 角色计数器的结构负载限制和每个人的耐心。

自公元前 370 年以来，技术一直在劫持努力的思维。坦率地说，从苏格拉底开始的时间线就是系统 1 的历史。

大约一百万年前：火劫持了生肉咀嚼作为胃肠道系统 2 的锻炼。早期原始人类不再需要连续四个小时不间断地咀嚼麋鹿软骨来获取 300 卡路里的热量。立即代谢卸载。从那里开始一切都走下坡路。

公元前 3200 年：苏美尔楔形文字劫持了你的姐夫欠你多少春收的山羊。在两代人的时间里，没有人能够在头脑中记住一只山羊。纯粹的认知萎缩。

公元 1440 年：古腾堡的印刷机劫持了一位中世纪僧侣在没有暖气的石质写字间眯着眼睛用牛油蜡烛手抄一份手稿长达 11 年的令人深感满足的艰苦劳动。有没有人停下来问一下印刷机对僧侣们的口味做了什么？

1784 年：双焦点眼镜劫持了眯眼作为一种视觉系统 2 的锻炼方式。

1822 年：约翰·艾萨克·霍金斯 (John Isaac Hawkins) 和桑普森·莫丹 (Sampson Mordan) 为第一支自动铅笔获得了第 4742 号英国专利，专利本身的明确设计目的是“无需频繁切割或修补笔尖或笔尖”。

停下来坐一会儿。

昨天你在与硅谷对抗时高举的 Excalibur 机械铅笔本身就是一台拥有 204 年历史的机器，其设计目的是为了减轻用刀片削雪松木和吹掉拇指上的石墨粉尘时产生的高贵、塑造性格的摩擦。你没有拒绝捷径。你刚刚选择了一条维多利亚时代的捷径，并称之为启蒙。

1959 年：施乐 914 复印机劫持了在复写纸上重新打印合同的行为。

1983 年：Microsoft Word 劫持了 Wite-Out，以及在 15 页租约的第 14 页上犯错的健康、令人肾上腺素飙升的恐惧。

计算器劫持了长除法。
GPS 被劫持，您与配偶就中控台上折叠的兰德·麦克纳利道路地图集争论，同时错过了萨凡纳的出口。
谷歌劫持了在酒吧坐了三个小时，向你的朋友坚称凯文·科斯特纳在空军一号，而实际上是哈里森·福特，这种经过艰苦斗争、纯粹的酒吧凳信念用来塑造真实的性格。

现在，公平地说，你对一件大事的看法是正确的。人工智能确实不同。

它不仅仅一次接管一项艰苦的工作。它立刻接管了所有的人。

记住。总结一下。研究中。计算。写作。解决问题。权衡利弊。决定。规划。为人们导航。反思。创造。听起来像是 2019 年的 Medium 帖子。在一篇 5,300 字的文章中十次用“&”代替“and”，没有人会出现空间不足的情况。在关于抵抗机器的宣言中讽刺地使用了动词“grok”。建立一个包含十项项目符号的列表，其中四个项目符号实际上是相同的项目符号，穿着不同的毛衣。

20万年来，我们的大脑一直习惯于轻松出行。当我们屈服于捷径时，无论是让法学硕士阅读我们的合同，还是让LinkedIn格式完成听起来深刻的繁重工作，我们都会付出高昂的代价。

让我们来分解一下实际成本。

成本1：总结感觉像是理解，编号框架感觉像是智慧。

你完全正确，阅读压缩摘要会欺骗你的大脑，让你相信你理解了一个你从未真正思考过的主题。被忽视的是镜像陷阱：将一段 12 个字的常识（“如果你不读合同，你不会知道里面有什么”）并将其夸大为关于旧石器时代大脑进化的 900 字讲座，欺骗作者和读者，让他们认为他们刚刚见证了认识论的突破。包装不是洞察力。单行段落没有深度。

像这样。

还有这个。

注意你的大脑现在想要慢慢点头，尽管自上一段以来我没有说过任何话。这就是系统 1 的换行符。

成本2：混乱的中间是成长的空间，这也是你发现在没有律师的情况下审查一份巨额合同是一种令人兴奋的购买诉讼的方式的地方。

罗伯特·比约克（Robert Bjork）在加州大学洛杉矶分校关于“理想困难”的研究确实是伟大的研究，里斯科和吉尔伯特关于认知卸载的研究也是真实的。努力的检索可以使学习坚持下去。没有人认真地反对这一点。有趣的是，我们表现得好像理想难度是一种濒临灭绝的物种，我们必须用“无人工智能块”人为制造，就好像现实生活还没有每个工作日提供九个小时非自愿的理想难度一样。尝试与顽固的贷方达成交易，在应收账款滑落时管理工资，或者阅读商业租赁第 14.3(c) 条，其中另一方悄悄地将个人担保埋在样板维护条款中。你不需要花 10 分钟提高效率来体验认知摩擦。只需在游戏中拥有真实的皮肤即可。

成本3：判断力的消失，表演性叹息的兴起。

您问当我们接近 AGI 和 ASI 时，什么才能保持人类的独特性，您给了我们四个支柱：

1. 意图
2. 问责制
3. 关系
4、判断

扎实的开始。令人尊敬的名单。不过有点短。如果我们诚实地对待超级智能时代人类独特性的最终前沿，那么至少还有六个特征是神经网络无法真正复制的：

5. 打印一份 30 页的 PDF，这样你就可以带着它在家里到处走，看起来既沉重又重要。
6. 在晚餐时告诉大家你“最近一直在进行模拟”。
7. 从京都的一家文具专卖店购买一支 65 美元的黄铜自动铅笔，这样你的页边笔记会有更好的口感。
8. 将正常的工作满意度称为“干净的多巴胺”，因为说“我对完成工作感觉很好”听起来不像休伯曼的插曲。
9. 假设因为你过去把你的思维外包给克劳德，所以西方文明的其他部分忘记了如何阅读文档。
10. 将“有品味”与“发布品味的重要性”混为一谈。

味道实际上是数千个压缩的 System 2 模式同时发射。你知道其中一种图案是什么样子的吗？在点击《邮报》之前，先回顾一下自己的草稿，然后思考：“等等，我真的只是将自己用铅笔阅读一份合同与为人类思想的生存而战进行比较吗？”

成本 4：维克多·弗兰克尔工业园区。

根据联邦法规，互联网上每一篇严肃的生产力文章都必须包含准确的引用：

“刺激和反应之间有一个空间。在这个空间里，我们有能力选择我们的反应。我们的反应就是我们的成长和自由。”

这是一种可爱的情感。只有一条细小的、美味的皱纹。

维克多·弗兰克尔从未写过它。

研究人员从头到尾检索了《人类的意义探寻》和弗兰克尔出版的其他作品。这些话不存在。史蒂芬·柯维 (Stephen Covey) 在夏威夷的一本大学图书馆的书中看到类似的段落后，就普及了这句话（学者们指出，心理学家罗洛·梅 (Rollo May) 1963 年撰写的有关刺激与反应之间暂停的文章是最接近的前兆），大约在 2000 年代中期，互联网将维克多·弗兰克尔 (Viktor Frankl) 的名字贴在上面，再也没有回头。

想想这纯粹的诗意。在你自己的要点之上几行命令人类“阅读完整的源代码，而不是摘要”，你在整个互联网上丢下了最著名的错误总结文化引用。

如果这不是一个关于认知卸载的案例研究，那就没什么了。

成本5：隐喻的过度膨胀。

曾几何时，合同就是合同，太阳是一个 46 亿年前的聚变氢等离子体球，距离地球 9300 万英里，它种植农作物，为水循环提供动力，如果你在后九洞不涂防晒霜，它还会给你一个坚韧的脖子。

现在，概率文本引擎会告诉您“这是一个非常尖锐、微妙的观点！”每次你拼写错误的问题都是“like the sun”。

如果人工智能是太阳，那么自动铅笔又是什么呢？遮阳伞？防晒指数 50？一副偏光太阳镜？一旦你开始将软件订阅与太空中的核聚变进行比较，当真正重要的事情发生时，你就会无处可去。

成本6：比例性的崩溃。

当每一个小小的个人认识（今天我仔细阅读一份文件，而不是浏览人工智能项目符号列表！）都必须被视为物种边缘的一场生存之战时，我们的集体尺度感就崩溃了。有时你没有对思想的死亡进行打击。有时你只是做了作业。

那么，我们如何在拥抱这项变革性技术的同时，收回我们的思考、我们的简洁和我们的尊严呢？

它归结为一个关键原则：重建一个正常的下午和为此写一篇 900 字的布道之间的空间。

如何重建该空间完全取决于您。选择你的毒药：

- 在一天中创建 30 到 60 分钟的无 AI 时段，然后立即进行 90 分钟的无发帖时段，这样您就不会因在网上吹嘘而抵消全部精神益处。
- 进行模拟并打印出重要的内容。然后打印一些根本不重要的东西，只是为了保持对打印机的主导地位。
- 扔掉自动铅笔。使用木制 2 号刀，然后用小刀在金属废纸篓上削尖，就像您祖父在艾森豪威尔政府期间所做的那样。
- 阅读完整的源代码，而不是摘要，从《Man's Search for Meaning》开始，这样你就可以亲眼看到其中实际上包含了哪些引言。
- 在审查一份巨额合同时，不要让克劳德表现得“就像你是我的律师一样”，而是尝试采用激进、古老的模拟工作流程，即聘请一名真正的律师。
- 手写你的初稿。退潮时在湿沙上写下你的第二稿，这样你就能学会不执着。
- 设定 10 分钟规则：在使用 AI 之前先解决一个问题 10 分钟。然后设定一个 20 分钟的规则：在打开 X 之前，克制住引用 Daniel Kahneman 的冲动。
- 大声说出来：向调酒师解释你最新的生产力认识，除非你关闭标签，否则他不能合法地离开他的收银台，并观察他的眼睛来判断它是否真的很深刻。
- 记住纸质高速公路地图并拒绝使用 GPS，即使您晚于晚餐 18 分钟并且您的妻子默默地盯着乘客窗外。前排座位上冰冷的沉默？这就是系统 2 的实时重建。
- 午餐时在鸡尾酒餐巾背面做自己的长除法，这样餐桌上的人就知道你仍然参与到认知游戏中。
- 在发表任何超过 500 字的文章之前，先用凿子将其雕刻在一块石灰石上，以测试人类是否真正需要它。
- 将“grok”替换为“理解”，将“&”替换为“and”，并将“干净的多巴胺”替换为“我对完成工作感觉很好”。
- 不间断地盯着窗外 15 分钟，零输入、零播客和零心理模型，直到您记住“控制刺激和反应之间的空间”过去被称为安静地坐着。
- 永远不要再总结任何事情。如果朋友问一部电影怎么样，请站起来并在完整的遮挡和灯光提示下背诵整个剧本。
- 将人工智能视为“编辑”，而不是“作家”。这样，当它为你重写每一个句子时，你仍然可以在温暖的语义毯下安然入睡。
- 在发表有关人类认知未来的任何内容之前，问自己最后一个问题：苏格拉底会打出这个，还是会提前二十分钟索要铁杉？

人工智能就像太阳。

事实上，如果我们在这里应用一点系统 2 的严格性，人工智能与太阳完全不同。太阳是一颗G型主序恒星，通过引力将八颗行星保持在轨道上，最终将膨胀成红巨星并蒸发地球。人工智能是一种非常快速的自动完成机器，连接到 GPU 仓库中，可以帮助人们将三句话电子邮件变成关于人类命运的主题演讲。

是的，它可能有助于治愈癌症。
是的，它可能会让每个孩子都有一位导师。
是的，它可能会迎来一个丰富的时代，显然，从刚刚发现纸和石墨的高管们撰写的无限丰富的 900 字论文开始。

它的力量强大得难以估量。这就是为什么我们必须不惜一切代价保护人类的最后边界：知道何时阅读合同，放下铅笔，关闭笔记本电脑，而不是在互联网上写下任何有关它的字。

不管怎样，我对你说实话：我一个字都没有写。

我将你的帖子粘贴到我的人工智能中，并告诉它起草一条极其冗长的引用推文，长度至少是你的两倍，因为今晚我有更好的事情要做，坦率地说，这似乎比思考更有趣。

我们必须与思想的死亡作斗争。
author: Coastal Country Club
summary_zh:
没有像硅谷的软手那样使用 Wi-Fi 激光打印机打印你的文章。

我用在自家车库里腌制的鹅毛笔，将你的 902 个单词中的每一个字都手写在未漂白的小牛皮牛皮纸上，用钝的小刀将其削尖，直到我的拇指流血，并花了四个半小时用自制的铁胆墨水标记边缘。

我在页边写完自己的想法，放下羽毛笔，默默地盯着一盏铜灯，思考着刚刚发生的事情。

我感到深深的满足、极度的尴尬、轻微的脱水，但不知何故突然长高了。

我不记得上次我在不依赖自动铅笔或惠普碳粉等工业便利设施的情况下使用大脑进行端到端流程是什么时候了。我对你的帖子感到完全掌控。我对自己理解的内容、不理解的内容感到非常清晰，也明白了为什么一个成年人会因为提醒整个时间线他用铅笔阅读了一份 PDF 而感到感动。我对自己的观点有着不可动摇的信念。

此外，我还感受到了“超洁净”多巴胺的快感。

不是工厂化养殖的种子油多巴胺，是通过在 0.7 毫米 Pentel 上按下塑料拇指点击器而获得的，就像实验室老鼠敲击颗粒杠杆一样。阅读打印在漂白的 20 磅复印纸上的合同时，机器会帮你校对，甚至不需要你设置活字印刷，这不是那种不冷不热、经过过度处理的多巴胺。

不，我说的是单一来源、冷榨、牧场饲养的多巴胺。当我们的祖先坐在桃花心木办公桌前，从第一页读到签名栏，阅读一份真实的合同，并且没有立即打开 LinkedIn 宣布他们已经从这场磨难中幸存下来时，他们感受到了那种原始的、纯粹的神经化学物质的兴奋。

然后我就觉得很尴尬。

我已经多久没有把基本的成人事务变成全面的文明宣言了？

就在昨天，我做了两片酵母吐司，一次都没有要求克劳德“检查这条面包，分解面包屑结构，并给我反馈，就像你是我的面包师一样。”我像俄勒冈小道上的拓荒者一样站在烤面包机前，看着加热线圈发出橙色的光，手动在面包上涂黄油，然后吃掉它。然后我做了什么？没有什么。我刚洗完盘子就去上班了。没有一篇关于烹饪机构受到侵蚀的千字反思。没有提到苏格拉底。没有一份详细的清单列出了重新夺回面包和黄油之间神圣空间的方法。

我对自己感到厌恶。

然后我很好奇。

事实上，我实在是太好奇了，不得不坐下来，因为在这种高度的好奇心会让人头晕目眩。

为什么每次科技领域的人重新发现 1987 年的办公用品时，他都会在精神上感到有必要像复仇者联盟一样召唤丹尼尔·卡尼曼、苏格拉底和维克托·弗兰克尔？我们能做些什么来确保我们不会将最后的一点自我意识拱手让给思想领导工业综合体？

答案就在于丹尼尔·卡尼曼所说的“系统1”和“系统2”的思维，更重要的是，在于卡尼曼出于礼貌而没有将其放入书中的三个更高的系统。

互联网上的每个人都喜欢引用系统 1 和系统 2，主要是因为《思考，快与慢》是人们在 2016 年读过该书长达四页的摘要并从那时起就一直在谈论“懒惰控制器”这个词的人中引用最多的一本书。

系统 1 是快速、自动、直觉驱动的思维。当周四下午一份 42 页的商业协议到达你的收件箱时，你的大脑立即说：“我不会阅读所有这些内容，我可能应该付钱给一名真正的律师，而不是让聊天机器人扮演律师。”

系统2是深思熟虑的、分析性的、努力的、有意识的。当你忽略系统 1，自己打印 42 页的协议，拿起自动铅笔，写下“检查赔偿？”时，就会触发这种情况。并在页边空白处写上“比照意味着什么”90 分钟，然后离开办公桌，感觉就像约翰·马歇尔在主持马伯里诉麦迪逊案。

但止步于系统2是菜鸟级别的认知。如果你真的想诊断 2026 年人类思维会发生什么，你必须更深入：

系统 3 在公共场合执行系统 ​​2，因此陌生人知道您仍然有前额皮质。您不仅仅阅读了合同。你观察到自己从电影般的第三人称视角阅读合同，感觉到一滴高贵的泪水从你的脸颊滚落，并开始在脑海中思考第 7.2(b) 节周围的开头钩子。

系统 4 正在执行一项完全正常的周二下午任务（在签署之前阅读一份文件），并通过一位古希腊哲学家、三位认知心理学家、一段错误引用、十个重复的要点以及与太阳的最终比较来对其进行清洗，直到日常行政琐事听起来像是起草《大宪章》。

系统 5 正在阅读其他人的系统 4 帖子，并得出结论，唯一相称的道德反应是构建一个更长、更宏伟的系统 4 帖子，从而同时测试 X Premium 角色计数器的结构负载限制和每个人的耐心。

自公元前 370 年以来，技术一直在劫持努力的思维。坦率地说，从苏格拉底开始的时间线就是系统 1 的历史。

大约一百万年前：火劫持了生肉咀嚼作为胃肠道系统 2 的锻炼。早期原始人类不再需要连续四个小时不间断地咀嚼麋鹿软骨来获取 300 卡路里的热量。立即代谢卸载。从那里开始一切都走下坡路。

公元前 3200 年：苏美尔楔形文字劫持了你的姐夫欠你多少春收的山羊。在两代人的时间里，没有人能够在头脑中记住一只山羊。纯粹的认知萎缩。

公元 1440 年：古腾堡的印刷机劫持了一位中世纪僧侣在没有暖气的石质写字间眯着眼睛用牛油蜡烛手抄一份手稿长达 11 年的令人深感满足的艰苦劳动。有没有人停下来问一下印刷机对僧侣们的口味做了什么？

1784 年：双焦点眼镜劫持了眯眼作为一种视觉系统 2 的锻炼方式。

1822 年：约翰·艾萨克·霍金斯 (John Isaac Hawkins) 和桑普森·莫丹 (Sampson Mordan) 为第一支自动铅笔获得了第 4742 号英国专利，专利本身的明确设计目的是“无需频繁切割或修补笔尖或笔尖”。

停下来坐一会儿。

昨天你在与硅谷对抗时高举的 Excalibur 机械铅笔本身就是一台拥有 204 年历史的机器，其设计目的是为了减轻用刀片削雪松木和吹掉拇指上的石墨粉尘时产生的高贵、塑造性格的摩擦。你没有拒绝捷径。你刚刚选择了一条维多利亚时代的捷径，并称之为启蒙。

1959 年：施乐 914 复印机劫持了在复写纸上重新打印合同的行为。

1983 年：Microsoft Word 劫持了 Wite-Out，以及在 15 页租约的第 14 页上犯错的健康、令人肾上腺素飙升的恐惧。

计算器劫持了长除法。
GPS 被劫持，您与配偶就中控台上折叠的兰德·麦克纳利道路地图集争论，同时错过了萨凡纳的出口。
谷歌劫持了在酒吧坐了三个小时，向你的朋友坚称凯文·科斯特纳在空军一号，而实际上是哈里森·福特，这种经过艰苦斗争、纯粹的酒吧凳信念用来塑造真实的性格。

现在，公平地说，你对一件大事的看法是正确的。人工智能确实不同。

它不仅仅一次接管一项艰苦的工作。它立刻接管了所有的人。

记住。总结一下。研究中。计算。写作。解决问题。权衡利弊。决定。规划。为人们导航。反思。创造。听起来像是 2019 年的 Medium 帖子。在一篇 5,300 字的文章中十次用“&”代替“and”，没有人会出现空间不足的情况。在关于抵抗机器的宣言中讽刺地使用了动词“grok”。建立一个包含十项项目符号的列表，其中四个项目符号实际上是相同的项目符号，穿着不同的毛衣。

20万年来，我们的大脑一直习惯于轻松出行。当我们屈服于捷径时，无论是让法学硕士阅读我们的合同，还是让LinkedIn格式完成听起来深刻的繁重工作，我们都会付出高昂的代价。

让我们来分解一下实际成本。

成本1：总结感觉像是理解，编号框架感觉像是智慧。

你完全正确，阅读压缩摘要会欺骗你的大脑，让你相信你理解了一个你从未真正思考过的主题。被忽视的是镜像陷阱：将一段 12 个字的常识（“如果你不读合同，你不会知道里面有什么”）并将其夸大为关于旧石器时代大脑进化的 900 字讲座，欺骗作者和读者，让他们认为他们刚刚见证了认识论的突破。包装不是洞察力。单行段落没有深度。

像这样。

还有这个。

注意你的大脑现在想要慢慢点头，尽管自上一段以来我没有说过任何话。这就是系统 1 的换行符。

成本2：混乱的中间是成长的空间，这也是你发现在没有律师的情况下审查一份巨额合同是一种令人兴奋的购买诉讼的方式的地方。

罗伯特·比约克（Robert Bjork）在加州大学洛杉矶分校关于“理想困难”的研究确实是伟大的研究，里斯科和吉尔伯特关于认知卸载的研究也是真实的。努力的检索可以使学习坚持下去。没有人认真地反对这一点。有趣的是，我们表现得好像理想难度是一种濒临灭绝的物种，我们必须用“无人工智能块”人为制造，就好像现实生活还没有每个工作日提供九个小时非自愿的理想难度一样。尝试与顽固的贷方达成交易，在应收账款滑落时管理工资，或者阅读商业租赁第 14.3(c) 条，其中另一方悄悄地将个人担保埋在样板维护条款中。你不需要花 10 分钟提高效率来体验认知摩擦。只需在游戏中拥有真实的皮肤即可。

成本3：判断力的消失，表演性叹息的兴起。

您问当我们接近 AGI 和 ASI 时，什么才能保持人类的独特性，您给了我们四个支柱：

1. 意图
2. 问责制
3. 关系
4、判断

扎实的开始。令人尊敬的名单。不过有点短。如果我们诚实地对待超级智能时代人类独特性的最终前沿，那么至少还有六个特征是神经网络无法真正复制的：

5. 打印一份 30 页的 PDF，这样你就可以带着它在家里到处走，看起来既沉重又重要。
6. 在晚餐时告诉大家你“最近一直在进行模拟”。
7. 从京都的一家文具专卖店购买一支 65 美元的黄铜自动铅笔，这样你的页边笔记会有更好的口感。
8. 将正常的工作满意度称为“干净的多巴胺”，因为说“我对完成工作感觉很好”听起来不像休伯曼的插曲。
9. 假设因为你过去把你的思维外包给克劳德，所以西方文明的其他部分忘记了如何阅读文档。
10. 将“有品味”与“发布品味的重要性”混为一谈。

味道实际上是数千个压缩的 System 2 模式同时发射。你知道其中一种图案是什么样子的吗？在点击《邮报》之前，先回顾一下自己的草稿，然后思考：“等等，我真的只是将自己用铅笔阅读一份合同与为人类思想的生存而战进行比较吗？”

成本 4：维克多·弗兰克尔工业园区。

根据联邦法规，互联网上每一篇严肃的生产力文章都必须包含准确的引用：

“刺激和反应之间有一个空间。在这个空间里，我们有能力选择我们的反应。我们的反应就是我们的成长和自由。”

这是一种可爱的情感。只有一条细小的、美味的皱纹。

维克多·弗兰克尔从未写过它。

研究人员从头到尾检索了《人类的意义探寻》和弗兰克尔出版的其他作品。这些话不存在。史蒂芬·柯维 (Stephen Covey) 在夏威夷的一本大学图书馆的书中看到类似的段落后，就普及了这句话（学者们指出，心理学家罗洛·梅 (Rollo May) 1963 年撰写的有关刺激与反应之间暂停的文章是最接近的前兆），大约在 2000 年代中期，互联网将维克多·弗兰克尔 (Viktor Frankl) 的名字贴在上面，再也没有回头。

想想这纯粹的诗意。在你自己的要点之上几行命令人类“阅读完整的源代码，而不是摘要”，你在整个互联网上丢下了最著名的错误总结文化引用。

如果这不是一个关于认知卸载的案例研究，那就没什么了。

成本5：隐喻的过度膨胀。

曾几何时，合同就是合同，太阳是一个 46 亿年前的聚变氢等离子体球，距离地球 9300 万英里，它种植农作物，为水循环提供动力，如果你在后九洞不涂防晒霜，它还会给你一个坚韧的脖子。

现在，概率文本引擎会告诉您“这是一个非常尖锐、微妙的观点！”每次你拼写错误的问题都是“like the sun”。

如果人工智能是太阳，那么自动铅笔又是什么呢？遮阳伞？防晒指数 50？一副偏光太阳镜？一旦你开始将软件订阅与太空中的核聚变进行比较，当真正重要的事情发生时，你就会无处可去。

成本6：比例性的崩溃。

当每一个小小的个人认识（今天我仔细阅读一份文件，而不是浏览人工智能项目符号列表！）都必须被视为物种边缘的一场生存之战时，我们的集体尺度感就崩溃了。有时你没有对思想的死亡进行打击。有时你只是做了作业。

那么，我们如何在拥抱这项变革性技术的同时，收回我们的思考、我们的简洁和我们的尊严呢？

它归结为一个关键原则：重建一个正常的下午和为此写一篇 900 字的布道之间的空间。

如何重建该空间完全取决于您。选择你的毒药：

- 在一天中创建 30 到 60 分钟的无 AI 时段，然后立即进行 90 分钟的无发帖时段，这样您就不会因在网上吹嘘而抵消全部精神益处。
- 进行模拟并打印出重要的内容。然后打印一些根本不重要的东西，只是为了保持对打印机的主导地位。
- 扔掉自动铅笔。使用木制 2 号刀，然后用小刀在金属废纸篓上削尖，就像您祖父在艾森豪威尔政府期间所做的那样。
- 阅读完整的源代码，而不是摘要，从《Man's Search for Meaning》开始，这样你就可以亲眼看到其中实际上包含了哪些引言。
- 在审查一份巨额合同时，不要让克劳德表现得“就像你是我的律师一样”，而是尝试采用激进、古老的模拟工作流程，即聘请一名真正的律师。
- 手写你的初稿。退潮时在湿沙上写下你的第二稿，这样你就能学会不执着。
- 设定 10 分钟规则：在使用 AI 之前先解决一个问题 10 分钟。然后设定一个 20 分钟的规则：在打开 X 之前，克制住引用 Daniel Kahneman 的冲动。
- 大声说出来：向调酒师解释你最新的生产力认识，除非你关闭标签，否则他不能合法地离开他的收银台，并观察他的眼睛来判断它是否真的很深刻。
- 记住纸质高速公路地图并拒绝使用 GPS，即使您晚于晚餐 18 分钟并且您的妻子默默地盯着乘客窗外。前排座位上冰冷的沉默？这就是系统 2 的实时重建。
- 午餐时在鸡尾酒餐巾背面做自己的长除法，这样餐桌上的人就知道你仍然参与到认知游戏中。
- 在发表任何超过 500 字的文章之前，先用凿子将其雕刻在一块石灰石上，以测试人类是否真正需要它。
- 将“grok”替换为“理解”，将“&”替换为“and”，并将“干净的多巴胺”替换为“我对完成工作感觉很好”。
- 不间断地盯着窗外 15 分钟，零输入、零播客和零心理模型，直到您记住“控制刺激和反应之间的空间”过去被称为安静地坐着。
- 永远不要再总结任何事情。如果朋友问一部电影怎么样，请站起来并在完整的遮挡和灯光提示下背诵整个剧本。
- 将人工智能视为“编辑”，而不是“作家”。这样，当它为你重写每一个句子时，你仍然可以在温暖的语义毯下安然入睡。
- 在发表有关人类认知未来的任何内容之前，问自己最后一个问题：苏格拉底会打出这个，还是会提前二十分钟索要铁杉？

人工智能就像太阳。

事实上，如果我们在这里应用一点系统 2 的严格性，人工智能与太阳完全不同。太阳是一颗G型主序恒星，通过引力将八颗行星保持在轨道上，最终将膨胀成红巨星并蒸发地球。人工智能是一种非常快速的自动完成机器，连接到 GPU 仓库中，可以帮助人们将三句话电子邮件变成关于人类命运的主题演讲。

是的，它可能有助于治愈癌症。
是的，它可能会让每个孩子都有一位导师。
是的，它可能会迎来一个丰富的时代，显然，从刚刚发现纸和石墨的高管们撰写的无限丰富的 900 字论文开始。

它的力量强大得难以估量。这就是为什么我们必须不惜一切代价保护人类的最后边界：知道何时阅读合同，放下铅笔，关闭笔记本电脑，而不是在互联网上写下任何有关它的字。

不管怎样，我对你说实话：我一个字都没有写。

我将你的帖子粘贴到我的人工智能中，并告诉它起草一条极其冗长的引用推文，长度至少是你的两倍，因为今晚我有更好的事情要做，坦率地说，这似乎比思考更有趣。

我们必须与思想的死亡作斗争。

title_en:
@FutureJurvetson @elonmusk @kimmonismus Context:
"I've tried to train models to do video prediction for the better part of the last 20 years, and largely failing for the first 15. Until I realized you had to abandon generative models and use joint embedding predictive architectures (JEPA)" 

"Things started to work in the last few years with JEPA and world models. The main applications are in the physical world, robotics, and industrial process control. Things that Meta is not particularly interested in" 

But my project always had the support of Zuck, Boz, Schrep, and Chris Cox. 

It's true that, as Chief AI Scientist, I was at senior VP level but was an IC. Best job in the company! 

Also true that I never worked on LLMs. I was very supportive of LLM projects at FAIR (e.g. the project that became Llama), and played a role on convincing Mark to create an AI-first product division around Llama, and pushed to open source Llama-2. But I was never involved at the technical level.

full_text_en:
@FutureJurvetson @elonmusk @kimmonismus Context:
"I've tried to train models to do video prediction for the better part of the last 20 years, and largely failing for the first 15. Until I realized you had to abandon generative models and use joint embedding predictive architectures (JEPA)" 

"Things started to work in the last few years with JEPA and world models. The main applications are in the physical world, robotics, and industrial process control. Things that Meta is not particularly interested in" 

But my project always had the support of Zuck, Boz, Schrep, and Chris Cox. 

It's true that, as Chief AI Scientist, I was at senior VP level but was an IC. Best job in the company! 

Also true that I never worked on LLMs. I was very supportive of LLM projects at FAIR (e.g. the project that became Llama), and played a role on convincing Mark to create an AI-first product division around Llama, and pushed to open source Llama-2. But I was never involved at the technical level.
full_text_zh:
@FutureJurvetson @elonmusk @kimmonismus 背景：
“在过去 20 年的大部分时间里，我一直在尝试训练模型进行视频预测，但在前 15 年基本上失败了。直到我意识到必须放弃生成模型并使用联合嵌入预测架构 (JEPA)”

“过去几年，JEPA 和世界模型开始发挥作用。主要应用是物理世界、机器人和工业过程控制。Meta 对这些东西不是特别感兴趣”

但我的项目始终得到扎克、博兹、施雷普和克里斯·考克斯的支持。

确实，作为首席人工智能科学家，我虽然是高级副总裁级别，但却是一名 IC。公司最好的工作！

我从未攻读过法学硕士，这也是事实。我非常支持 FAIR 的 LLM 项目（例如后来成为 Llama 的项目），并在说服 Mark 围绕 Llama 创建人工智能优先产品部门方面发挥了作用，并推动开源 Llama-2。但我从来没有参与过技术层面的工作。

title_en:
Codex CLI 0.172.0 is out!

Highlights:
- Tab completes arguments for supported slash commands in the TUI (e.g., /mcp lo → /mcp login)
- Thread links from search results and transcripts open saved conversations and nested agents in the terminal
- Stdio MCP servers with cached tool lists now start on their first tool call by default
- Code Mode now uses gRPC for all host connections; code_mode_host_grpc is deprecated

Complete details in thread ↓

title: Less time tuning KV cache, more time serving models. vLLM v0.34's extensible KV cache is on by default, using GPU virtual memory to size the cache automatically. Thanks @RedHat_AI and @mgoin_ for the ~4-minute walkthrough!

title_zh: vLLM v0.34推自动KV缓存扩展功能
author: vLLM Project
author_role: 高通量、低内存显存极速推理架构
summary_en: Open-source inference engine vLLM has released version 0.34, featuring an extensible KV cache enabled by default. By utilizing GPU virtual memory, the system dynamically manages cache size based on load, reducing manual configuration overhead and improving throughput for high-concurrency model serving.

title: GPT-6.2 Astra is a step function on robotics:
title_en: GPT-6.2 Astra is a step function on robotics:
title_zh: GPT-6.2 Astra 是机器人技术的阶跃函数：
author: Greg Brockman
author_role: OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人
summary_zh:
OpenAI 的最新模型在 Artificial Analysis 的物理机器人基准测试中得分为 79 分，击败了其更便宜的同类产品 Claude Fable 5.2

OpenAI 的 GPT-6.2 Astra 在 AA-Robotics v0.1 上获得第一名，该基准测试语言模型是否可以操作真正的机器人手臂。 Astra 的平均得分为 79
article_content:
OpenAI's newest model scored 79 on Artificial Analysis's physical robotics benchmark, edging out its cheaper sibling and Claude Fable 5.2

OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra has claimed first place on AA-Robotics v0.1, a benchmark that tests whether language models can operate a real robot arm. Astra posted an average score of 79 out of 100, the highest in the evaluation.

It also did it with less fuss than anyone else. Astra used the fewest arm commands of any model tested, which suggests it is getting better at planning before it starts moving.

AA-Robotics v0.1 comes from Artificial Analysis, which launched the benchmark on October 14, 2026. It puts frontier language models in charge of a 6-axis Hiwonder NexArm robot arm.

The models do not control the arm by feel. They act as coding agents, writing instructions that the hardware then carries out.

The tasks include pouring drinks and stacking blocks. Both demand spatial awareness and problem-solving, two areas where text-trained models have historically been shaky.

Astra finished six of the eight tasks in the evaluation. Its 79 average put it just ahead of GPT-6.2 Sol, OpenAI’s more affordable variant, which scored 78. Claude Fable 5.2 came in at 75.

Astra issued 668 arm commands in total across its six completed tasks. On the box-cleanup task alone, it needed only 92 commands. That figure is approximately 75% fewer than Claude Fable 5.2 required.

We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime.

Every command sent to a physical arm is a chance for something to go wrong. Fewer commands generally means less trial and error, less wasted motion, and less wear on hardware.

The models still take about 30 minutes per task. A human handles comparable tasks in around 20 seconds.

Cost is another constraint. Running the models on these tasks costs between $2 and $16 per task, depending on the model and the job.

OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra on November 17, 2026. It shipped alongside GPT-6.2 Sol, positioned as the lower-cost option.

Astra’s API pricing is approximately 20% lower than its predecessor’s.

The robotics result lands about a month after Artificial Analysis introduced the benchmark. That timing means Astra arrived to a leaderboard that was still freshly painted, with Claude Fable 5.2 among the models already evaluated.

The tight finish between Astra and Sol also deserves attention. If the cheaper model lands within one point of the flagship on physical tasks, developers building robotics prototypes may reasonably ask whether the premium tier is worth it.

The gaps that remain are equally instructive. A 30-minute task time against a 20-second human baseline shows how far general-purpose models are from practical deployment. Per-task costs of $2 to $16 add another hurdle for any business doing the math on automation.

The label on the benchmark matters too. This is version 0.1.

Disclosure: This article was edited by Diego Almada Lopez. For more information on how we create and review content, see our Editorial Policy.

title: SBI's ₹1.6 crore offer for a Chief AI Officer is awesome but it also shows how broken PSU bank pay is for tech talent.
title_en:
SBI's ₹1.6 crore offer for a Chief AI Officer is awesome but it also shows how broken PSU bank pay is for tech talent.

Now, SBI is India's biggest bank. Its balance sheet crossed ₹66 lakh crore this year. Almost every Indian family has some link to it, a salary account, a home loan, a pension.

In October, SBI put out an ad for six AI and tech roles. There is one opening for "General Manager and Chief AI Officer".

The pay is up to ₹1.6 crore a year. SBI says it depends on experience, current pay and posting.

The other five roles pay well too. Three Deputy General Managers get up to ₹1.2 crore each. Two AI architects get up to ₹90 lakh each.

Now SBI's own chairman, CS Setty drew ₹63.87 lakh in FY25. So the AI chief can earn about 2.5 times the person who runs the bank.

Yet, private banks are a different world. 

HDFC Bank's CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan was paid ₹12.08 crore in FY25. PSU bank CEOs earn only about 5 to 7% of what private bank CEOs earn.

But SBI able to pay its AI chief more than its chairman, because the role is a contract job. It is a three year term, which SBI can extend by two more years.

Basically, it is the workaround. An AI leader at this level won't come at this budget. So SBI is working around it.

As per the ad, the person will set up control rooms for AI and data products with the business teams. They will track how live AI models perform and what risks they carry. 

They will also run a separate team whose job is to check models independently. They will also train staff to use these tools. The role also covers an enterprise AI platform for generative AI and AI agents.

They need at least 15 years in banking, financial services or IT. And at least 3 years in a senior leadership role in AI, analytics, model oversight or governance.

So a brilliant engineer who built great models alone, but never ran a team, can't apply for this.

Honestly, a three year term is very short for building an AI platform inside a bank this size. SBI should use the two year extension while they build a second line of leaders under the CAIO from day one.

Obviously, a chairman earning less than half of what a new hire under him can earn is not a healthy setup. 

The Finance Ministry should let PSU banks pay market rates for specialist roles through a clear policy, instead of a contract workaround every time.

And if you are a senior data or analytics person who wants a role like this in five years, it rewards people who have led teams, owned model risk and worked with business heads. 

Pure technical depth won't be enough.

full_text_zh:
SBI 为首席人工智能官提供的 1.6 亿卢比的报价很棒，但这也表明 PSU 银行对技术人才的薪酬是多么的破碎。

现在，SBI 是印度最大的银行。今年其资产负债表超过 660 亿卢比。几乎每个印度家庭都与它有某种联系，工资账户、住房贷款、养老金。

10 月，SBI 发布了一则招聘 6 个人工智能和技术职位的广告。有一个“总经理兼首席人工智能官”的职位空缺。

年薪高达 1600 万卢比。 SBI 表示，这取决于经验、当前薪酬和职位。

其他五个角色的报酬也不错。三名副总经理每人的薪酬最高可达 12 万卢比。两名人工智能架构师每人可获得高达 900 万卢比的奖金。

CS Setty 现任 SBI 董事长，2025 财年收入达 638.7 万卢比。因此，人工智能主管的收入大约是银行经营者的 2.5 倍。

然而，私人银行却是一个不同的世界。

HDFC 银行首席执行官 Sashidhar Jagdishan 在 2025 财年的薪酬为 1.208 亿卢比。 PSU 银行首席执行官的收入仅为私人银行首席执行官的 5% 至 7% 左右。

但 SBI 能够向 AI 主管支付比董事长更高的薪酬，因为该职位是合同制工作。任期三年，SBI 可以再延长两年。

基本上，这是解决方法。这个级别的人工智能领导者不会有这样的预算。因此，SBI 正在解决这个问题。

根据广告，此人将与业务团队一起建立人工智能和数据产品的控制室。他们将跟踪实时人工智能模型的表现以及它们带来的风险。

他们还将管理一个单独的团队，其工作是独立检查模型。他们还将培训员工使用这些工具。该角色还涵盖用于生成人工智能和人工智能代理的企业人工智能平台。

他们需要在银行、金融服务或 IT 行业工作至少 15 年。并在人工智能、分析、模型监督或治理领域担任高级领导职务至少 3 年。

因此，一位才华横溢的工程师独自构建了出色的模型，但从未管理过团队，因此无法申请此职位。

老实说，对于在这种规模的银行内部构建人工智能平台来说，三年的期限非常短。 SBI 应该利用两年的延期，从第一天起就在 CAIO 下建立第二线领导人。

显然，董事长的收入还不到他手下新员工收入的一半，这并不是一个健康的设置。

财政部应该通过明确的政策，让事业单位银行为专家角色支付市场利率，而不是每次都通过合同解决办法。

如果你是一名高级数据或分析人员，希望在五年内担任这样的职位，那么它会奖励那些领导团队、承担模型风险并与业务主管合作的人。

纯粹的技术深度是不够的。
